item.title: Lord of the Rings Stars to Reunite for Netflix's The Gentlemen

item.title: Tope Alabi threatens legal action over online defamation
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Popular Nigerian gospel singer Tope Alabi has threatened legal action against individuals who publish, share or circulate statements she considers false and defamatory about her on social media and other platforms. The warning was contained in a public notice issued by her lawyers, Oakmount Legal Practitioners, and shared on the singer’s Instagram page on Friday, October 23, 2026. In the notice, the legal team said the singer, whose full name is Evangelist Patricia Temitope Alabi, had instructed them to take steps to protect her reputation against publications capable of causing damage to her personal, professional and spiritual standing. According to the lawyers, Alabi has spent nearly three decades building a reputation based on integrity, honour and public trust. The notice stated: “Our Client has, for almost thirty (30) years, built a reputation of integrity, honour and public trust in her personal, professional and spiritual life.” The legal team expressed concern over what it described as false, misleading and harmful statements allegedly being circulated about the singer. The lawyers warned that anyone responsible for publishing such statements could face legal consequences, depending on the circumstances and applicable legal provisions. They also cautioned social media users against reposting or forwarding potentially defamatory content, stressing that responsibility may extend beyond the person who originally made the statement. The notice explained that liability could affect “the originator of the statement and to any person who repeats, republishes, reposts, shares, forwards or otherwise amplifies the same,” subject to the facts of each case and any applicable legal defences. The lawyers further warned that operating anonymous or pseudonymous social media accounts would not automatically shield individuals from legal liability. “The use of anonymous, pseudonymous or unverified accounts does not, of itself, confer immunity from legal liability,” the notice stated. As part of the warning, the lawyers directed individuals who had already published material considered defamatory to remove it immediately and refrain from further publication. They stated that deleting a post would not automatically eliminate possible liability for its earlier publication. The legal team also indicated that the singer could seek legal remedies, including damages, injunctions to prevent further publication, court-ordered retractions, public apologies and legal costs. The notice added that the lawyers had been authorised to institute legal proceedings against individuals whose actions gave rise to an actionable claim, without further notice. However, the legal warning clarified that it was not intended to prevent legitimate criticism, truthful statements or the lawful exercise of freedom of expression. item.content:encoded: By Wasiu Rokibat Popular Nigerian gospel singer Tope Alabi has threatened legal action against individuals who publish, share or circulate statements she considers false and defamatory about her on social media and other platforms. The warning was contained in a public notice issued by her lawyers, Oakmount Legal Practitioners, and shared on the singer’s Instagram page on Friday, October 23, 2026. In the notice, the legal team said the singer, whose full name is Evangelist Patricia Temitope Alabi, had instructed them to take steps to protect her reputation against publications capable of causing damage to her personal, professional and spiritual standing. According to the lawyers, Alabi has spent nearly three decades building a reputation based on integrity, honour and public trust. The notice stated: “Our Client has, for almost thirty (30) years, built a reputation of integrity, honour and public trust in her personal, professional and spiritual life.” The legal team expressed concern over what it described as false, misleading and harmful statements allegedly being circulated about the singer. The lawyers warned that anyone responsible for publishing such statements could face legal consequences, depending on the circumstances and applicable legal provisions. They also cautioned social media users against reposting or forwarding potentially defamatory content, stressing that responsibility may extend beyond the person who originally made the statement. The notice explained that liability could affect “the originator of the statement and to any person who repeats, republishes, reposts, shares, forwards or otherwise amplifies the same,” subject to the facts of each case and any applicable legal defences. The lawyers further warned that operating anonymous or pseudonymous social media accounts would not automatically shield individuals from legal liability. “The use of anonymous, pseudonymous or unverified accounts does not, of itself, confer immunity from legal liability,” the notice stated. As part of the warning, the lawyers directed individuals who had already published material considered defamatory to remove it immediately and refrain from further publication. They stated that deleting a post would not automatically eliminate possible liability for its earlier publication. The legal team also indicated that the singer could seek legal remedies, including damages, injunctions to prevent further publication, court-ordered retractions, public apologies and legal costs. The notice added that the lawyers had been authorised to institute legal proceedings against individuals whose actions gave rise to an actionable claim, without further notice. However, the legal warning clarified that it was not intended to prevent legitimate criticism, truthful statements or the lawful exercise of freedom of expression. The notice stated: “Nothing in this Notice is intended to restrict truthful statements, fair comment on matters of public interest, or the lawful exercise of the right to freedom of expression guaranteed by law.” The message serves as a warning to social media users to exercise caution when making or circulating claims about the singer. Although the legal notice outlined the potential consequences of defamatory publications, it did not identify specific individuals against whom legal proceedings had been initiated. The development highlights the growing concerns surrounding online defamation and the potential legal consequences of publishing or sharing harmful claims about public figures. Tope Alabi, widely known for her gospel music and contributions to Nigeria’s gospel music industry, remains a prominent figure among Christian music lovers. item.title: 2027: Wike debunks viral post backing Adamawa LP candidate, Abbo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has debunked a social media post claiming he is backing Senator Ishaku Abbo, the Labour Party LP candidate in next year’s Adamawa State governorship election. Wike, who spoke through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, described the report as fake. Olayinka said the minister has no relationship with the LP or any of its candidates in Adamawa State. The post in question quoted Wike as urging the people of Adamawa State to make informed and thoughtful decisions at the ballot, adding that, in his opinion, Abbo is best fit to lead the state. The minister, however, said he did not at any time endorse Abbo or any other LP candidate. He urged the people of Adamawa State to disregard the post, stressing that whoever he is supporting, he will say so with his own mouth. The post 2027: Wike debunks viral post backing Adamawa LP candidate, Abbo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
item.description: Meta is delaying the enforcement of its new business terms after publishers raised concerns that they could allow the company to scrape news sites for AI training, as reported earlier by Fast Company . In a statement to The Verge , Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says the terms will go into effect on November 20th "to allow more time for us to explain to our partners and stakeholders what's changing and what's not." The business terms , which were originally supposed to go into effect on October 30th, appeared to give Meta permission to freely scrape the new sites that use its platforms, while using the material for AI training. Though Meta u … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Melania Trump says secured ceasefire in Ukrainian city of Oleshky
item.description: US First Lady Melania Trump said in a surprise announcement Friday she had secured a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged city of Oleshky, where citizens are trapped and short of food. The localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky would begin on October 29, a statement issued by her office said. There was no immediate confirmation from Moscow or Kyiv. “The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster,” Melania, the wife of President Donald Trump, said in the statement. “It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.” The announcement comes a year after the Slovenian-born former model stunned the world by revealing she had established a back channel of communication with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Melania Trump has since secured the “reunifications” of 34 children separated from their parents by the war, her office said. In a number of cases they had been abducted by Russia. Her announcement also comes as President Trump has stepped up efforts to end Moscow’s war on Ukraine — largely by pivoting back towards Putin and away from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Melania Trump said she had worked with the Russian and Ukrainian leaderships on the Oleshky plan, and that civilian leaders from both countries would “work together” and visit the devastated city to assess aid needs. – Caught in the crossfire – “Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” she said. She added that she an “impartial American media organization” — which she did not identify — would “accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground throughout the process” to ensure residents’ wishes were respected. Oleshky, on the southern bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region, was seized by Russian troops in 2022. The population has dropped from about 24,000 before Russia invaded to around 2,000 today. Former residents of the city told AFP earlier this month that people there were caught in the crossfire between Russia and Ukraine and facing worsening shortages of food and medication. The 56-year-old First Lady carefully guards her image and is an infrequent presence at the White House, preferring to stay in New York where her son Barron is studying. But she has ramped up her public profile in recent months, launching a series of initiatives, including one to help older foster children and another to tackle online harassment. Last week Melania Trump unveiled a women’s health program in a press conference in the White House Rose Garden alongside her husband, who lavished praise on her. item.title: From theory to pitch: CBF, CONMEBOL and Pernambuco FA train academy staff
item.description: From theory to pitch: CBF, CONMEBOL and Pernambuco FA train academy staff The CBF, CONMEBOL Evolución and the Pernambuco Football Federation (FPF) brought a youth football training program to Recife. From October 20 to 22, 40 professionals from 27 different institutions attended the seminar, led by Wilton Santana and PC de Oliveira at Retrô’s training center. The three-day program combined theoretical classes and practical activities, covering topics such as the coach’s role in developing players, differences in training approaches and leadership in the development process, activity planning and the application of tactical principles. The first two days focused on theory, covering topics such as the coach’s role in developing players Credits: Rafael Vieira / FPF Participants came from a variety of backgrounds, including coaches, assistant coaches, coordinators, supervisors and club officials. The program also welcomed representatives from the state’s leading clubs, including Sport, Santa Cruz, Náutico, Retrô, Belo Jardim, Carpinense and Chã Grande On the first two days, participants attended classes in the morning and early afternoon, followed by on-field activities with players from Retrô’s Under-12/13 and Under-15/17 teams. On the final day, participants put their newly acquired knowledge into practice on the pitch during activities with Retrô’s youth teams Credits: Rafael Vieira / FPF On the final day, the format was reversed: participants themselves led drills with the Under-14 and Under-15 teams under the instructors’ supervision. This was followed by technical feedback and the presentation of certificates. For Pernambuco Football Federation president Evandro Carvalho, the initiative offers great prospects for the clubs’ future by enhancing professionals’ skills and strengthening youth development. “Investing in professional training means investing in the future of football. Closer ties between the FPF, the CBF and CONMEBOL help expand access to knowledge and working methods, ensuring our clubs are increasingly well equipped to develop young players. Pernambuco has an important role in this process, and hosting an initiative like this reinforces our commitment to the growth of football at every stage,” he told the FPF website. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: EU member states wrangle over all-important budget: Is a deal this year feasible?
item.description: A marathon EU summit on October 15-16 failed to produce a breakthrough on the European Union's next long-term budget. Although EU leaders put on a brave face at the end of the talks by saying that "the way forward is clearer", EU capitals appear deadlocked on what that path is. At stake is the EU's ability to finance its strategic priorities from 2028 to 2034. The main dividing line is between the so-called "frugal countries", who want deep cuts to the proposed budget, and the "friends of cohesion", who say that cuts are not the answer.

item.title: Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing set for golden opportunity they might not get again
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jordan Watkins #17 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball during an NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If the 49ers take the sensible, long-term approach, then they will not have Mike Evans available for their Week 7 matchup with the Atlanta Falcons after his Achilles issue flared up in their Monday Night Football win over the Washington Commanders. San Francisco is shorn of wide receiver depth due to a remarkable cluster of injuries at the position, and the 49er passing game was ineffective without Evans after he left the game against the Commanders. Evans has developed a superb rapport with Brock Purdy, serving as a devastatingly effective easy button for the San Francisco quarterback. The future Hall of Famer’s connection with Purdy is likely to be critical down the stretch and in the postseason as the 49ers aim to realize their Super Bowl aspirations and, as such, there is little reason for San Francisco to risk a serious injury to Evans by pushing him to play against the Falcons when they are 6-0 with a three-game lead in the NFC West. Though the 49ers look likely to be without Evans, they could get a boost with the return of Christian Kirk from the calf issue that has kept him out for the entire season to this point. But it is perhaps a tad ambitious to expert Kirk to hit the ground running right off the bat and, in Evans’ potential absence, the passing game will most likely predominantly go through tight end George Kittle. Yet the dearth of other options would also leave the Falcons game as a golden opportunity for Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing to impress and stake a claim for a larger amount of offensive snaps going forward. Both Cowing (2024) and Watkins (2025) came into the league as fourth-round picks with skill sets that suggested they could be dynamic options in the Kyle Shanahan offense. Yet their potential in that regard has remained largely untapped. Cowing and Watkins each displayed speed and route-running craft in college that figured to translate well to the NFL level. However, they have each seen injuries check their progress. After playing only a peripheral role in 2024, Cowing lost an entire season to injury in 2025, when a preseason high-ankle sprain curtailed the ascent Watkins was seemingly enjoying as a rookie. Heading into Week 7, Cowing and Watkins each have just five catches each in their respective careers. Cowing has only 89 yards to his name, while Watkins has 108, with the former seemingly on thin ice in his role as a return man having muffed a punt in the win over the Seattle Seahawks before making an ill-advised decision to return one from the four-yard line in the defeat of the Commanders. item.content:encoded: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jordan Watkins #17 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball during an NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If the 49ers take the sensible, long-term approach, then they will not have Mike Evans available for their Week 7 matchup with the Atlanta Falcons after his Achilles issue flared up in their Monday Night Football win over the Washington Commanders. San Francisco is shorn of wide receiver depth due to a remarkable cluster of injuries at the position, and the 49er passing game was ineffective without Evans after he left the game against the Commanders. Evans has developed a superb rapport with Brock Purdy, serving as a devastatingly effective easy button for the San Francisco quarterback. The future Hall of Famer’s connection with Purdy is likely to be critical down the stretch and in the postseason as the 49ers aim to realize their Super Bowl aspirations and, as such, there is little reason for San Francisco to risk a serious injury to Evans by pushing him to play against the Falcons when they are 6-0 with a three-game lead in the NFC West. Though the 49ers look likely to be without Evans, they could get a boost with the return of Christian Kirk from the calf issue that has kept him out for the entire season to this point. But it is perhaps a tad ambitious to expert Kirk to hit the ground running right off the bat and, in Evans’ potential absence, the passing game will most likely predominantly go through tight end George Kittle. Yet the dearth of other options would also leave the Falcons game as a golden opportunity for Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing to impress and stake a claim for a larger amount of offensive snaps going forward. Both Cowing (2024) and Watkins (2025) came into the league as fourth-round picks with skill sets that suggested they could be dynamic options in the Kyle Shanahan offense. Yet their potential in that regard has remained largely untapped. Cowing and Watkins each displayed speed and route-running craft in college that figured to translate well to the NFL level. However, they have each seen injuries check their progress. After playing only a peripheral role in 2024, Cowing lost an entire season to injury in 2025, when a preseason high-ankle sprain curtailed the ascent Watkins was seemingly enjoying as a rookie. Heading into Week 7, Cowing and Watkins each have just five catches each in their respective careers. Cowing has only 89 yards to his name, while Watkins has 108, with the former seemingly on thin ice in his role as a return man having muffed a punt in the win over the Seattle Seahawks before making an ill-advised decision to return one from the four-yard line in the defeat of the Commanders. After Evans again missed practice on Thursday, it seems highly likely Watkins and Cowing will have prominent roles to play regardless of Kirk’s involvement. Even with Christian Kirk probably returning on Sunday, Watkins should have a decent role to play. Nice work here recovering from the stumble on the incidental contact, working back to the ball and then managing to get upfield for YAC. pic.twitter.com/JqseP6Piwo — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 22, 2026 It is an opportunity neither can afford to waste, as they may not get another this season. While Evans’ Achilles issue will need to be managed throughout the year, he will be expected to return in Week 9 if he does indeed miss the Falcons game. Deebo Samuel is also expected back after the bye, though rookie De’Zhaun Stribling will have to wait a little longer to make his return from the ankle injury suffered in the season opener. In other words, they will each be down the pecking order again soon. From Watkins at least, there have been some encouraging flashes of promise this season, the former Ole Miss wideout making catches of 34 and 26 yards in the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals and doing an excellent job overcoming physical coverage to make a 22-yard reception against the Commanders. Nothing spectacular here, but Jordan Watkins has played 45% of the offensive snaps this season. Injuries aside, some of that will be tied to the fact that he's shown buy-in as a run-blocker, including on the weird inadvertent Kaelon Black direct snap play. pic.twitter.com/LSeeyvhr5y — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 22, 2026 Watkins has also displayed admirable commitment as a run blocker this season, with his effort in that area of the game likely a reason why he has been trusted to play 45 percent of the offensive snaps so far in 2026. Asked why Watkins hasn’t had more targets, quarterback Brock Purdy replied on Thursday: “Honestly, it has nothing to do with not trying to get him the ball or anything. I think that’s just sort of how the game’s gone. He’s definitely a playmaker. He’s done that since he’s got here. And it’s just been tough with him getting opportunities when we have like [WR] Mike Evans, [WR] Demarcus Robinson, [TE] George [Kittle], [RB] Christian [McCaffrey], like other guys too and he’s trying to get in that mix. But, he’s been consistent. He’s been a guy that has stayed faithful to this whole process. And now he’s getting a shot and opportunity. So, I feel like we will over time. Hopefully this game too, I can get him the ball. Watching the film, that’s definitely a guy that I’m like, ‘Yeah, I’d love to get the ball to him.’ He’s shown flashes and glimpses of not even just catching the ball, but making plays after the catch too or getting YAC after the catch. So, I feel you on that and that’s something that I watch and I want to have our connection get better and better, but has nothing to do with not trying to give him the ball or anything like that.” Of the two, Watkins seems the more likely to have success in carving out a long-term role in the offense. Cowing was put the behind the 8-ball by his lost 2025 and has not caught up, with his stock at a low ebb amid his questionable performance as a returner. But if either is going to have a compelling case for being involved in the offense once the likes of Evans and Samuel return, then they need to make the most of the chance that looks set to come their way on Sunday. There is concern about how the 49er passing game will look without Evans in Atlanta. If either Cowing or Watkins can ensure it still succeeds, then it would serve as a great boost to their long-term prospects and the depth of the 49er receiving corps.

item.title: The 2026-27 Marquette Women’s Basketball Season Preview: The Transfers
item.description: Look, it’s Kayl Petersen defending Noelle Anthon in the same picture, how helpful. | Credit: Marquette University It’s time to continue our 2026-27 season preview for Marquette women’s basketball! We’re moving forward with our look at head coach Cara Consuegra’s roster for this year. We’ve already rummaged around in what to expect from Halle Vice , and peeked under the hood at who else is returning from last year’s roster . Go give those a click to get caught up on things if you haven’t already, and heck, wander around in our entire season preview package if you haven’t done that, too. Today we’re looking at the five transfers on the Marquette roster right now. There’s four that have made their way to Milwaukee from a Division 1 team and one from the junior college ranks. We’ll go through them in order of Division 1 experience, although that’s obviously not going to be sorted by post-high school experience, if that makes sense. Anyway, off we go, starting off with the player on the roster who already has some experience playing in the Big East….. MacKenzie Givens Junior — #12 — Guard — 6’0” — Cincinnati, Ohio MacKenzie Givens comes to Marquette after two seasons at Xavier. item.content:encoded: Look, it’s Kayl Petersen defending Noelle Anthon in the same picture, how helpful. | Credit: Marquette University It’s time to continue our 2026-27 season preview for Marquette women’s basketball! We’re moving forward with our look at head coach Cara Consuegra’s roster for this year. We’ve already rummaged around in what to expect from Halle Vice , and peeked under the hood at who else is returning from last year’s roster . Go give those a click to get caught up on things if you haven’t already, and heck, wander around in our entire season preview package if you haven’t done that, too. Today we’re looking at the five transfers on the Marquette roster right now. There’s four that have made their way to Milwaukee from a Division 1 team and one from the junior college ranks. We’ll go through them in order of Division 1 experience, although that’s obviously not going to be sorted by post-high school experience, if that makes sense. Anyway, off we go, starting off with the player on the roster who already has some experience playing in the Big East….. MacKenzie Givens Junior — #12 — Guard — 6’0” — Cincinnati, Ohio MacKenzie Givens comes to Marquette after two seasons at Xavier. This is literally leaving a hometown team for her, so that seems like kind of a big deal. She played just 139 total minutes as a freshman for the Musketeers as they went 7-24 under the direction of Billi Chambers, but Givens was a most-of-the-time starter for Xavier this past season. She got the nod in 24 of her 29 appearances, missing a road trip to Providence in early February. She was coming off the bench to start the season but then was in the first five the rest of the way after that. Givens was Xavier’s #2 scorer at 11.7 points per game, and she chipped in 4.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals as well. BartTorvik.com has Givens as the most productive player on Xavier’s roster last season, rating the best both in terms of how efficient she was in her usage and points above average. She was also the only Musketeer with an offensive rating north of 90, and she was waaaaay up there at 106.6. Her Hoop Stats has her in the top 500 in the country in offensive rating and top 400 in turnover rate. In other words: If you were going to swipe one person off a roster that went 11-19 overall and 4-16 in the Big East, you could do a lot worse than Givens. In terms of immediate obvious fit for Marquette, at worst Givens is a reliable backcourt option. I wouldn’t be shocked to see her start on opening night at either the 2 or the 3, depending on how head coach Cara Consuegra considers the talents of Jordan Meulemans relative to the positions on the floor. If Givens can keep developing her three-point shot — she hit less than 32% last season — that will pay dividends for the Golden Eagles. With Halle Vice being the only player that has an obvious set role, the sky’s the limit for what Givens could contribute. The only question we have to ask is: If she was capable of a lot more, why didn’t we see it at Xavier? Or is that just a Musketeers bad/Billi Chambers bad problem? Kayl Petersen Junior — #34 — Forward — 6’1” — Waupun, Wisconsin Finally, this November, we will get to see Kayl Petersen debut in a Marquette uniform. She was originally set to join the Golden Eagles in the fall of 2024, but the coaching change led her to follow Megan Duffy to Virginia Tech. That worked out decently well for Petersen in Year 1, averaging just under 16 minutes a game mostly off the bench and adding 4.2 points and 2.9 rebounds as the Hokies went 19-13, but missed the NCAA tournament. Year #2, not so hot for Petersen, as she played in all but one game, but her minutes fell to just under 11 per game. She was a little less productive in general as a result, perhaps as a result of not quite getting in rhythm in her reduced role. VaTech went 23-10 last year and got to the NCAA tournament, so it’s hard to judge Duffy’s roster management here…. but you can see why Petersen perhaps went looking for an option with a little bit more playing time available to her. At 6’1”, perhaps Petersen doesn’t immediately showcase as an obvious productive force inside, but the fact of the matter is that she has a career rebounding rate of 8.8 per 40 minutes, and she was north of 10 per 40 minutes this past season. Her Hoop Stats ranks her top 500 in the country on the glass on both ends of the floor, and she was just barely outside the top 250 in the country in defensive win shares per 40 minutes last season. If all she does is body people inside and clean the glass, that’s okay by me. If she’s going to pull in nearly four offensive rebounds per 40 minutes of action like she did last year, Petersen’s going to have to do better than shooting 43% on two-pointers, though. Yu Han Lin Sophomore — #11 — Guard — 5’9” — Hualien, Taiwan The thing we have to unlock about Yu Han Lin when it comes to figuring out what she can bring to Marquette this season is answering the question as to why she started in seven of Middle Tennessee’s first 11 games, then not at all the rest of the season. Then as a secondary question, we have to figure out why Lin played at least 14 minutes in all seven games that she started and averaged over 23 minutes in those games … but then just over 11 minutes in her 26 games off the bench. That includes 14 games where she played single digit minutes, and 10 games where she played less than five minutes. That includes single digit outings in each of MTSU’s last six games of the year. I think all of that explains why she’s not at Middle Tennessee any more, it’s just not particularly encouraging for what it means for her ability to play at Marquette in the Big East. Middle Tennessee went 17-16 last season with an 11-7 record in Conference USA. Head coach Rick Insell is far from a goof, last year broke a run of four straight 26+ win seasons, and he’s gotten to at least 20 wins in 18 of his seasons with the Blue Raiders dating back to 2005-06. He’s been to the NCAA tournament 12 times with MTSU, but there’s something about Lin that said “okay, gotta play her” and then something that said “oh, no, can’t play her at all” even while the season wasn’t bending towards a more typical season for him. As a starter, Yu Han Lin averaged 9.0 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game last season. She was great inside the arc, shooting 58% on twos, but she shot 1-for-16 from behind the three-point line. Off the bench, she averaged just 3.5 points plus an assist and a rebound per game. She was suddenly not good inside the arc at just 40%, but suddenly she found a shooting touch, going 9-for-25, which is 36% which is absolutely fine by me. From a deeper analytical level, she had a tremendous assist rate according to Her Hoop Stats , ranking #314 in the country. That’s great, especially as Marquette clearly needs a point guard. However, her nearly 28% turnover rate was somewhere in the bottom third of the entire country, maybe worse since not every player on every team would have had the minutes to qualify for the rankings. Is that why Lin couldn’t play regularly for the Blue Raiders? Her 34 turnovers in her first 11 games with Middle Tennessee? And if that is the problem, what’s going to change about how she plays when she goes from Conference USA to the Big East to stop that problem from reoccurring… or even getting worse? Brooklyn Hall Redshirt Freshman — #1 — Guard — 6’1” — Dayton, Ohio Brooklyn Hall gets to be Not Last in this list because she spent half a season on a Division 1 roster last year. She was a spring semester enrollee at South Florida last January, but then she hit the transfer portal since USF elected to not keep on their interim head coach after Jose Fernandez left to coach the Dallas Wings in the WNBA. One Marquette hire of Sheila Boykin as an assistant coach later, and Hall is a Golden Eagle now instead of a Bull. Here’s how USF described Hall when she signed with them last November: Hall is the No. 2 Forward

item.title: 2027: Tinubu’s aide claims CityBoy Movement has support across party lines
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Digital/New Media, O’tega Ogra, has claimed that the CityBoy Movement has been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths and has attracted members across party lines, including from opposition parties, ahead of the 2027 general election. Ogra, who is also Deputy Director-General of the CityBoy Movement, a group campaigning in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, made the claim on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday while responding to questions about the movement’s reach and acceptance among young Nigerians. When asked about areas where the movement had yet to gain acceptance, Ogra said he was open to discussing any such areas but maintained that the movement had received support from a majority of Nigerian youths. “I mean, if you show me one, I might be able to speak to that. But as far as I know, we have been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths,” he said. Ogra also claimed that the movement had members across the political divide, including people associated with major opposition parties. “We’re a movement that has members across the political space. We have members from the PDP. We have members from Alhaji Atiku’s own party. We have members that have come from Peter Obi’s own party. We have members who belong to Seyi Makinde’s government within our structure,” he said. Explaining what he believed was driving the movement’s appeal among young Nigerians, Ogra said youths were tired of political leaders who, in his view, made promises they failed to keep and diverted public funds for private interests. “Because at the end of the day, the Nigerian youths, we are done with people telling us lies. We are done with people promising one thing and putting government funds into their private enterprise,” he said. He further argued that young Nigerians were better equipped to scrutinise political leaders because of their access to information and fact-checking tools. “We’re done with people, you know, trying to play on our intelligence. We are smarter than whatever was in the 1990s or in the 2000s. We have access to news, we have access to information, we can fact check, we can revalidate, we have these things at our fingertips and one thing that we have chosen to do at the City Boy movement, our motto is inform, engage, empower,” Ogra added. The post 2027: Tinubu’s aide claims CityBoy Movement has support across party lines appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Purdue Baseball invites fans to annual Halloween bash
item.description: Purdue Baseball is bringing costumes and trick-or-treating onto the field for its annual Halloween Bash at Alexander Field on Oct. 28. The free, all-ages event begins at 6 p.m., according to a community announcement. Players will dress up for a brief costume scrimmage before children take the field to trick-or-treat with players and coaches. Azzip Pizza is returning as the event's official sponsor for the second year. Fans are also encouraged to attend in costume. The event date could change if the forecast indicates another evening would offer more favorable weather. Fans can get a free Purdue Baseball ticket Everyone attending the Halloween Bash will receive a voucher redeemable for one free ticket to any regular-season Purdue Baseball home game during the 2027 season. Purdue has six home weekends plus several midweek dates scheduled at Alexander Field after winning 20 home games last season for the second time in team history. The Halloween Bash debuted at Alexander Field in 2019 and returned to the calendar in 2021. It has continued as an October event since then. More Purdue Baseball events are planned Purdue is also planning its First Pitch Dinner at the Ross-Ade Pavilion and its all-ages Preseason Fan Fest inside the Mollenkopf Athletic Center. Both events are held early in the spring semester. The Preseason Fan Fest generally takes place the weekend before college baseball’s national opening day, which is Feb. 19 this school year. item.title: The Sigma FP2 brings significant upgrades to the ‘world’s smallest’ full-frame camera
item.description: Seven years after Sigma claimed its original fp was the world's smallest and lightest full-frame mirrorless camera, the company has announced a similarly compact follow-up with several welcome upgrades including an improved sensor, an articulating LCD display, and longer battery life. But this time around Sigma is only claiming its new FP2 is the "world's smallest" full-frame shooter as those upgrades have increased its body-only weight by about six grams. The Sigma FP2 will be available on November 11th and starts at $2,199 for the camera body alone. item.title: Personalised cancer vaccine expected to be approved next year
item.description: A scanning electron micrograph of a melanoma cell Science Photo Library/Alamy A personalised mRNA vaccine for melanoma, the deadliest form of skin cancer , is expected to be approved for use in the US, Europe and the UK next year. The vaccine is designed to stimulate immune responses against genetic mutations that are unique to an individual’s cancer. When used alongside standard treatment in a late-stage trial, it substantially cut the risk of cancer recurrence or death within the next two years. “I think approval could be quick, and next year sounds reasonable,” says Alan Melcher at the Institute of Cancer Research in London, who wasn’t involved in the trial. Read more Rare cancer spread between twins in utero “It is a huge deal,” says Rebecca Lee at the University of Manchester, who also wasn’t involved. Thousands of people in the UK alone could benefit from this, based on the trial’s patient population, she says. “It’s highly likely the US and Europe [including the UK] will approve it next year”. However, producing the vaccine is very expensive, and it may not be deemed cost-effective for use on the UK’s National Health Services (NHS), she says. Advertisement In August, drugmaker Modern announced that the vaccine had positive results in a late-stage trial . More specific findings have now been released. The trial recruited more than 1100 adults who had surgery to remove high-risk melanomas that were likely to recur or spread to distant sites. In the UK, 19,400 melanoma cases are diagnosed annually, of which about 25 per cent are deemed high risk. Two-thirds of the participants were randomly assigned to receive a bespoke vaccine on top of standard immunotherapy, called pembrolizumab, which helps the immune system find and destroy cancer. Both were delivered every 3 weeks for up to a year. The remaining participants received placebo injections plus pembrolizumab. The vaccine is made by genetically sequencing a small sample of a person’s cancer and comparing that sequence with the DNA in the individual’s healthy blood cells. This enables researchers to pinpoint mutations specific to the cancer. item.dc:creator: Carissa Wong
item.content:encoded: A scanning electron micrograph of a melanoma cell Science Photo Library/Alamy A personalised mRNA vaccine for melanoma, the deadliest form of skin cancer , is expected to be approved for use in the US, Europe and the UK next year. The vaccine is designed to stimulate immune responses against genetic mutations that are unique to an individual’s cancer. When used alongside standard treatment in a late-stage trial, it substantially cut the risk of cancer recurrence or death within the next two years. “I think approval could be quick, and next year sounds reasonable,” says Alan Melcher at the Institute of Cancer Research in London, who wasn’t involved in the trial. Read more Rare cancer spread between twins in utero “It is a huge deal,” says Rebecca Lee at the University of Manchester, who also wasn’t involved. Thousands of people in the UK alone could benefit from this, based on the trial’s patient population, she says. “It’s highly likely the US and Europe [including the UK] will approve it next year”. However, producing the vaccine is very expensive, and it may not be deemed cost-effective for use on the UK’s National Health Services (NHS), she says. Advertisement In August, drugmaker Modern announced that the vaccine had positive results in a late-stage trial . More specific findings have now been released. The trial recruited more than 1100 adults who had surgery to remove high-risk melanomas that were likely to recur or spread to distant sites. In the UK, 19,400 melanoma cases are diagnosed annually, of which about 25 per cent are deemed high risk. Two-thirds of the participants were randomly assigned to receive a bespoke vaccine on top of standard immunotherapy, called pembrolizumab, which helps the immune system find and destroy cancer. Both were delivered every 3 weeks for up to a year. The remaining participants received placebo injections plus pembrolizumab. The vaccine is made by genetically sequencing a small sample of a person’s cancer and comparing that sequence with the DNA in the individual’s healthy blood cells. This enables researchers to pinpoint mutations specific to the cancer. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter Based on the same technology used in covid-19 vaccines, the cancer vaccine contains mRNA molecules that encode for proteins with up to 34 of those mutations. “The jab contains a fingerprint of proteins specifically associated with the cancer,” says Lee. “This helps [immune] T cells recognise the cancer better, and then pembrolizumab prevents those T cells from becoming exhausted once they’ve started attacking the cancer cells.” About two years after the start of treatment, 82 per cent of the participants who received the vaccine plus pembrolizumab were alive without their cancer recurring, on average, compared with 70 per cent among those on pembrolizumab alone. “It’s a really exciting result,” says Lee. Side effects were similar between the two groups. The results combine cancer recurrence and death rates into one figure, but since a treated cancer has to recur for it to cause death, this combined measure should be interpreted mostly as a sign of the vaccine reducing recurrence, says Melcher. The participants haven’t been tracked for long enough to robustly determine whether the vaccine improves survival rates. These results should be available within a few years, says Lee. A revolutionary way of targeting tumours could beat even the worst cancers We have long treated cancer based on its location in the body. But a whole new approach that analyses tumours differently is now helping people survive forms of cancer that were once considered a death sentence But because the vaccine has to be tailored to and manufactured for each individual, it is expected to be very costly, which could affect NHS access. “If it was a cheap drug, I’d definitely say it will get approved [for NHS use], but it’s going to be expensive,” says Lee. In January, a report by Reuters suggested it would cost around $200,000 per treatment. Merck and Moderna did not respond to a request about its cost. Further research is needed to better understand who is mostly likely to benefit from the vaccine, says Melcher. Some people may have mutations included in their vaccine that fail to stimulate anti-cancer immunity as predicted, or pembrolizumab could work so well that the vaccine can’t lead to further improvement. “If we can find immune markers in the blood or tumour that predict patient responses, we could use those to determine who to give the jab to,” says Melcher. James Larkin , also at the Institute of Cancer Research, says personalised vaccines could also work for other types of cancer, such as those affecting the lungs, bladder and kidneys, which are also routinely treated with immunotherapy. Further research is needed to verify this and explore whether the vaccines could work as standalone treatments.

item.title: North Shore gets a surprise visit from Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud
item.description: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud runs onto the field as he is introduced before an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) C.J. Stroud brought a little more star power to North Shore's preparations for one of its biggest games of the season . The Texans' quarterback visited the No. 2 state-ranked Mustangs as part of a Jordan Brand event ahead of Friday's matchup against No. 7 C.E. King at Galena Park ISD Stadium. A video shared by VYPE Houston on Wednesday morning captured a celebration that included custom apparel, music and Houston rapper Bun B's famous Trill Burgers. Stroud's entrance fit the occasion. The video shows a red slab rolling up to a gathering at the Mustangs' home stadium, with Stroud greeting the crowd as people surround the car and raise their phones to capture the moment. The festivities extended beyond the football team. Children and adults mingled outside, fans posed with North Shore apparel, and the school's Mustang mascot made an appearance. Inside the locker room, players showed off black clothing featuring North Shore's red-and-white logo. Other scenes highlighted a Nike-branded setup with the phrase "Proof is in the pressure" with shirts bearing the same message. VYPE's post identified Jordan Brand as the organizer of the visit. Stroud has his own connection to the Jumpman. He agreed to a multiyear endorsement deal with Jordan Brand in September 2024. Stroud's appearance added to the buildup for a game featuring two programs that played for state championships last season. North Shore (7-0, 4-0), the defending Class 6A Division I champion, faces a C.E. King (6-1, 4-0) team that finished as the Division II runner-up. The winner will take sole possession of first place in District 17-6A. North Shore leads the series 10-0 since 2016 and rolled to a decisive 42-27 victory last year on the road. item.title: Poulter leaves LIV as exodus of big names continues
item.description: Ian Poulter was co-captain of the Majesticks team alongside Lee Westwood [Getty Images] Ryder Cup legend Ian Poulter has become the latest star name to confirm he is quitting LIV Golf - leaving the breakaway tour's future looking increasingly uncertain. The 50-year-old Englishman was among a plethora of stars lured by LIV when the Saudi Arabia-backed project was launched in 2022 and was a staunch defender of the circuit when it was criticised. But Poulter has followed the likes of Jon Rahm, Louis Oosthuizen and Sergio Garcia in announcing his departure. He has said he wants to help his two sons, Luke and Joshua, pursue professional careers, as well as develop his YouTube channel. Saudi's Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing from LIV in April - having pumped in more than $5bn (£3.8bn) of investment - leading to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in the United States last month. It has secured a possible $300m (£224m) in financing from BC Partners Credit to try and move forward with 'LIV 2.0', but only a handful of players have so far committed to the proposed competition in 2027. "I wanted everyone to hear it direct from me that I have decided to not move forward with being part of LIV 2.0," Poulter wrote on his social media channels. "Needless to say, it was a tough decision and one I thought about and discussed at length with my family and team. "Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career." Former Open champion Oosthuizen quits LIV Golf Rahm sacrifices £75m to secure exit from LIV Golf LIV Golf secures potential $300m investment Former world number five Poulter was co-captain of the Majesticks team alongside fellow Englishman and Ryder Cup icon Lee Westwood. Westwood's future plans remain unclear. Poulter's decision to leave comes in the same week as 2010 Open champion Oosthuizen, who captained the Southern Guards GC team and said quitting was the "hardest decision" of his career. Last week, two-time major winner Rahm gave up a reported £75m owed to him by LIV after reaching a separation agreement. Garcia, Thomas Pieters, Abraham Ancer, David Puig and Adrian Meronk have also announced their departures. LIV's future could hinge on whether it can secure the signature of American superstar Bryson DeChambeau, who ESPN reported earlier this week "remains committed" to the league. In his statement, Poulter acknowledged LIV has "clearly divided opinion", but said he will be "forever proud" to be part of its founding group. "Change is never easy and it's fair to say professional golf has experienced plenty of it over the last few years," he added. item.title: Several OKC Thunder players react to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ending 20-point streak
item.description: All good things come to an end. At least Shai Gilgeous-Alexander did that on his own terms. With a chance to extend his historic 20-point streak with just one outside jumper in the final minute, the two-time MVP winner elected to call it a night. The Oklahoma City Thunder scrapped by with an ugly 96-84 win over the Denver Nuggets . Gilgeous-Alexander mustered up 17 points on 6-of-19 shooting. And for the first time since Nov. 2024, he fell short of eclipsing 20-plus points in a regular-season matchup. When Gilgeous-Alexander only had two points at halftime, his legendary streak was in jeopardy. The outside shot didn't fall as he was just 3-of-11. But he had a chance at the end to keep it going. That was initially the plan. Until he saw the Nuggets wave the white flag with 1:43 left in the fourth quarter. Now, Gilgeous-Alexander's streak ends at an NBA-record 141 consecutive games. He surpassed Wilt Chamberlain's record late in the 2025-26 regular season. Now, he sits atop the record book as the most consistent high-volume scorer in league history. Here's what the Thunder said about the record and his decision to end it: Mark Daigneault "I just have to note, he asked out of the game at the end of the game. He's got a historic streak going. Which is a remarkable streak, obviously. I just think that for the class that it shows and the perspective that it shows for him to say, 'Hey, I'm out now. The game's calling for me to be subbed out of the game.' That was his substitution. Of all the things that I admire about him, that's towards the top of the list in terms of moments that I appreciate about him. It shows tremendous class as a competitor." Shai Gilgeous-Alexander "I was gonna go out in there and then I saw that they had sub, so I was just like, 'We should sub, too.' I feel like you always treat the game with respect. God willing, I have many more games to start on a streak. So it's not the end of the world." Chet Holmgren "I mean, I asked him. I said, 'You want to shoot some threes right here?' And he's like, 'Nah.' And then he went up to Mark and subbed himself out. So he's a better man than me. Obviously, shooting some pull-up threes. But I think it was a selfless moment. He's a selfless guy. He's one of the hardest workers that I know. Shows up out there and so does his leadership. He does that in a great way." "I don't think people understand how challenging it is. Not only to be talented enough to do it, but also, he's never sprained an ankle and missed the rest of a game early on. He's never gotten ejected early on. Just the physical and mental endurance that it takes to do something like that is extremely impressive. It's not surprising. If anybody's able to do it, it's him." Jalen Williams "He's a smart man. item.title: Chase Elliott Removes Name From Most Popular Driver Ballot In Honor of Kyle Busch
item.description: On Friday, Chase Elliott showcased why he has become NASCAR’s most popular driver over the last eight seasons. The driver of the No. 9 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet has officially chosen to opt out of a chance to be crowned the most popular driver in the NASCAR Cup Series this season. The reason? To give Kyle Busch, who passed away in May, a clearer path to securing the award posthumously. Busch, who is featured on the ballot, has never taken home the NASCAR Most Popular Driver Award. If this gesture by Elliott feels eerily familiar, it’s because his father, Bill Elliott, also removed his name from the ballot in 2001, which paved the way for Dale Earnhardt, a seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion who was killed in a final lap crash of the Daytona 500 that season, to win the award for the only time in his Hall of Fame career. Bill Elliott won the NMPA Most Popular Driver Award a record 16 times. With Chase Elliott removing his name from the ballot, this means for the first time since Darrell Waltrip took home the award in 1990, there will be a driver not named Earnhardt or Elliott taking home the Most Popular Driver Award in the NASCAR Cup Series. Prior to the Coca-Cola 600 race weekend, Busch fell ill with a bout of sepsis and suddenly passed away at the age of 41. Busch, a two-time NASCAR Cup Series champion, was the winningest driver in the history of the NASCAR National Series, as he had racked up 234 victories between NASCAR’s three National Series divisions. Busch’s final NASCAR National Series win came at Dover Motor Speedway, a week prior to his unexpected death. Fans looking to vote for the 2026 Most Popular Driver are encouraged to visit the Most Popular Driver landing page . Fans can vote for one driver per ballot submission with voting being limited to five submissions per day, per email at NASCAR.com/mostpopulardriver or on the NASCAR Mobile App. The five votes per day aren’t limited to a single driver. The post Chase Elliott Removes Name From Most Popular Driver Ballot In Honor of Kyle Busch appeared first on TobyChristie.com .

item.title: Mainz 05 vs Werder Bremen Preview: Battle of the strikers
item.description: Mainz 05 vs Werder Bremen Preview: Battle of the strikers Mainz Mainz have started very strongly into the season and sit in fifth place after an away win against Schalke but they are yet to convince at home. Their start to the season has been hugely helped by one player - Phillip Tietz. The German striker has five goals from the first six league games and has scored in all but two this campaign. By contrast, Tietz now already has one less goal than he managed in the entire 2025-26 Bundesliga campaign on matchday seven. Mainz have the upper hand defensively against Saturday's opponent too as they have managed three clean sheets this campaign already. In spite of this, Werder Bremen will be comforted by the fact that when Mainz do concede the goals start pouring in. In the games during this campaign where Mainz has conceded, all their opponents have managed to score at least three goals against them in the Bundesliga. Mainz have only won once in their last five games against Werder Bremen with their last home win coming back in 2020. Mainz's secondary striker Sheraldo Becker has been the second fastest player this season in the Bundesliga with a top speed of 36.6 km/h. Ahead of the tie, Mainz coach Urs Fischer said: “The entire Bremen side makes a very strong impression. On three occasions they have been 2-0 down and they have come back.” Team news Dominik Kohr is out with an ankle injury alongside Otto Ruoppi and Silas who are also injured. Robin Zentner continues to be out with a hand issue and will be replaced by Alexander Schwolow. Werder Bremen With their third consecutive game coming from two goals down to grab a result, Werder Bremen drew 2-2 with Paderborn after being 2-0 down securing their status as the comeback kings. Helping out in this run has been the return to form of striker Niclas Füllkrug who is the Bundesliga's top scorer with six goals. His return to Werder Bremen on loan has helped to revive his career after leaving the club in 2023 to then have mixed spells at Dortmund (where he left after a year), West Ham and AC Milan on loan. However, it has not just been Füllkrug who has made Bremen's attack one to be feared this season as Marco Grüll has set up four goals and sits as the league's highest assister. Despite the attacking power, Bremen have been vulnerable at the back in conceding 12 goals and are yet to keep a clean sheet this season. Sitting in 8th place, they will leapfrog Mainz if they manage to grab all three points away from home on Saturday for the first time this Bundesliga season. Before the game, Bremen coach Daniel Thioune said: “Mainz defend a lot with a low block and are very physical and strong. We have to be at 100 percent.” Team news Felix Agu, Moussa N'Diaye, Jens Stage, Skelly Alvero, Salim Musah, Niklas Stark, Keke Topp and Justin Njinmah make for a lenghty injury list for Werder Bremen. Senne Lynen is also a doubt for the tie.

item.title: Bukayo Saka injury ‘not good’ as Arsenal face nervous wait
item.description: Arsenal are still yet to discover the extent of Bukayo Saka ’s thigh injury but Mikel Arteta has admitted the early signs are “not good”. The England international pulled up with the issue in the first half of the 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday. Saka is set to undergo further assessment ahead of Arsenal’s home match against Everton on Saturday. Bukayo Saka leaves the pitch after incurring an injury (Adam Davy/PA) (PA Wire) But he did not train on Friday and Arsenal face a nervous wait before discovering how long he could be sidelined for. The BBC reported that Saka could miss a minimum of six weeks, up to two months, with the quadriceps problem. “He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury,” Arteta said. "We will know more probably tomorrow. We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. "Obviously when a player has to walk off the pitch and is struggling to walk without any pain and is restricted to movement, they are not good signs. “So let's be very patient so we can give a definitive assessment, and then let you know." Saka’s injury means Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze will have the opportunity to start against Everton. Madueke scored Arsenal’s winner at Nottingham Forest last Sunday while Eze was on target in the draw at the Allianz Arena in midweek. With forward Christos Tzolis also sidelined, Madueke and Eze will be given additional responsibility for leading Arsenal’s attack. Saka missed several stretches of the past two seasons due to a mixture of muscle injuries - dealing with hamstring, thigh and hip problems. Saka went down unopposed before limping off in Munich (Reuters) The 25-year-old was also affected by an Achilles injury over the final stretch of last season, which impacted his fitness at the summer’s World Cup. Arsenal play five times before the November international break and travel to Liverpool in the Premier League next weekend. Following Saturday’s home game against Everton, there are also trips to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup and Slavia Prague in the Champions League. They conclude the stretch of fixtures by hosting Hull in the Premier League on 7 November ahead of the two-week international window. A longer lay-off could rule Saka out of matches against Newcastle, Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham and Real Madrid after the break.

item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added.

By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added. The post Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Locksley the first domino to fall; is anybody next?
item.description: Nov 30, 2019; East Lansing, MI, USA; Maryland Terrapins head coach Mike Locksley stands on the field during the second half against the Michigan State Spartans at Spartan Stadium. Kenahora is meant to ward off bad things. Sort of like, don’t say it and it won’t happen. Well, The Athletic said it , or wrote it, on October 16: Why haven’t any college football head coaches been fired yet this season? Boom! Mike Locksley is gone. We recently posted about a website we came across, Coaches Hotseat , that had Locksley as the hottest seat in the country. With his dismissal – or mutual separation – the top spot among hotseat coaches falls to No. 2, Greg Schiano. Although not everyone has GS as the heir apparent, at least from a betting perspective: It took seven weeks, but Mike Locksley is the first coach fired this season. The NEW odds for "next coach fired", Via @BetOnline_ag . DeBoer and Sark 75/1. pic.twitter.com/ZW4ikB3GH6 — Pat Smith (@patsmithradio) October 21, 2026 We are at the midpoint, more or less, of the season. And as the article in The Athletic points out, firing a coach, even for teams with the financial wherewithal, is not an easy call. According to agents, administrators and coaches who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the market candidly, many schools have finally reached a spending ceiling, leading them to rethink when to make changes and whether a change is really the solution. “It’s a combination of losing a roster and finding the budget to compete while also paying absurd buyouts,” one agent said. The money that was – or wasn’t – spent? Wisconsin is a prime example, per The Athletic article. Luke Fickell was in trouble last year, certainly among the fan base. He spoke with his AD and said he wanted to finish the job. Rather than spend money on a new coach and all that entails (and costs), Wisconsin increased its roster budget and life is once again good in Madison. The article also pointed to how Virginia did that the year before and made a run to the ACC title game. Locksley got fired during Maryland’s bye week, an opportune time to regroup under an interim. With Rutgers’ horrific start, there were some who thought that the same thing would happen: the bye week would be when the axe would fall. It didn’t, and it seems most now figure if Schiano is going to be fired, it would be at the end of the season. If…. Personally, I think it’s less and less likely that another coach gets fired during the season. Barring an egregious action or some horrific loss, it isn’t financially logical to dump a coach before the season ends. item.title: Elliotte Friedman Reveals Major Shift in What Red Wings Want for Dylan Larkin, Simon Edvinsson
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings could be changing their approach to the trade market, and NHL insider Elliotte Friedman has revealed what interim general manager Shawn Horcoff is now looking for. With the futures of Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson uncertain, Detroit reportedly has begun targeting young centers, including prospects who have not yet reached the NHL. That represents an interesting development for an organization that previously emphasized receiving established NHL talent in a potential Larkin trade. It also raises a significant question about whether the Red Wings are preparing to reshape their roster rather than simply replace departing veterans. Oct 22, 2026; Vancouver, British Columbia, CAN; Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) handles the puck against the Vancouver Canucks in the first period at Rogers Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Elliotte Friedman Reveals What Red Wings Are Asking For During Thursday’s episode of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast , Friedman explained that multiple NHL teams have indicated Detroit is exploring a different type of return in trade discussions. Rather than focusing exclusively on players who can contribute immediately, the Red Wings reportedly are asking about young centers with significant long-term potential. “The one thing I think they are doing,” Friedman said , “is they’re starting to ask about young centres.” Friedman also indicated that Detroit is examining highly regarded prospects who have not yet established themselves in the NHL. He emphasized that he could not definitively say whether those discussions involved Larkin, Edvinsson, or both players. That distinction is important because it does not mean Detroit has decided to trade either player. However, it does suggest Horcoff is preparing for multiple possibilities as the organization navigates two difficult situations involving players once viewed as long-term cornerstones. Detroit’s Interest in Young Centers Makes Sense The Red Wings have spent years attempting to establish reliable center depth, but the organization still has significant questions beyond Larkin. Andrew Copp remains an option down the middle, while Emmitt Finnie has moved from the wing to center as Detroit searches for additional answers.
