item.content:encoded: The Detroit Red Wings could be changing their approach to the trade market, and NHL insider Elliotte Friedman has revealed what interim general manager Shawn Horcoff is now looking for. With the futures of Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson uncertain, Detroit reportedly has begun targeting young centers, including prospects who have not yet reached the NHL. That represents an interesting development for an organization that previously emphasized receiving established NHL talent in a potential Larkin trade. It also raises a significant question about whether the Red Wings are preparing to reshape their roster rather than simply replace departing veterans. Oct 22, 2026; Vancouver, British Columbia, CAN; Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) handles the puck against the Vancouver Canucks in the first period at Rogers Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Elliotte Friedman Reveals What Red Wings Are Asking For During Thursday’s episode of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast , Friedman explained that multiple NHL teams have indicated Detroit is exploring a different type of return in trade discussions. Rather than focusing exclusively on players who can contribute immediately, the Red Wings reportedly are asking about young centers with significant long-term potential. “The one thing I think they are doing,” Friedman said , “is they’re starting to ask about young centres.” Friedman also indicated that Detroit is examining highly regarded prospects who have not yet established themselves in the NHL. He emphasized that he could not definitively say whether those discussions involved Larkin, Edvinsson, or both players. That distinction is important because it does not mean Detroit has decided to trade either player. However, it does suggest Horcoff is preparing for multiple possibilities as the organization navigates two difficult situations involving players once viewed as long-term cornerstones. Detroit’s Interest in Young Centers Makes Sense The Red Wings have spent years attempting to establish reliable center depth, but the organization still has significant questions beyond Larkin. Andrew Copp remains an option down the middle, while Emmitt Finnie has moved from the wing to center as Detroit searches for additional answers. Former first-round selections Marco Kasper and Nate Danielson were expected to play important roles in the team’s future, but injuries have disrupted their development and availability. Those setbacks have left Detroit without the dependable young center depth it hoped would emerge during its rebuild. For Horcoff, acquiring a talented young center would address one of the organization’s most pressing long-term weaknesses. It would also give Detroit another potential building block to develop alongside players such as Lucas Raymond, Moritz Seider, and Alex DeBrincat. There is a downside to that approach, especially if it involves trading Larkin. A promising prospect might eventually develop into a top-line center, but Detroit would be surrendering a proven player capable of handling that responsibility right now. Dylan Larkin Trade Talks Could Become More Complicated Friedman’s report arrives as Detroit continues exploring its options involving Larkin, who requested a trade following last season. The 30-year-old center has reportedly expanded his list of acceptable destinations to 10 teams, giving Horcoff additional flexibility to evaluate potential offers. However, finding the right destination is only half the battle. Detroit must also convince another organization to surrender enough talent to justify losing one of its most important offensive players. As we previously reported , the Red Wings reportedly expressed concerns about Minnesota Wild prospect Danila Yurov serving as a centerpiece in a potential Larkin package. Frank Seravalli indicated that the two teams differed in their evaluations of the 22-year-old forward, creating another obstacle to a possible agreement. That situation illustrates why Friedman’s latest comments are particularly relevant. Detroit may be willing to consider younger assets, but that does not mean management intends to lower its standards regarding the quality of players coming back. If the Red Wings are going to sacrifice immediate production for future upside, they need to be confident that the player they acquire can eventually become a difference-maker. Otherwise, Detroit risks moving backward without obtaining the franchise-altering talent necessary to justify such a significant decision. Simon Edvinsson’s Situation Adds Another Layer The uncertainty surrounding Edvinsson makes Detroit’s reported interest in young centers even more intriguing. The 23-year-old defenseman remains unsigned, and his absence has created a substantial hole in the Red Wings’ lineup. Horcoff has repeatedly maintained that signing Edvinsson remains a priority, and he has publicly expressed no desire to trade him. As we previously reported , the Red Wings are willing to explore different contract structures in hopes of keeping their talented defenseman. Nevertheless, the ongoing stalemate has forced Detroit to consider what happens if an agreement cannot be reached. Edvinsson must sign a contract by December 1 to remain eligible to play in the NHL during the 2026-27 season. Moving Edvinsson could potentially give Detroit access to a young center that another organization would be unwilling to include in a Larkin trade. His combination of size, skating ability, and top-pair potential would make him an attractive asset for teams searching for a long-term solution on defense. Of course, that would create another significant problem for the Red Wings. Trading a 23-year-old defenseman with Edvinsson’s potential could leave Detroit searching for a replacement at one of the most difficult positions to fill. Apr 7, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings defenseman Simon Edvinsson (77) passes in the first period against the Columbus Blue Jackets at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Are the Red Wings Preparing for Another Roster Reset? The bigger takeaway from Friedman’s reporting is that Detroit may be reconsidering how it wants to construct its next competitive team. For years, the organization has attempted to build around Larkin while developing young players who could eventually help return the Red Wings to the playoffs. Now, the uncertainty surrounding Larkin and Edvinsson has complicated that vision. Horcoff must determine whether acquiring established NHL contributors or investing in younger players provides the best opportunity for sustainable success. There is also an important distinction between preparing for a trade and committing to one. Detroit could be gathering information about young centers simply to understand its options while continuing to pursue resolutions that keep both Larkin and Edvinsson with the organization. Still, Friedman’s comments suggest rival general managers are beginning to understand exactly what Detroit values. If another team wants one of the Red Wings’ cornerstone players, offering the right young center could become the key to getting Horcoff’s attention. The Red Wings have already spent a decade trying to find their way back to the Stanley Cup Playoffs, and another prolonged rebuild would be difficult for fans to accept. But making a short-term move that leaves the organization worse off for years would be an even bigger mistake. For now, Detroit’s reported pursuit of young centers provides the clearest indication yet of the type of return Horcoff may be seeking. Whether that ultimately leads to a blockbuster trade involving Larkin or Edvinsson remains to be seen.

item.title: IndyCar headed to Barcelona in 2027
item.description: (Photo by Perry Nelson/Lumen via Getty Images) | Lumen via Getty Images INDYCAR announced a new “marquee international event” for the 2027 season, a new race at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Spain as the “centerpiece” of Phase Two of the 2027 INDYCAR schedule. The inaugural INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona is slated for Sunday, July 18, bringing the North American open-wheel series to Spain for the first time. The race will also serve as a home event for Barcelona native and five-time series champion Alex Palou of Chip Ganassi Racing. This race will mark the first event for INDYCAR outside North America since 2013, when James Hinchcliffe won on the streets of São Paulo, Brazil. It is also a return to Europe for the series, which last raced at the TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands in 2007. “This is a monumental day for our sport,” Penske Entertainment Corp. President and CEO Mark Miles said in the announcement. “We are pleased to be able to take our ultra-competitive brand of wheel-to-wheel racing to Europe and thrilled that we can showcase INDYCAR in Alex Palou’s hometown. We have seen Alex’s remarkable skill and talent for several years and know his fans in Spain have been clamoring to watch him race in person. “We cannot wait to see the NTT INDYCAR SERIES compete at one of the world’s most recognizable motorsports venues set against the backdrop of a very historic and breathtaking international destination like Barcelona.” “I’m so excited to be part of INDYCAR’s first race in Barcelona,” said Palou. “It is an amazing opportunity, and it means so much to me to have a race at home in Barcelona, it’s hard to put into words. I know the fans are going to love it, and I think we are going to put on a great show. We’re going to try hard with the team at Chip Ganassi Racing to bring home the trophy in July.” “The arrival of INDYCAR is a major milestone and an exciting challenge for the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya,” Chairman of the Board of Fira de Barcelona and Fira Circuit Pau Relat said. “Bringing one of the most prestigious and spectacular championships in global motorsport to our venue strengthens our international positioning, connects us with new audiences and markets, and reinforces our strategy of diversifying the circuit’s activity through world-class events. We are working with a long-term vision to make INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona a benchmark event on the international racing calendar for years to come.” The announcement comes in the wake of Formula 1 moving away from the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, with the 2027 schedule including just one stop in Spain, at the new Madring street course in Madrid. That ends a run of over two decades at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya for the F1 grid, but the circuit’s permanent presence presented an opportunity for INDYCAR. That ends a run of over two decades at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya for the F1 grid, but the circuit’s permanent presence presented an opportunity for INDYCAR. Speaking during Thursday’s media day in Austin at the United States Grand Prix, Spanish driver Fernando Alonso talked about the series adding a stop in Barcelona. “I think it’s gonna be good, you know, obviously a historic event for our country and Barcelona. That’s the benefit of having a permanent circuit, that you have that opportunity to, to test any day in the year, but also to host races here and there,” said Alonso to the media, including SB Nation, in Austin on Thursday. “They did the WEC race last week, now Indy, they do MotoGP. “That’s why, you know, when we compare the street circuits to the normal conventional circuits, that’s the biggest advantage. And that’s why Barcelona is crucial to motorsport in Spain.” The rest of Phase Two of the 2027 INDYCAR schedule will be confirmed and announced at a later date.

item.title: Liverpool must go 'full gas' despite injury issues, says Iraola
item.description: Andoni Iraola will not relent from his high-energy playing style (Glyn KIRK) Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said on Friday he will not ease off his high intensity demands despite suffering a series of injuries. The Reds are set to be without Dominik Szoboszlai, Jeremie Frimpong and Victor Munoz for the visit of Brighton on Sunday, while Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo have recently returned from injuries picked up on international duty. Iraola's high-energy style at Bournemouth reaped success which earned him the job at Anfield, but for the first time in his managerial career he is having to deal with the added toll of European football. "The way we want to play you cannot play 70 per cent," Iraola said at his pre-match press conference. "Imagine you don't have a right-winger on the bench, I will put someone as a right-winger. I prefer to do this than you save your energy so you have to last 90 minutes. "Give everything for 60 minutes, 65, 70, 72, then someone will do the 18, 35, whatever because we need to play full gas. "I would like to say we are good enough to play 70 percent and win games but it's not (the case). We have to play our very best because the teams we have in front of us are very good." Liverpool go into the weekend four points adrift of third-placed Brighton, who are the Premier League's top scorers with 23 goals in seven games. "I think they are doing incredibly well. They deserved all the praise they are getting and I think there is little doubt there. I think it's a team that is very well coached," Iraola said. "We have to be at our very best to beat Brighton because now they are with confidence. But I also see my team in a good place." Szoboszlai's return from injury was cut short in last weekend's victory at Brentford, but Iraola is hopeful the Hungarian will not be sidelined for long. "I don't think he's far, but he hasn't trained with the group still and also considering that we started him and he had to go out, we will probably take one or two days more than we would last week," said the Spaniard. "He's in a good place. Dom is already training outside alone and he's going to train with the group but he's not ready for this one." kca/iwd

item.title: Former 1st round NFL Draft pick Anthony Richardson charged with misdemeanor
item.description: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson, a former first-overall NFL Draft pick, has reportedly been charged with misdemeanor possession of marijuana following a traffic stop in Indiana. The 24-year-old quarterback was reportedly stopped by police on October 12 in Carmel, Indiana, after officers noticed that the vehicle’s registration had expired and belonged to a different vehicle. Colts QB Anthony Richardson has been charged with misdemeanor possession of marijuana following a traffic stop in Carmel, Indiana, according to court documents, per @FOX59. More: https://t.co/Sc5awOsuK6 https://t.co/vezgxF95PL — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 23, 2026 According to reports, officers approached Richardson’s car and detected the odour of marijuana. When questioned about the smell, Richardson reportedly admitted to smoking inside the vehicle, explaining that he did so to avoid smoking in front of his children. He also allegedly acknowledged possessing a small amount of marijuana in the car. MORE: Cardinals star unlikely to play in Week 7 vs Broncos Details of the traffic stop Aug 22, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. (5) throws a pass against the Atlanta Falcons during the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Richardson was handcuffed while officers searched the vehicle, according to reports. During the search, police reportedly discovered a small mason jar containing a substance believed to be marijuana, along with an opened bag of THC-infused gummies. In addition to the reported misdemeanor possession charge, Richardson was cited for the expired licence plate. The circumstances surrounding the stop have attracted attention given the quarterback’s profile as a former top NFL Draft selection and his position with the Colts. A hearing was initially scheduled for December 9. However, that hearing has reportedly been waived, and a bench trial is now expected to take place in January 2027. A bench trial is a court proceeding in which a judge, rather than a jury, determines the outcome of the case. Further details about the proceedings have not been confirmed. MORE: Josh Jacobs speaks out while Week 7 status remains unclear Colts respond as Richardson’s season remains uncertain Aug 29, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. (5) looks to pass against the Detroit Lions during the first half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images The Indianapolis Colts have acknowledged the situation but have declined to provide further details while gathering information. “We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information,” the team said in a statement. “We will have no further comment at this time.” Richardson has yet to appear in a game for the Colts during the 2026 season. His playing time has also been limited in recent years, with the quarterback appearing in just two games last season. Selected first overall in the 2023 NFL Draft, Richardson entered the league with considerable expectations. However, injuries and limited availability have complicated his progress in Indianapolis. With a court proceeding reportedly scheduled for January 2027, the situation remains unresolved. The case represents another development surrounding the young quarterback as he looks to establish his future with the Colts. – Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter –

item.title: SparkyOS: Lightweight general-purpose Arch, on a pendrive
item.description: SparkyOS is a novel distro from the folks behind SparkyLinux: it's a version of Arch that can you can use without installing it at all. SparkyOS is a new distro from the team behind the Debian-based SparkyLinux, but it's quite different. SparkyOS is based on Arch, and it runs entirely from USB. It's not a conventional live medium – this is a full local install, but shipped as an image of a USB key that you can boot and run. It comes with the Xfce desktop and an array of apps. The idea is that you can boot and run it on any x86-64 UEFI computer, entirely from a USB key, without touching the hard disk at all. This is quite different from its forerunner, which is a relatively conventional Debian-based distro, one which The Register has mentioned a few times over the years: first back in 2015 in a lightweight distro roundup , and more recently in 2024 when we praised its array of desktop environments . Earlier this year, we noted that the latest SparkyLinux featured a complete 32-bit edition , even though its parent distro has dropped its 32-bit x86 kernel . This is also not your typical live distro. Unless you're running on some Arm computer with nonstandard firmware, most Linux distros install from an image written to a USB pendrive, the same way that they did decades ago: in the noughties when they installed from a DVD, and back in the 20th century, when it was a CD instead. Most optical media use some form of the ISO standard 9660 filesystem , which is quite limited – despite multiple extensions, the core is a basic structure comparable to the ancient MS-DOS FAT. That's not much use for Linux, which needs long filenames, permissions, and metadata, plus things like symbolic links. So, to this day, most live Linux media have a few boot files and the OS itself is kept inside a big compressed file called a SquashFS , inside which is a real Linux filesystem. However, because it's inside something akin to a Zip file, it's read-only. You can't update the OS or add new software. Some live media optionally offer persistence , which stores changes in another separate file. That works, but if you update the OS, all the original pre-update files remain untouched, and new ones are stored in the persistence structure in addition to the space still consumed by the originals. So, it's slow, and it's very inefficient; it takes substantially more space than a conventional disk install. So, although there are dozens, maybe hundreds, of live Linux media images out there, most fall into one of two types of single-purpose product: either stripped-out special-purpose distros, such as SystemRescue, GParted Live, and Grml , or Rescuezilla , or Clonezilla . Alternatively, it's a full OS, but only meant as a sampler, not for daily use, with limited and inefficient tools for updates and changes. item.content:encoded: SparkyOS is a novel distro from the folks behind SparkyLinux: it's a version of Arch that can you can use without installing it at all. SparkyOS is a new distro from the team behind the Debian-based SparkyLinux, but it's quite different. SparkyOS is based on Arch, and it runs entirely from USB. It's not a conventional live medium – this is a full local install, but shipped as an image of a USB key that you can boot and run. It comes with the Xfce desktop and an array of apps. The idea is that you can boot and run it on any x86-64 UEFI computer, entirely from a USB key, without touching the hard disk at all. This is quite different from its forerunner, which is a relatively conventional Debian-based distro, one which The Register has mentioned a few times over the years: first back in 2015 in a lightweight distro roundup , and more recently in 2024 when we praised its array of desktop environments . Earlier this year, we noted that the latest SparkyLinux featured a complete 32-bit edition , even though its parent distro has dropped its 32-bit x86 kernel . This is also not your typical live distro. Unless you're running on some Arm computer with nonstandard firmware, most Linux distros install from an image written to a USB pendrive, the same way that they did decades ago: in the noughties when they installed from a DVD, and back in the 20th century, when it was a CD instead. Most optical media use some form of the ISO standard 9660 filesystem , which is quite limited – despite multiple extensions, the core is a basic structure comparable to the ancient MS-DOS FAT. That's not much use for Linux, which needs long filenames, permissions, and metadata, plus things like symbolic links. So, to this day, most live Linux media have a few boot files and the OS itself is kept inside a big compressed file called a SquashFS , inside which is a real Linux filesystem. However, because it's inside something akin to a Zip file, it's read-only. You can't update the OS or add new software. Some live media optionally offer persistence , which stores changes in another separate file. That works, but if you update the OS, all the original pre-update files remain untouched, and new ones are stored in the persistence structure in addition to the space still consumed by the originals. So, it's slow, and it's very inefficient; it takes substantially more space than a conventional disk install. So, although there are dozens, maybe hundreds, of live Linux media images out there, most fall into one of two types of single-purpose product: either stripped-out special-purpose distros, such as SystemRescue, GParted Live, and Grml , or Rescuezilla , or Clonezilla . Alternatively, it's a full OS, but only meant as a sampler, not for daily use, with limited and inefficient tools for updates and changes. We're not sure if twice counts as a FAQ, but there are questions on StackExchange on how to install Ubuntu to USB as well as how to install Debian to USB . SparkyOS is an answer to this question. It's a complete, pre-configured installation of Arch, directly onto a USB key. That does impose some limits, so for instance, like the Desktop Classic System we looked at in January , it only includes UEFI boot files. You can't use it on a computer with just a "legacy" BIOS, and it requires format conversion to use it in a VM. The current SparkyOS version 2026.10 is the first release, but there are already some How-to documentation pages covering things like expanding the filesystem to fill the USB medium, changing its settings, and how to crowbar it into a VM. The image is 10 GB in size, compressed to 3.2 GB for download, and because this is an image of an entire key, it won't work with multiboot tools such as Reg FOSS desk favorite Ventoy . We put it onto a 64 GB key, and we chose one that has two connectors for both USB-A and USB-C ports. We tested it on our oldest UEFI box, a 15-year-old Thinkpad W520, and our newest UEFI testbed, a Dell XPS13 new enough that it only has USB-C ports. We would suggest a USB 3 key, though, and use a blue-colored USB-A port if you have one. It will run on a USB-2 only machine, but a bit slower. We tried it on our X220, currently running OpenBSD 8.0 , and it worked fine. It could even see OpenBSD’s 10 separate partitions, although not mount them. SparkyOS worked flawlessly on all three machines. The team has made some concessions to running from USB flash media. The root volume is mounted with the noatime parameter , which stops Linux from recording the last access time on files. That dramatically lowers the number of writes to the drive. There’s also no swap configured – to our surprise, not even ZRAM , which doesn’t touch the disk. SparkyOS does what it says: it's a complete, very usable, ready-to-run Linux OS, as fully capable of being updated, customized, and having apps added or removed as any other distro… running off a pendrive. We do suggest a big fast key, though, and don't fill it up. Flash isn't like RAM: you can't change a single byte, or word, at a time. Flash can only erase a whole block at a time, and block sizes vary from 16 kB for the smallest flash chips, up to multiple megabytes. To rewrite one byte on a flash drive, the storage controller has to copy a megabyte or more of data elsewhere, format the block, and then copy it back. So, leaving more free space on a flash drive gives the on-device storage-management chip more room to work. The more free space there is on a flash drive, the longer it will last. This is one reason flash-based SSDs wear out – and also why we wrote that the end of Optane was bad news for the whole industry . SSDs often have multiple, high-speed flash chips on. Pendrives don't – there’s usually just one. In a previous life, over a decade and a half ago, this vulture had a small startup company, and one of our products was a live Linux-based OS, pre-installed on bootable USB keys. I did everything I could to reduce writes to the drive: they were formatted with journalling disabled , mounted with no atime , with ZRAM for swap, the temporary-files directory kept in a RAMdisk, and more. The keys sold quite well, but one of the problems was that despite all my precautions, heavy users found that the drives simply wore out. Flash media do not fail in the same way that industry old-timers know from spinning hard disks. A dying hard disk often struggles on, just with some blocks unreadable. That’s why tools such as GNU ddrescue exist – to try to copy the data off the regions that still work. When flash media fail, they tend to fail totally: you can't read from the device at all, meaning that nothing can be recovered from them. An example of a fairly extreme adaptation in this direction is the FreeBSD-based XigmaNAS OS . In its Embedded installation mode on a flash drive, it writes its log files to a RAM drive to prevent wear to the flash. (The snag being that they are lost when it reboots .) A user add-on for to the proprietary unRAID NAS OS does the same. There's room for future enhancements to SparkyOS here. Booting from both BIOS and UEFI is already on the "to do" list at the bottom of the release announcement. Additionally, steps to keep any files the OS writes to in RAM, and only write them out to flash at shutdown time, and so on. But saying all that, it's here, it works, and it already looks like a handy tool if you regularly use multiple different computers and want to carry your own environment around with you. For routine use, though, use a big fast drive, connect it to USB-3 or USB-C ports whenever possible, and ensure it stays mostly empty — keep it under 50 percent full. Most importantly of all, regularly back up any data you keep on it. ®

item.title: Under-15s and under-17s eye Campeonato Paulista quarter-final spots
item.description: Under-15s and under-17s eye Campeonato Paulista quarter-final spots This Saturday (24), São Paulo’s Under-15 and Under-17 teams take to the field seeking a place in the quarterfinals of the Campeonato Paulista. The Under-15s will play first. After thrashing Guarani 5-0 in Cotia in the first leg of the round of 16, with goals from Juninho, Luisinho, Gilbert, Pietro and Yahgo, Vinícius dos Santos’s side will face their opponents at 9 a.m. at Estádio Brinco de Ouro da Princesa in Campinas, São Paulo state. Thanks to their first-leg advantage, the Tricolor can lose by up to four goals and still qualify. Next, at 11 a.m., the Under-17s will face I9 at CFA Laudo Natel in Cotia, São Paulo state. In the first leg, played at I9’s training ground in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo state, Alexandre Torrezan’s side won 4-0, with two goals from Kelvyn and one each from Nicolas Francisco and Brenno. The team will now look to secure qualification at home. The match will be broadcast exclusively on SPFC Play. Both teams head into these matches with strong records in the state championship. The Under-17s finished top of their group in both the first and second stages. In total, they recorded 12 wins, three draws and three defeats, scoring 57 goals and conceding 15. They then faced Meia Noite, winning the first leg 2-0 away before cruising to a 6-0 victory in the return leg in Cotia. The Under-15s also topped their group in both previous stages, recording 14 wins, three draws and just one defeat. The team scored 68 goals and conceded 10. In the third stage, they faced AA Flamengo, drawing the first leg 1-1 away and winning the return leg 3-0 in Cotia. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Who Skip Bayless thinks will win the NFC North following the Chicago Bears’ latest game
item.description: Photo by Steve Zak Photography/FilmMagic The Chicago Bears have won the joint-most games in the NFC North at the time of writing, but Skip Bayless is not backing them to win the division. The Bears secured a 30-24 win on Thursday night against the New England Patriots to go 5-2 for the season. In turn, they are one place below the currently 5-0 Minnesota Vikings and one above the Green Bay Packers, who are yet to take to the field in Week 7 (4-2). Meanwhile, the Detroit Lions have only played five games in 2026/27 so far and have a record of 3-2. Now, Skip Bayless has taken to X/Twitter after the Bears won their Week 7 game to share his opinion that the Vikings are still going to win the division. He wrote: “Vikings are still winning the North.” The Vikings had a bye last week but are now taking on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7 on Sunday. The Colts have had a mixed start to the season, sitting with a 2-4 record. Elsewhere in the NFC North this weekend, the Green Bay Packers will take on the Lions in what could prove to be a big game in the division. Should the Packers secure the victory, they will end Week 7 with the same record as the Bears. Read more: ESPN analyst names the ‘single biggest reason’ why the Seattle Seahawks are losing games ‘Unwatchable’ – NFL fans name Amazon analyst going ‘unnoticed’ because of Al Michaels on TNF ‘Is that Eddie Lacy?’ – NFL fans have noticed a big Josh Jacobs change after his Packers return

item.title: ‘Jeremy Lin Does Not Have a Voice for Broadcasting Games,’ ‘A Natural’ — NBA World Divided As Ex-Knicks Star Makes ESPN Commentary Debut
item.description: Jeremy Lin's ESPN regular-season commentary debut sparks debate as the NBA world clashes over his broadcasting skills, delivery and sharp basketball analysis. Former New York Knicks guard Jeremy Lin made his regular-season debut as an ESPN game analyst Thursday during the Denver Nuggets’ matchup against the Oklahoma City Thunder. His commentary drew mixed reactions online. Lin first appeared as a guest analyst on NBA Today in March 2026, then contributed to ESPN’s NBA Finals and Summer League coverage before joining its regular-season game-analyst rotation. Social Media React to Jeremy Lin’s ESPN Regular-Season Commentary Debut Lin worked alongside play-by-play announcer Ryan Ruocco for the Nuggets-Thunder broadcast. It was another step in his transition from professional basketball to television commentary. Not everyone was impressed. Media personality Jason Whitlock criticized Lin’s suitability for the role. “Jeremy Lin does not have a voice for broadcasting games,” Whitlock posted on X. One X user shared a similar opinion: “Jeremy Lin is a man of many talents, broadcasting is not one of them.” Another questioned whether Lin should have gained more experience before working on a national broadcast. “Jeremy Lin pretty rough listen so far. Why do we drop these guys into national broadcasts. Get some reps first,” podcaster Chad Lowe commented . Lin became an international sensation with the Knicks during the 2012 ‘Linsanity’ run, averaging 24.6 points and 9.2 assists over a 10-game stretch from Feb. 4-20. The undrafted guard’s sudden rise catapulted him into international fame. After his breakout in New York, Lin played for several NBA teams, including the Houston Rockets, Los Angeles Lakers, and Brooklyn Nets. He also won an NBA championship with the Toronto Raptors in 2019. SEE ALSO: ‘Worst Coach of All Time,’ ‘Never Seems To Have Any Answers’ – Kenny Atkinson Under Fire As Cavaliers Squander 29-Point Lead in Season Opener His years in professional basketball exposed him to different coaching systems, teammates, and playing styles. That background gives him firsthand knowledge of the decisions players make on the court, something he can draw on when breaking down games for viewers. Podcaster Sam Vecenie offered a more favorable assessment of Lin’s work behind the microphone. “Already love Jeremy Lin on commentary. Laid back style and clear communicator, but also doesn’t dumb it down for the audience. Explains what’s actually happening schematically clearly. And you can feel like he’s only going to get better as he gets more comfortable,” Vecenie declared . Another X user called Lin a ‘natural on commentary,’ writing, “Jeremy Lin is a natural on commentary. One of the best recent hires on @espn. ” Lin’s playing career extended beyond the NBA, with stints in professional leagues overseas. He continued competing after his final NBA season, then announced his retirement from professional basketball in August 2025. ESPN brought him into its coverage

One of the best recent hires on @espn. ” Lin’s playing career extended beyond the NBA, with stints in professional leagues overseas. He continued competing after his final NBA season, then announced his retirement from professional basketball in August 2025. ESPN brought him into its coverage during the Finals and Summer League before giving him a regular-season role. Thursday’s game was his latest opportunity to adjust to working alongside an established play-by-play announcer while providing analysis for a national audience. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Carrick ‘100%’ sure he can lead United forward; Dortmund take on the influencers: football – live
item.description: ⚽ All the latest news going into the weekend’s action ⚽ Premier League: weekend guide | Mail Rob Álvaro Arbeloa’s been talking ahead of Fulham’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, and buoyed up by last weekend’s much needed win over Hull. “Nothing has changed for us,” insisted the manager, “we were not winning games but we believed in ourselves, we were doing so many things well, “The most important thing [about the Hull win] is we were in same situation against Manchester United and Ipswich but didn’t win but now we had to improve in our transition and did. We controlled the ball in their half better than before.” As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Sunday’s match at Camp Nou will be watched by hundreds of millions of viewers all over the world. A clásico always carries significance, but this weekend’s edition will be especially significant. A Barça win would move them nine points clear of their rivals at the top of La Liga . A Real Madrid victory could be a catalyst for the rest of their season. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Poulter becomes latest high profile player to quit LIV Golf
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Team Europe's Ian Poulter celebrates after his team won the Ryder Cup Golf Tournament over Team USA, at Le Golf National. (is associated with: «Ian Poulter becomes latest high profile player to quit LIV Golf») Gareth Fuller/PA Wire/dpa Ian Poulter has become the latest big name to quit LIV Golf as the ailing breakaway league looks to relaunch this year. Poulter said it was a "tough decision" to leave but he would relish "the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests." England's Poulter is the second player this week to announce he is leaving the troubled tour, after Louis Oosthuizen announced his intention to return to the DP World Tour next year. LIV is attempting to relaunch in 2027 as LIV 2.0. with new money from BC Partners Capital after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support after ploughing in $5 billion over four years. In order to do that it has had to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and, as a result, it has had to cancel the contracts of all its existing players, clearly in the hope that they will re-sign on new terms. However, Poulter will not be among them. He insisted he had no regrets about moving to the rival tour, which split the sport down the middle and continues to cause friction between opposing players. The DP World Tour has confirmed it will be taking a tougher line and that any player signing with the new-look LIV will be ineligible for membership and therefore ruled out of Ryder Cup contention. Poulter added: "Clearly LIV Golf has divided opinion, but to be part of the founding group who took world class golf around the globe... is something I will be forever proud of. "Change is never easy and it's fair to say professional golf has experienced plenty of it over the last few years. But I've always believed that change can create opportunities and ultimately lead to positive outcomes."

item.title: Eckert issues updates on Southampton duo ahead of West Ham
item.description: Eckert issues updates on Southampton duo ahead of West Ham Tonda Eckert is hopeful Flynn Downes and Cyle Larin could play for Southampton against West Ham. Downes is continuing his recovery and will be assessed ahead of Saturday’s game, with the midfielder pushing to make himself available. “Flynn is getting better day after day, will assess him today and he’s doing everything to be involved tomorrow,” Eckert said. Larin is also a doubt after suffering a hamstring issue, although Eckert confirmed his previous back problem is no longer a concern. “Cyle’s issue is part of the hamstring towards the tendon, the bottom part, but it’s the same for him,” he said. “He’s trying everything to make it for tomorrow. “It’s different, his back is fine, this just came from the collision.”

item.title: Messi Drops 2 Goals To Crush D.C. United And End Streak
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Lionel Messi proved he is still the king of Major League Soccer just four days after hanging up his Argentina jersey. He scored two goals to lead Inter Miami to a crushing 4-0 victory over D.C. United on Saturday night. This win snaps a five-match winless streak and puts the team back in the hunt for a top playoff seed. The 39-year-old superstar is not slowing down. He now has 23 goals this season, leading the entire league by a wide margin. According to Fox Sports , this performance cements his case as the favorite to win a third straight MVP award. His return to form shows that his focus is now fully on winning another MLS Cup with Miami. A Dominant Start for New Coach Kily Inter Miami needed this win badly after a rough patch of four draws and one loss. Cristian “Kily” González, the new coach who assumed control in mid-September, celebrated his first league win with this victory. The team looked sharp from the start, with Luis Suárez scoring twice in the first half to build a 2-0 lead. Messi joined the party shortly after the break. He scored in the 47th minute after Suárez set him up with a simple pass. He added his second goal in the 60th minute with a brilliant solo effort. He dribbled past two defenders and beat the goalkeeper with a precise shot from 12 yards out. This display was a reminder of why he is the best player in the world. Why His Retirement Changes Everything Messi brought his curtain down on his Argentina career earlier this week in Buenos Aires. He scored his 126th and final goal for the country in a friendly match. Now, he has a contract with Miami through 2028, so his future is secure in Florida. His coach, Cristian “Kily” González, knows exactly how to handle this situation. “He’ll be missed in that jersey, of course, but today we have him here, and we have to enjoy having him with us now,” Kily said this week. The sentiment is simple: stop worrying about the past and watch him dominate the present. In 10 straight MLS games, he has already registered a goal contribution. Inter Miami now sits second in the Eastern Conference, just behind the leaders. They need a top-four seed to secure home-field advantage for the playoffs, which begin next month. With Messi contributing 13 assists and 23 goals, the team is well on its way to becoming the first to win back-to-back titles since 2011. The next test comes on Wednesday night when they host New York City FC.

item.title: Predictions: Michigan football vs. Indiana
item.description: Angelique S. Chengelis, Connor Earegood, John Niyo, and Bob Wojnowski of The Detroit News predict the outcome of Saturday's Michigan- Indiana game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor (Noon, Fox/94.7 FM) . ▶ Angelique S. Chengelis: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham wouldn't share who will start at quarterback against the Hoosiers , because he didn't want to give Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti a head start in preparations. But Cignetti assumes it will be freshman Tommy Carr and also assumes Bryce Underwood will play and perhaps both will be on the field at the same time. IU also has a QB issue with Josh Hoover, who had right arm soreness in the loss to Ohio State last weekend but has said he's fine. This game could swing on the run defenses — Indiana ranks No. 4 nationally, allowing 75.4 yards, and Michigan is 13th, giving up an average 89.7 yards. Michigan's run game gained some confidence against Penn State in the win last weekend and finally had some big-burst 40-plus-yard runs, but the Nittany Lions have one of the worst run defenses in the Big Ten. Pick: Indiana, 20-17 ▶ Connor Earegood: Michigan finally benched Bryce Underwood , and though it'd be foolish to assume he won't find his way onto the field for a drive or two, it looks like Tommy Carr's ball. That's a lot on the shoulders of a true freshman, as his teammate well knows. Doubly so when a team like Indiana comes to town. Curt Cignetti's squad isn't the one that went undefeated as flippin' champs last season, but its defense has some premier talent, and Josh Hoover has thrown for 18 touchdowns and no picks. Seven have gone to former Michigan State receiver Nick Marsh, who caught a 20-yard touchdown at Michigan Stadium in 2024, and the River Rouge product returns to the Mitten looking for his first win against the Wolverines . This game hinges on UM's defense to put Carr in positions to thrive on the other end. Pick: Indiana, 28-20 ▶ John Niyo: Michigan's defense has done its job, and then some. But Indiana's the best team the Wolverines will have faced, and if the Hoosiers find some success running the ball, it could make for a long afternoon. Curt Cignetti's team won't beat itself with turnovers or penalties: Josh Hoover has yet to throw an interception, and only Notre Dame has been flagged less than Indiana this season. Meanwhile, asking for a mistake-free day from a true freshman quarterback making his first start seems like an extremely tall order. Michigan finally found a rhythm on the ground in the second half against Penn State, but I'm not sure that's really saying much. Pick: Indiana, 27-17 More: Wojo’s Pigskin Picks: Can Wolverines steal back big-boy status from haughty Hoosiers? ▶ Bob Wojnowski: A statement game for Michigan or another slow-starting offensive slog? Well, it could be both. Indiana and Michigan have excellent defenses ranked in the top five in the country. Freshman Tommy Carr appears to have the composure to handle this, but don’t expect him to come out wing

Meanwhile, asking for a mistake-free day from a true freshman quarterback making his first start seems like an extremely tall order. Michigan finally found a rhythm on the ground in the second half against Penn State, but I'm not sure that's really saying much. Pick: Indiana, 27-17 More: Wojo’s Pigskin Picks: Can Wolverines steal back big-boy status from haughty Hoosiers? ▶ Bob Wojnowski: A statement game for Michigan or another slow-starting offensive slog? Well, it could be both. Indiana and Michigan have excellent defenses ranked in the top five in the country. Freshman Tommy Carr appears to have the composure to handle this, but don’t expect him to come out winging it for the Wolverines. More production from the run game is a must, and perhaps Bryce Underwood could come off the bench in some run packages. If the Wolverines can’t top 20 points — they’ve done it twice all season — it’ll be up to the defense, which will have to force a turnover or two. Problem is, Josh Hoover has been mostly mistake-free (18 TD passes, 0 ints), although the Hoosiers aren’t as explosive as last year’s national champs. Indiana’s receiving tandem of Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh will severely test the secondary, and the Hoosiers won’t be intimidated by the Big House. They will be pushed hard by UM’s defense, but the Wolverines will struggle to find enough offense. Pick: Indiana, 17-13 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Predictions: Michigan football vs. Indiana

item.title: Buchtel athletic director/football coach placed on administrative leave
item.description: Akron Public Schools has placed Buchtel athletic director and football head coach Bryan Williams on administrative leave. Williams did not coach in last week's game when host Buchtel earned a 14-6 win in overtime against Garfield at Tim Flossie Stadium , and he is not set to be on the sidelines at 10 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 23 when Buchtel meets East in a Week 10 game at Kenmore Stadium. " Akron Public Schools can confirm that the athletic director and head football coach at Buchtel High School has been placed on administrative leave," APS assistant director of marketing and communications Joanne Isaac said in an email to the Akron Beacon Journal. "As this is a personnel matter, the District will not comment further on the circumstances or details. To ensure continuity for our student-athletes and football program, Tahj Dent has served as interim head coach and will continue to serve in that role pending further notice," Isaac said. "The District remains focused on supporting our students and maintaining normal team operations." Buchtel enters Week 10 with a 2-7 overall record and a 2-2 mark in the Akron City Series after it had to forfeit four wins last week before playing Garfield. APS self-reported to the OHSAA that North and Buchtel had academically ineligible players competing in games earlier this season. North's win over Cleveland East Technical became a forfeit loss. Buchtel's wins over Mentor Lake Catholic, Cleveland Heights Lutheran East and Firestone became a forfeit loss, and the win over North became a double forfeit as both teams played ineligible players. Williams did not return messages from the Akron Beacon Journal seeking comment. Bryan Williams led Buchtel to OHSAA football playoff appearances as players, coach Williams is in his sixth year as Buchtel's coach and has a 26-37 record. Williams guided Buchtel to records of 4-6 in 2021, 7-5 in 2022, 6-6 in 2023, 4-7 in 2024 and 4-6 in 2025. Buchtel won an Akron City Series outright championship with Williams as coach in 2022 and shared a league title with East in 2023. He guided the Griffins to the OHSAA playoffs in 2022, 2023 and 2024. The 2022 Buchtel team was a Division IV, Region 13 semifinalist after it defeated Woodridge and Northwest, and then lost to Beloit West Branch in the playoffs. The Griffins beat Youngstown Cardinal Mooney in the 2023 playoffs and then lost to Canton South in a Division IV, Region 13 quarterfinal. Williams graduated from Buchtel in 2005, Valley Forge Military Academy in 2007 and the University of Akron in 2009. He earned an associate's degree at Valley Forge and a bachelor's degree in mass media communications at UA. He played running back and defensive back for the Griffins, Cadets and Zips. He earned All-Ohio first-team honors while at Buchtel, and was an All-Mid-American Conference selection for the Zips. Williams did not coach in last week's game when host Buchtel earned a 14-6 win in overtime against Garfield at Tim Flossie Stadium , and he is not set to be on the sidelines at 10 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 23 when Buchtel meets East in a Week 10 game at Kenmore Stadium. " Akron Public Schools can confirm that the athletic director and head football coach at Buchtel High School has been placed on administrative leave," APS assistant director of marketing and communications Joanne Isaac said in an email to the Akron Beacon Journal. "As this is a personnel matter, the District will not comment further on the circumstances or details. To ensure continuity for our student-athletes and football program, Tahj Dent has served as interim head coach and will continue to serve in that role pending further notice," Isaac said. "The District remains focused on supporting our students and maintaining normal team operations." Buchtel enters Week 10 with a 2-7 overall record and a 2-2 mark in the Akron City Series after it had to forfeit four wins last week before playing Garfield. APS self-reported to the OHSAA that North and Buchtel had academically ineligible players competing in games earlier this season. North's win over Cleveland East Technical became a forfeit loss. Buchtel's wins over Mentor Lake Catholic, Cleveland Heights Lutheran East and Firestone became a forfeit loss, and the win over North became a double forfeit as both teams played ineligible players. Williams did not return messages from the Akron Beacon Journal seeking comment. Bryan Williams led Buchtel to OHSAA football playoff appearances as players, coach Williams is in his sixth year as Buchtel's coach and has a 26-37 record. Williams guided Buchtel to records of 4-6 in 2021, 7-5 in 2022, 6-6 in 2023, 4-7 in 2024 and 4-6 in 2025. Buchtel won an Akron City Series outright championship with Williams as coach in 2022 and shared a league title with East in 2023. He guided the Griffins to the OHSAA playoffs in 2022, 2023 and 2024. The 2022 Buchtel team was a Division IV, Region 13 semifinalist after it defeated Woodridge and Northwest, and then lost to Beloit West Branch in the playoffs. The Griffins beat Youngstown Cardinal Mooney in the 2023 playoffs and then lost to Canton South in a Division IV, Region 13 quarterfinal. Williams graduated from Buchtel in 2005, Valley Forge Military Academy in 2007 and the University of Akron in 2009. He earned an associate's degree at Valley Forge and a bachelor's degree in mass media communications at UA. He played running back and defensive back for the Griffins, Cadets and Zips. He earned All-Ohio first-team honors while at Buchtel, and was an All-Mid-American Conference selection for the Zips. Williams recevied four letters in football at Buchtel, helping the Griffins win Akron City Series titles with an undefeated league record in 2002, 2003 and 2004, and compete in the OHSAA playoffs in 2001 in Division II and in 2002 and 2004 in Division III. Buchtel went 34-11 overall and 26-1 in the City Series during his time as a player. Williams signed as an undrafted free agent with the Cleveland Browns for a few months in 2009. Between 2010 and 2013, he played for the Marion Mayhem, Fort Wayne FireHawks and Marion Blue Racers in the Continental Indoor Football League, the Pittsburgh Power in the Arena Football League and the Edmonton Eskimos in the Canadian Football League. Williams got into coaching as an assistant for the Marion indoor football team and for one season at Buchtel under former coach Ricky Powers. He spent five years as the strength and conditioning coordinator at St. Vincent-St. Mary High School before being hired as Buchtel's football coach. He worked alongside then STVM Athletic Director Willie McGee, and was the running backs coach for three seasons on former STVM coach Robert Nickol's staff. Akron Beacon Journal sports writer Michael Beaven can be reached by email at mbeaven@thebeaconjournal . item.title: Bruce Springsteen gave Brewers’ Pat Murphy special phone call before World Series
item.description: Bruce Springsteen gave Brewers’ Pat Murphy special phone call before World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There’s no doubt that Pat Murphy loves Bruce Springsteen, and The Boss gave the manager a ring before the Milwaukee Brewers start the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. Murphy, who has a tattoo quoting the song “No Surrender” that reads, “No retreat, no surrender,” received a phone call from The Boss himself, as he told USA Today. He was getting a call from an unknown number that was trying to FaceTime him. However, upon looking at the area code (732), which is from Freehold, New Jersey, he knew who it was. They had a 10-minute chat that left Murphy “blown away,” though it’s exactly “what I expected” from a phone call with Springsteen. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It was as real as you can get,” the Brewers’ manager described, “like we knew each other.” As the Brewers returned home from Los Angeles after beating the Dodgers to secure their spot in the World Series, Murphy was alerted that The Boss had called the office asking for his number. He wanted to speak with the manager, but it didn’t happen when he expected. Instead, it happened early in the morning when his kids were still sleeping. Murphy couldn’t help but fanboy a little bit. He told The Boss how he’s inspired him throughout his life and how a “big night out” is listening to Springsteen on Broadway while eating at home. Luckily, he wasn’t starstruck or nervous talking to him. He explained, “I felt pretty normal. It’s like you knew him your whole life. I feel like I do know him because I know so much about him. It was just as real as always, just like you’d want it.” He wishes he could do it all over again. After all, his fandom dates back decades. Murphy drove in the pouring rain to see Springsteen’s River Tour in the ’80s. Now, the focus is on the Brewers winning the World Series. Springsteen didn’t say he was rooting for the Brewers. Murphy said, “he didn’t go that far.” He has a few chances to “Prove It All Night” to The Boss. Related: Ex-Dodgers pitcher Dustin May gets brutally honest on reaching World Series with Brewers Related: Brewers superstar pitcher Jacob Misiorowski’s World Series strategy includes Pokemon plan

item.title: ‘I killed lots of terrorists, but it didn’t make me feel better’: The trauma haunting Israel's elections
item.description: After more than three years of war, the number of Israeli soldiers suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder following bloody campaigns in Gaza and Lebanon has risen drastically. In the lead-up to Israel’s crucial legislative elections, FRANCE 24 speaks with soldiers left shell-shocked by the country’s wars.

It feels like a missed opportunity not to stage the gala in the Blackpool Tower ballroom . Someone could take Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal for fish and chips at Harry Ramsden's afterwards. Proud as we are of that particular delicacy, there's not much us Brits can teach Germans about fried foods that taste great with a cold beer. So we just gave them Harry Kane instead. item.content:encoded: Forget the Messi and Ronaldo era, Harry Kane deserves the Ballon d'Or originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Ballon d'Or is coming to London to mark its 70th anniversary and honour the inaugural winner. In some respects, it's a shame organisers have not really doubled down on their Stanley Matthews tribute. Matthews, an all-time great of English soccer, pipped Real Madrid icon Alfredo Di Stefano to the first Ballon d'Or in 1956 when he was playing at Blackpool. It feels like a missed opportunity not to stage the gala in the Blackpool Tower ballroom . Someone could take Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal for fish and chips at Harry Ramsden's afterwards. Proud as we are of that particular delicacy, there's not much us Brits can teach Germans about fried foods that taste great with a cold beer. So we just gave them Harry Kane instead. MORE: What is the Ballon d'Or? Award history and why it matters so much to soccer players Why Harry Kane is Ballon d'Or favorite England captain Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to win soccer's most coveted individual prize. In a field featuring the likes of Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, along with resurgent 2024 winner Rodri and fellow Spain World Cup winner Fabian Ruiz, this has caused some consternation. But the numbers amassed by a 33-year-old who matures like a fine wine (crisp white, or maybe even some fizz with fish and chips) mark out an iron-clad case. Kane spearheaded Bayern's charge to the Bundesliga title with 36 goals in 31 appearances. He plundered 10 more in six games en route to DFB-Pokal glory, having also netted in the DFL-Supercup win over Stuttgart. Only Mbappe, with 15, scored more than Kane's 14 Champions League goals. At Bayern last season, Kane averaged a goal every 66.2 minutes and, with seven assists, a goal involvement every 59.4 minutes. Kane also excelled on England's run to the World Cup semifinals and is now level one of his Bayern predecessors, the great Gerd Muller, in fifth on the all-time list with 14 goals at the finals. In 2025/26, Kane scored 12 times in 14 England appearances, meaning an astonishing 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country in 2025/26. This gives Kane the second-best scoring season by an individual player this century, only behind Lionel Messi 's unfathomable 82 in 69 games for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011/12. Getty Images Kane the perfect story in the post-Messi/Ronaldo era Messi's great deeds and his Ballon d'Or duopoly with Cristiano Ronaldo cast a shadow over all candidates for the award, to some extent. Between them, Messi and Ronaldo ringfenced the prize between 2008 and 2017, winning five apiece. After Luka Modric's 2018 success, Messi won three more. It meant the Ballon d'Or became a battleground in the race to be considered the greatest player of all time. Both men are coming to the end now. Messi has retired from international football, while Ronaldo is raging against the dying of the light and the Portugal national team setup. CR7 is absent from the nominees list once again, while rumours that Messi was in line to present the main award this year demonstrated where he sat in the 2026 pecking order. MORE: Complete list of Ballon d'Or winners No one would put Harry Kane among the very best soccer players in history. He is certainly in the frame to usurp the likes of Matthews and Bobby Charlton as England's greatest ever by the time he hangs up his boots, but that is a different conversation. Is he the best player in the world right now? Lamine Yamal. Mbappe, Desire Doue and the scandalously not-nominated Raphinha would have something to say about that. But it is very difficult to argue that there is a player with a better body of work than 73 goals in 65 games, a league title, a domestic cup and a World Cup semifinal spot. And that's enough. More than enough. Voters are only supposed to consider the "reference period" of August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026. But Kane's wider story makes this feel right. He was never seen as a sure thing to make the grade at Tottenham, spending several spells of varying success on loan in England's lower leagues. There were suspicions of a "one-season wonder" when he belatedly made his Spurs breakthrough in 2014/15, but Kane kept scoring and never stopped – something that also applies to his England career after a debut goal just 79 seconds after coming off the bench against Lithuania in March 2015. Getty Images Since then, Kane has added unforeseen gears to his game, most notably his phenomenal range of passing from deeper positions on the field. Just check out his assist for Alphonso Davies against Arsenal this week. He also has one of continental Europe's best teams built around him. Historically, that sort of thing doesn't happened for English players. Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Kevin Keegan could claim that at Hamburg in the late 1970s and Jude Bellingham might end up laying claim to one of the great Real Madrid careers. But from a country that is considered soccer's homeland, Kane has put himself in rarefied company. After Matthew, Charlton, Keegan and Michael Owen, he would be only the fifth Englishman to lift the Ballon d'Or. Owen's unlikely win in 2001 came during a spell of 14 first-time winners in 15 years before Ronaldo and Messi started doing their relentless thing. Brazil great Ronaldo was the only man to repeat during that 1993 to 2007 period. MORE: The complete list of trophies Lionel Messi won for club and country No one is saying Kane should be placed alongside Messi and Ronaldo and it's not something he's ever seemed to aspire to, in a way that Lamine and Mbappe fairly nakedly do. But his 2025/26 is as good as any season from the Ballon d'Or's before times. Roberto Baggio in 1993, Hristo Stoichkov in 1994, Fabio Cannavaro in 2006 and Kaka in 2007. Harry Kane in 2026 can sit proudly in that company as a great of his era.

item.title: Bucs OC Makes Tough Admission About Struggling Offense
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 4: Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the third quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Raymond James Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) Getty Former Atlanta Falcons offensive coordinator Zac Robinson in 2025. Getty The Tampa Bay Buccaneers‘ passing offense has been one of the biggest disappointments across the board this season. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson noted that the team had a tough meeting and that they need to get back to focusing on attention to detail. “I think it first starts with our level of detail across the board,” said Robinson on the offensive woes. “We had a pretty tough meeting on Monday. Talking about the pass game and the missed opportunities and the lack of detail that we showed.” #Bucs OC Zac Robinson said that they had a "tough meeting" on Monday about the overall passing game and how they have to be better at it. pic.twitter.com/RCusYmSEsr — PewterReport 🏴‍☠️ (@PewterReport) October 22, 2026 Robinson noted that veteran Chris Godwin had a drop and that the simple things, such as pass and catch, are being missed. “We’ve got to throw and catch,” stated Robinson. “With CG, an uncharacteristic drop, for sure. Those are the big plays in those games that we need every single play.” Tampa Bay Buccaneers Passing Game Struggles Through Week 6 Getty offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. Robinson noted that it is not just Godwin. He took accountability for the issues, but added that everyone is having a role. From the defense they play to the receivers, quarterbacks, and coaches. It has combined to form a bad passing attack. “Obviously, coverage can dictate certain things,” said Robinson, noting that the opposition has a role. “Route detail, and the timing of when things are happening. Those things matter as well. So we all have to get on the same page because the pass game has not been good enough by any standard. That starts with me and starts with the rest of the guys.” The Bucs currently rank 31st in expected points added per pass attempt. They rank 28th in success rate when throwing the ball. Bucs Passing Attack Struggles As Robinson notes, there are a lot of reasons for the passing game struggles. To start, he is a new coordinator. He is the Bucs fourth coordinator in as many years, and it might be starting to take a toll on the team. More than that, they have not had Baker Mayfield for the past three weeks. To be fair, Mayfield struggled in the first three games. However, he could have been into the flow of the year by now, and the offense could have been progressing. Now, they took three games to get used to Mayfield and now three games to get used to Jalon Daniels. More than that, the pass catchers are not holding up their end of the bargain. Bucs Passing Attack Struggles As Robinson notes, there are a lot of reasons for the passing game struggles. To start, he is a new coordinator. As Robinson noted, Godwin has made uncharacteristic drops. He is getting older, and his injuries have sapped some of his explosiveness. Emeka Egbuka dealt with turf toe in the offseason and has not been as efficient at the start of the regular season. Ted Hurst is a third-round rookie, and Jalen McMillan is on the IR. They are not getting enough from this group. With all of it combined, they have one of the worst passing attacks in the NFL . item.title: 4-star PF Jayon Connor Commits to Wake Forest
item.description: Feb 7, 2023; Winston-Salem, North Carolina, USA; A general view of a Wake Forest Demon Deacons basketball in front of the ACC floor logo prior to the first half at Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: William Howard-USA TODAY Sports As the Deacs get ready for opening night in a couple of weeks, the staff has picked up a commit from local 4-star power forward Jayon Connor NEWS: 4⭐️ Jayon Connor has committed to Wake Forest, he told @Rivals . ⁰⁰The 6-foot-7 forward is a top-100 recruit in the 2027 class. https://t.co/xwhtJUjkaj pic.twitter.com/fgAQnr0MXp — Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton) October 23, 2026 Connor is a 6-7 PF who plays right down the road at Forsyth Country Day. He is rated as a 4-star prospect and the 83rd best player in the 2027 class by 247Sports. He chose to stay in Winston Salem and play for the Deacs over competing offers from a ton of schools, including: Virginia Tech, Clemson, NC State, Georgia Tech, Houston, Illinois, Tennessee, Texas A&M, Vanderbilt, USC, and West Virginia. As a junior at Forsyth Country Day, Connor averaged 20 points, 9.4 rebounds, 1.9 steals, and 0.9 blocks per game. From the scouting reports, it seems like his biggest asset is his motor—despite being undersized for a power forward, his aggression and tenacity make him a formidable rebounder and defender. He is a player who doesn’t mind doing the dirty work or sacrificing his body to help the team. Offensively, Connor scored most of his points around the rim, either off of drives or offensive rebounds. His shooting is going to require some development—Connor shot just 2-18 (11%) from beyond the arc and 24-55 (44%) from the free throw line last season. Check out some of his Team CP3 highlights below.

item.title: Seedy K’s Card Talk: Puzzlers
item.description: This space shall be a periodic depository for random musings about U of L hoops. It is dedicated to The Professor and Bruce, sadly departed Cardinal diehards with forever front row seats in Freedom Hall Heaven. Glaring Rankings Omission. In the ramp up to the season, there have been a spate of various and sundry rankings across the universe of college basketball reportage. Best lists, etc, etc, etc. Somewhere — don’t ask where, I read too many sites to recall — there’s a list of Top Newcomers. 67 are named. Includes freshman, transfers, mercenaries from across the ponds. Three Cardinals are included. Flory Bidunga. Jackson Shelstad. Seth Trimble, fingers crossed. But . . . No . . . Obinna Ekezie Jr. Tsk, tsk. To refresh your memory about the kid who had Seth Greenberg’s head on a swivel, the numbers from his debut performance as a Cardinal in Allen Fieldhouse. 19 minutes. 16 points. 5/7 FG, including 4/6 from beyond the arc. 8 rebounds. 5 blocks. An assist. No turnovers, though to be honest, he should have gotten one for not being in the right spot to catch a beauty of pass from the Cards’ resident dime-generating Spaniard. There are debuts. And there are DEBUTS. I saw another list, Top Freshman. Not on it? Need I spell it out? The hippest Obi since his Jedi forefather Wan Kenobi. The all purpose, all over the court big that Bill Self, coach of the purported best newcomer in the land Tyran Stokes, said was one of the two best players on the court Wednesday evening. Pine Time Full Time. I found it interesting — confusing? — that rookies Isaac Ellis and Bo Zhang, along with Gabe Dynes never saw a second of action. If only to give them a few minutes to get a sense of the action in a hostile environment. Odd. Self emptied his bench. What it tells me is this. Pal Kelsey, all pronouncements that it’s just an exhibition aside, felt really compelled and driven to win the game. Which is not a bad thing, and certainly mirrors the feelings of the fan base. New Offensive Philosophy? Weren’t the Cards going to feature the inside game more this season? (Yes, I know, it was an exhibition. It was obvious PK wasn’t going to roll out the whole playbook.) Louisville took 60 shots. Half of them were threes. Only a couple of planned post ups. Though it was part of the Jayhawks’ scheme to thwart those. Two Other Guys. Not a lot of chatter about Alvaro Folgueiras and De’Shayne Montgomery. Both were really solid, mature support mates for the “stars.” AF is a great passer. Plays solid D. Hits the boards. Drains his shots. DM just plays the game. Curious +/-. Karter Knox only played 12 minutes. He was a -15, when only one other Card was a negative number at -3. Not sure what it means, frankly. He does take it to the hoop. Both of his scores were at the rim. Once on a dribble drive. The other, when he zoomed along the endline for a feed at the hoop. Next. item.title: Panthers Rookie Earns Recognition After Hot Start
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Zakee Wheatley #20 of the Carolina Panthers reacts after an incomplete pass intended for DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles in the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Panthers defeated the Eagles 25-14. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 04: Zakee Wheatley #20 of the Carolina Panthers reacts during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Bank of America Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty It has only been six weeks, but one thing that is already clear is that fifth-round rookie Zakee Wheatley has already proven he belongs in the NFL. With three starts under his belt, Wheatley has already proven to be one of the biggest steals in the 2026 NFL Draft, according to Justin Melo of Sports Illustrated. “Wheatley forced a fumble on his first NFL snap and hasn’t really looked back,” wrote Melo. “He’s been credited with allowing just 39 receiving yards in coverage and has two pass breakups. The ex Nittany Lions defender has been solid in coverage, and he’s very disciplined and willing when coming downhill to tackle.” Wheatley has 18 tackles, two passes defensed, and a forced fumble. Carolina Panthers Have a 2026 Draft Steal in Zakee Wheatley Getty Zakee Wheatley #20 of the Carolina Panthers Despite the hot start, Wheatley has maintained a humble demeanor. The fifth-round rookie noted that he has heard about the talk around him and that he has seen his PFF grades. However, his focus is blocking out the noise. “I’m really just trying to get better every day and not look at that,” said Wheatley . “Whether it’s good noise, bad noise, keep my head down and keep working and keep getting better.“ Wheatley has an 89.8 PFF grade, which is elite. However, the rookie not focusing on that is exactly the type of person that second-team All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd sees that makes Wheatley so great. Lloyd noted that he is humble off the field, but plays with a chip on his shoulder on the field. “The person he is, real humble, great teammate, great person to have in the locker room,” said Lloyd. “He has a chip on his shoulder, which is great.” #Panthers inside linebacker Devin Lloyd on safety Zakee Wheatley, who has had a heck of a start to his NFL career. Among the positives: “He’s got a chip on his shoulder, which is great.” pic.twitter.com/jMyx1nkd4i — Alex Zietlow (@alexzietlow05) October 22, 2026 He noted that what impresses him most is that he is so good at communicating. That is hard to do in the NFL at all, let alone for a rookie. “Really good at communicating, knowing where he needs to be, what he needs to say to whoever he needs to say it to,” said Lloyd on the confidence Wheatley brings. “Continuing to master the scheme allows him to be in the right position. When you have that then you let your ability take over and make the play

When you have that then you let your ability take over and make the plays and be the player that he is.” Wheatley did not take a defensive snap in Week 1, but has started to become a mainstay on defense. Wheatley is Unlocking Panthers Defense The team has been able to put veteran safety Trevon Moehrig into the slot due to the addition of Wheatley. The Panthers play Wheatley and Nick Scott at safety, which puts Moehrig in much more of a versatile role. The Panthers can now use him like the Chargers use Derwin James or the Baltimore Ravens use Kyle Hamilton. It makes him much more valuable. So, the addition actually improves two positions. This has allowed the Panthers’ defense to survive a lot of injuries at cornerback and on the defensive line. item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Atiku challenges Tinubu to name ministers, appointees involved in alleged bribery
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to identify those who allegedly received billions of naira in bribes from ministers to secure appointments, following the allegation by All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign spokesperson Alwan Hassan. Atiku made the demand in a post on his X handle on Friday, questioning who received the alleged payments and criticising the Tinubu administration over the rising cost of living and the funding of ministries. “Bola @officialABAT, your campaign spokesman has admitted that ministers paid billions in bribes to secure their appointments. You appointed them, so who received the money? Nigerians deserve names, not silence,” Atiku wrote. The former vice president also blamed the administration’s decisions for the cost-of-living crisis, alleging that the government’s handling of ministry funding had left Nigerians bearing the consequences. “Your government’s reckless decisions have driven the cost-of-living crisis. And when you withhold funds from ministries because you distrust your own ministers, Nigerians are left paying for a government that has abandoned them,” he added. Bola @officialABAT , your campaign spokesman has admitted that ministers paid billions in bribes to secure their appointments. You appointed them, so who received the money? Nigerians deserve names, not silence. Your government’s reckless decisions have driven the cost-of-living… pic.twitter.com/OlNYIfOCbf — Atiku Abubakar (@atiku) October 23, 2026 Hassan, a spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, made the allegation during an interview on Arise News on Thursday while defending Tinubu’s record ahead of the 2027 general election. He alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and then focus on recovering the money after assuming office. He also maintained that the practice was not limited to the APC administration but predated the party’s time in government. “A lot of ministers pay billions to be appointed, and the first thing they think of is how to recoup that money after being appointed,” Hassan said. “It is the truth about our country and not just APC ministers; it started before the APC,” he added. Hassan did not name any minister who allegedly paid for an appointment or identify the recipients of the purported payments in the reported interview. While defending Tinubu’s administration, the APC campaign spokesperson also cited government initiatives in the power sector and education, including funding for electricity meters and the renovation of primary schools and classrooms, as examples of the administration’s performance ahead of the 2027 election. The post Atiku challenges Tinubu to name ministers, appointees involved in alleged bribery appeared first on Vanguard News .
