item.title: Crude oil rises to $115 with stocks mixed on earnings, AI
item.description: Oil prices traded at five-month highs on Friday, with benchmark crude contract Brent North Sea rising above $115 a barrel, as the Middle East conflict raged on. Global markets were contending “with concerns around surging oil prices and the sustainability of AI spending”, noted AJ Bell head of financial analysis Danni Hewson. “Oil is at five-month highs amid speculation there may be renewed US-Israeli strikes after next month’s US midterm elections. “Escalating tensions in Ukraine and the prospect of increased energy demand as the northern hemisphere heads into the winter months are only adding to the upwards pressure on oil and gas prices,” Hewson added. Benchmark international oil contract Brent crude for December delivery rose as high as $115.45. Wall Street’s main indices slid at the start of trading, with the blue-chip Dow sinking one percent. “The ongoing agitation of the oil market has contributed to the lack of a buy-the-dip impulse” that has often helped Wall Street stocks avoid pulling lower this year. High oil prices also “keep inflation concerns and rate hike concerns on the front burner”, he added. Higher borrowing costs would make it more expensive for companies to borrow, which could pull the rug out from under breakneck development of AI that is being financed by debt and has underpinned the rise in equity markets this year. Stock markets mostly dropped in Europe following some poorly-received earnings from Gucci parent Kering and Swedish group Volvo Cars. Asian equity indices closed out the week mixed as technology firms managed to claw back some of the week’s hefty losses. Rising energy prices have influenced movements across stock markets in recent days along with developments in the AI sector. Facebook parent Meta and chip equipment maker Lam Research saw their share prices dive this week despite above-forecast earnings for the pair. “Strong results are no longer enough if the outlook fails to match an already demanding valuation,” noted Fawad Razaqzada, a markets analyst at traders FOREX.com. “Investors are becoming much less forgiving.” Non-AI companies have also seen their share prices slump this week. Kering shed more than 16 percent in Paris afternoon deals on Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand. Volvo Cars meanwhile plunged more than 26 percent after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss. In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally. Aside from energy markets, AI and earnings next week, focus will fall firmly on interest-rate meetings for the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank, as well as an update on US economic growth data. – Key figures at around 1330 GMT – Brent North Sea crude: UP 1.9 percent at $115.29 per barrel West Texas Intermediate: UP 2.3

item.title: Gunmen kill 7 at church in southern Jordan
item.description: Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded 10 more in an attack on a church in southern Jordan on Friday, authorities said. Two assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate before opening fire, the public security directorate said in a statement. “Seven people died at least… while around 10 people were wounded, some of them critically,” the directorate said. The gunmen got out of a vehicle and opened fire during a funeral procession, it added, saying that a manhunt was underway for the perpetrators. Minister of Government Communications Mohammed Al-Momani said security forces were investigating the attack. An eyewitness told the kingdom’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka that a vehicle arrived carrying the gunmen, who fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing the scene. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said, adding that most of the victims were aged between 50 and 70. Karak is home to a significant Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom. AFP The post Gunmen kill 7 at church in southern Jordan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Umahi accuses Obi of starting confrontation, faults his silence over supporters’ ‘Jesus’ remarks
item.description: Minister of Works David Umahi has accused former Anambra State governor Peter Obi of initiating their public disagreement, saying the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate first confronted him at a construction site. In an interview with Arise News, Umahi said Obi had publicly criticised him while he was working at the site, describing the incident as unfair. “I did not criticise Peter Obi; he started the confrontation by coming to the construction site where I was working and publicly castigating me. I consider that very unfair,” Umahi said. The minister added that his comments about Obi were a response to what he described as a pattern of condemning others. “I only said that when you continually condemn others, you bring judgment upon yourself,” he said. Umahi also faulted Obi for allegedly failing to caution some of his supporters over comments he considered offensive to Christians. He cited a remark reportedly made by one of Obi’s supporters that even if Jesus contested an election, Obi would win, describing it as an affront to the Christian faith. “One of them reportedly said that even if Jesus contested in an election, Peter Obi would win. That is an affront to our faith, and I expected Peter Obi to speak out against such a statement,” he said. The minister’s comments followed his criticism of Obi’s presidential credentials, arguing that the former Anambra governor was not the best candidate the South-East could produce. “Peter Obi is not the best of our finest in South-East,” Umahi said. “He’s not the best; he can never be the best.” Umahi maintained that his position was not motivated by personal differences with Obi, but by his belief that the region had other qualified political figures who could pursue the presidency. The former Ebonyi State governor argued that anyone seeking to represent the South-East’s political interests at the national level should first consult governors and other influential leaders in the region. “You cannot play politics in South-East without consulting people like us,” he said. Umahi said building consensus among regional stakeholders was important for anyone seeking to advance a presidential ambition on behalf of the South-East. The post Umahi accuses Obi of starting confrontation, faults his silence over supporters’ ‘Jesus’ remarks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Conte dismisses Man Utd job talks as ‘unfounded’ amid Carrick uncertainty
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Antonio Conte has dismissed reports linking him with Manchester United as Michael Carrick’s potential replacement, describing claims that he has demanded full control of the club’s transfer policy and made financial demands as “unfounded”. According to the BBC, the former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager said he was not in advanced negotiations with any club, despite reports in the Italian media that he had held talks with Manchester United’s board following their 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como. “My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage,” Conte wrote on Instagram. “I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my ‘strong personality’. These reports are unfounded.” The 57-year-old added that he would only discuss terms with a club if a concrete opportunity emerged, insisting that any agreement would have to consider the needs of both parties. “Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management,” Conte said, according to Reuters. “It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.” Conte is a free agent after leaving Napoli, where he won the Serie A title in the 2024-25 season. He previously guided Chelsea to the Premier League title in his debut campaign in 2016-17 and won the FA Cup the following season. Carrick’s future under scrutiny Speculation over Conte’s future at Old Trafford comes amid growing uncertainty surrounding Carrick, whose position has come under pressure following United’s heavy defeat by Como. The loss extended United’s winless run to seven matches in all competitions, while captain Bruno Fernandes questioned the team’s tactics and said the side had developed a “mood of defeat”. Although Carrick is expected to remain in charge for Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth, the BBC reports that United have begun identifying potential replacements. Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have also been linked with the job. Hurzeler distances himself from Man Utd links Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler has also played down speculation linking him with the United vacancy, insisting that his focus remains on his current club. Brighton are third in the Premier League, and the German manager is under contract until 2029. “I am really focused on my job here. I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days,” Hurzeler said. He also expressed respect for Carrick, describing the United head coach as “a great human being” and “a great personality”. Conte, who previously managed Tottenham before leaving in March 2023, has not confirmed when he intends to return to management. Th

He also expressed respect for Carrick, describing the United head coach as “a great human being” and “a great personality”. Conte, who previously managed Tottenham before leaving in March 2023, has not confirmed when he intends to return to management. item.title: Experts cast doubt on Anthropic report detailing how AI has altered work at the company
item.description: Anthropic claims AI will shift how work gets done and labor demand – but some experts are skeptical of the vision Last year, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that artificial intelligence could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs and that in six months it would be writing 90% of code . Neither of those predictions came to pass. Now, in a report Anthropic published on Thursday, the company said it was hiring fewer junior technical workers and that human attention has become the new “bottleneck” as it increasingly relies on its Claude AI agents. Continue reading...

item.title: 5 Sci-Fi Books That Are A Masterclass In Prose Writing
item.description: Although most good sci-fi books boast well-written prose, some stand out for several reasons. Take Time of Changes by Robert Silverberg, which is set in a world that forbids expressions of individuality, leading to a narrator who deliberately rebels by using terms like “I” or “me” repeatedly. Conversely, some books simply feature beautiful prose without any narrative gimmicks, elevating them to must-reads. Without further ado, here are five sci-fi books that are a masterclass in prose.

item.title: Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026
item.description: null The Griffin-1 lunar lander undergoes testing at NASA's Jet Propulsion Lab. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year. What is it? At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1 ) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. The spacecraft was put through environmental testing that explored how the vehicle will fare in the extreme conditions it will experience on its ride to the surface of the moon . This testing simulated the extreme temperatures, shaking and even the sounds that the spacecraft will experience from launch to landing. And, as JPL announced recently, the lander passed this series of tests with flying colors, as we can see in this image snapped Aug. 31 of the lander inside the 25-foot-wide (7.6 meters) space simulator at JPL. "NASA JPL’s Environmental Test Laboratory has been putting robotic explorers to the test since the Ranger program gave us NASA’s first up-close views of the moon's surface in the mid-1960s. We’re proud to provide our expertise and facilities to support this new phase of commercial lunar exploration," Charles Whetsel, manager for the Exploration Systems Development Office at JPL, said in a statement . Why is it incredible? Griffin-1 is expected to launch to the moon later this year as part of NASA's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative. The spacecraft will carry over 1,100 pounds (455 kilograms) of cargo to its landing site near the lunar south pole. In this cargo will be science experiments and new technologies that will be tested on the moon's surface, including Astrolab's FLIP rover , which will explore the lunar surface with a history-making supercomputer onboard. This suite of experimental hardware won't just expand our understanding of the moon up close. Griffin-1's exploration will also help set the stage for a future, crewed moon base , which NASA aims to build near the south pole over the next half-decade or so.

item.title: Man United goalie Onana rushed to hospital after car accident in Turkey
item.description: Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana was taken to hospital following a car accident in Turkey after Trabzonspor’s 2-0 victory over Hearts in the Conference League on Thursday. The Cameroon international was reportedly rear-ended by another vehicle, with images from the scene appearing to show debris from the collision. Onana was taken to hospital for medical checks but was later discharged after the results came back clear. Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan confirmed the incident while providing an update on the goalkeeper’s condition. “Andre Onana was involved in a road traffic accident earlier this evening. There are no problems with him, and we wish him a speedy recovery,” as reported by GOAL. Onana has made an impressive start to life at the Turkish club, where he is spending a second spell on loan from Manchester United. The 30-year-old started Thursday’s victory over Hearts, which followed Trabzonspor’s 4-2 win over Finnish side KuPS. The result also marked his fourth clean sheet in five games for the club. Trabzonspor have enjoyed a strong run of form in recent weeks, defeating Turkish heavyweights Besiktas and Galatasaray by an aggregate score of 6-0. The team will return to league action against Rizespor next Monday, giving Onana time to rest and recover before the fixture, depending on his condition following the accident. Onana joined Manchester United from Inter Milan in the summer of 2023 for £43.8 million but struggled to establish himself consistently during his time at Old Trafford. His position at the club came under pressure following the arrival of goalkeeper Senne Lammens, prompting his temporary move to Trabzonspor. During his previous spell at Manchester United, Onana made 42 appearances and kept six clean sheets. However, his return to Trabzonspor has offered signs of improvement, with the goalkeeper already approaching that clean-sheet tally as his side continues its positive start to the season. Vanguard News The post Man United goalie Onana rushed to hospital after car accident in Turkey appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Brazil presidential election dogged by alleged bias by Meta AI tools
item.description: Supporters of Lula protest at Meta’s headquarters in Dublin Natalia Campos/Getty Images A deluge of AI-generated content and unfair treatment by social media platforms could prove pivotal in Brazil’s presidential election , according to supporters of the left-wing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Lula will face off against right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro on 25 October in the second round of the contest. Lula’s campaign has formally accused Meta – which owns WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook – of favouring Bolsonaro by suspending Lula’s campaign advertising account, suppressing posts and blocking AI-generated content. Read more The truth about social media and screen time’s impact on young people Brazil’s electoral prosecutors have said Meta failed to fully comply with court orders to ensure equal treatment of both candidates, while United Nations human rights experts have said they are concerned by possible unequal treatment of the two campaigns. Advertisement Images have widely circulated showing Meta AI, a chatbot integrated into WhatsApp, refusing to generate campaign posters for Lula, while instantly producing an image for “Flávio”. In a statement, Meta said “claims that we are favoring or interfering on behalf of any candidate or political group are false and unfounded”. It said Lula’s account was suspended for 1 hour by mistake and that its systems blocked prompts referring to the names “Lula” and “Bolsonaro”, but not the common first names Luiz or Flávio. Free newsletter Sign up to The Daily Sign up to newsletter Lula’s campaign remains unconvinced. It submitted screenshots to the electoral court showing Meta AI repeatedly assigning Bolsonaro’s electoral number, 22, to generic, fictional politicians and allegedly translating “Flávio futuro presidiário ” (“Flávio future prisoner”) as “Flávio future president”. Determining whether the discrepancies are deliberate is impossible because Meta’s systems are opaque, says David Nemer at the University of Virginia. “But when a technical glitch tends to repeat its outcome, it’s very hard to accept that this is just a technical failure.” Lula finished behind Bolsonaro in the first round of voting, but polls show the gap is narrowing. The comeback has been partly credited to Lula’s Army, an intensive online campaign in which 8 million WhatsApp channel subscribers receive daily tasks, such as posting photographs on Instagram posing with their fingers forming an L. This year’s general election is Brazil’s first since large language models (LLMs) became widely popular, and it is awash with AI-generated content. Experts say Latin America’s largest democracy offers a glimpse of what is to come for AI in politics. item.dc:creator: Luke Taylor
item.content:encoded: Supporters of Lula protest at Meta’s headquarters in Dublin Natalia Campos/Getty Images A deluge of AI-generated content and unfair treatment by social media platforms could prove pivotal in Brazil’s presidential election , according to supporters of the left-wing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Lula will face off against right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro on 25 October in the second round of the contest. Lula’s campaign has formally accused Meta – which owns WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook – of favouring Bolsonaro by suspending Lula’s campaign advertising account, suppressing posts and blocking AI-generated content. Read more The truth about social media and screen time’s impact on young people Brazil’s electoral prosecutors have said Meta failed to fully comply with court orders to ensure equal treatment of both candidates, while United Nations human rights experts have said they are concerned by possible unequal treatment of the two campaigns. Advertisement Images have widely circulated showing Meta AI, a chatbot integrated into WhatsApp, refusing to generate campaign posters for Lula, while instantly producing an image for “Flávio”. In a statement, Meta said “claims that we are favoring or interfering on behalf of any candidate or political group are false and unfounded”. It said Lula’s account was suspended for 1 hour by mistake and that its systems blocked prompts referring to the names “Lula” and “Bolsonaro”, but not the common first names Luiz or Flávio. Free newsletter Sign up to The Daily Sign up to newsletter Lula’s campaign remains unconvinced. It submitted screenshots to the electoral court showing Meta AI repeatedly assigning Bolsonaro’s electoral number, 22, to generic, fictional politicians and allegedly translating “Flávio futuro presidiário ” (“Flávio future prisoner”) as “Flávio future president”. Determining whether the discrepancies are deliberate is impossible because Meta’s systems are opaque, says David Nemer at the University of Virginia. “But when a technical glitch tends to repeat its outcome, it’s very hard to accept that this is just a technical failure.” Lula finished behind Bolsonaro in the first round of voting, but polls show the gap is narrowing. The comeback has been partly credited to Lula’s Army, an intensive online campaign in which 8 million WhatsApp channel subscribers receive daily tasks, such as posting photographs on Instagram posing with their fingers forming an L. This year’s general election is Brazil’s first since large language models (LLMs) became widely popular, and it is awash with AI-generated content. Experts say Latin America’s largest democracy offers a glimpse of what is to come for AI in politics. Fact-checking organisation Lupa identified 920 pieces of AI-generated or manipulated election content ahead of the first round, primarily on Facebook and Instagram, 60 per cent of it unlabelled. Another investigation found that 26 Meta advertising accounts appeared to sidestep restrictions on foreign-funded political advertising by posting AI-generated videos, including one depicting Bolsonaro and Argentina’s president Javier Milei freeing Brazil from communists. Read more Do AIs already process information in a way that gives rise to consciousness? Meta’s independent oversight board says the company’s election safeguards have failed . “It’s very worrying,” says Nemer. “So much of our political campaign dynamics have been transferred to privatised companies that we have no idea how they operate.” Regulating AI in political campaigns won’t be as simple as it seems, says Heloísa Massaro at InternetLab, a Brazilian digital rights non-profit that studied how eight major AI chatbots respond to questions about Brazil’s election. Its report found that chatbots sometimes refused genuine questions about candidates, referring users to official electoral websites, but would agree to draft misleading claims questioning the integrity of elections for use in campaigning. Massaro says clearer safeguards for LLMs are needed, but first their objectives must be defined. “Are the safeguards working? That’s one question. But working for what, because it depends on what your goals are,” she says. “Is the solution to send people away without providing any kind of information? Is this what we want?”

item.title: Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri The Federal Government has secured a total of 653 convictions of persons arrested across the federation for their involvement in various acts of terrorism. The convicts, some of whom were found guilty of aiding insurgents or concealing information about their operations from security agencies, were among the 1,060 persons brought before the court in the third phase of the ongoing mass trial of terror suspects. Speaking to newsmen shortly after stepping out of the courtroom on Friday, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, disclosed that a total of 880 cases had been heard, out of which the court convicted 653, acquitted seven and discharged 27 of the defendants. He said the exercise would continue and the final figures would be announced after the conclusion of the trial. Describing the current phase of the mass trial as the largest since the FG commenced the special court sessions for the prosecution of terror suspects, the AGF attributed the success of the exercise to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration. He expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho. The AGF also commended the prosecution team, the defence counsel and the security agencies for contributing to the smooth conduct of the proceedings. Among the agencies he acknowledged for their contributions were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN). According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country. On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants. He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects. He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively. On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise. He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities. The post Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects appeared first on Vanguard News .

According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country. On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants. He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects. He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively. On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise. He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities. The post Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Yemi Alade Is Counting Cash and Serving Looks in “Alhaja” Video
item.description: Yemi Alade wears a gold-embroidered black abaya in her “Alhaja” music video. We love how Yemi Alade gives us something new to talk about with each music video. If she isn’t channelling a photographer who could give Don Jazzy a run for his money, she’s stepping into the shoes of an Alhaja who clearly has money to spend, and she’s having a great time doing it. In the official music video for “Alhaja”, a standout track from her latest album, It’s Yemi Alade , the Afropop star leans into rich cultural aesthetics, striking outfits and scenes that feel like a celebration of success. Directed by Clarence Peters , the video plays with neon lighting, atmospheric torchlight and a cast that knows how to make an entrance. Yemi Alade holds a stack of cash in a scene from her “Alhaja” music video. Yemi has a wardrobe change for every mood, too. In one scene, she appears in a traditional red outfit, complete with a structured headwrap and layers of coral beads. Then comes a black-and-gold embroidered abaya, paired with bold gold hand jewellery and ornate rings. She’s giving us an Alhaja who knows exactly what she’s worth, and the styling makes sure we don’t miss it. Yemi Alade holds a stack of cash in a scene from her “Alhaja” music video. The details around her are just as fun. Vintage cars set the scene, traditional drums bring in the cultural touches, and cast members count cash beneath warm lanterns. It all adds to the video’s celebration of identity, prosperity and personal achievement, with Yemi right at the centre of it. With “Alhaja”, Yemi Alade gives us another music video with a distinct visual world, memorable styling and plenty of personality. And really, would we expect anything less? Watch the video below *** Photo Credit: Yemi Alade/Instagram The post Yemi Alade Is Counting Cash and Serving Looks in “Alhaja” Video appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: 82-yr-old US senator charged with drug trafficking, money laundering
item.description: An 82-year-old Democratic state senator in Virginia, L. Louise Lucas, has been indicted alongside six others, including members of her family, over an alleged racketeering conspiracy involving the illegal sale of marijuana and money laundering. According to the indictment, Lucas, president pro tempore of Virginia’s Senate, allegedly operated several businesses that bought and sold illegal quantities of marijuana in the state to build her family’s wealth. The indictment also accuses her of using her political influence to protect the alleged operation from criminal scrutiny and influence legislation for financial gain. In a statement on the charges, FBI Director Kash Patel alleged that Lucas worked with “a close-knit group of family members and associates” to build a “criminal marijuana enterprise”. Patel further accused the senator of using her “position as Chairwoman of the Senate Finance and Appropriations Committee to insulate the enterprise from criminal scrutiny and influencing legislation to financially benefit themselves.” Lucas faces charges including racketeering conspiracy, conspiracy to possess and distribute marijuana, and conspiracy to launder money. A Justice Department spokesperson confirmed that she had surrendered to law enforcement. Responding to the indictment on Thursday, Lucas criticised the federal government’s actions against her. “Today, the FBI, the Department of Justice, and the full weight of the federal government have been wielded against an 82-year-old great-grandmother,” Lucas said in a statement. “I grew up under Jim Crow. I’ve seen what happens when people in power try to silence those who stand up to them. I spent my life fighting back, and I’m not stopping now.” Lucas has long advocated for the legalisation of marijuana in Virginia, including through legislative efforts. However, prosecutors allege that she and her co-conspirators spent years selling and maintaining illegal quantities of the drug through various businesses and shops. Virginia recently passed a law permitting regulated retail marijuana sales from July 1, 2027. The indictment comes weeks before Election Day, although Lucas is not seeking re-election this year. Her daughter, Lisa Lucas-Burke, who was also charged in the case, is running for City Council in Portsmouth, Virginia. Virginia Democratic Governor Abigail Spanberger said she had reviewed the charging document and maintained that Lucas and her family should be allowed to defend themselves against the allegations. “They deserve the opportunity to present their defense and speak to the allegations presented,” Spanberger said. She also criticised the timing of the indictment, arguing that it could undermine public confidence in the Justice Department. “The timing of this indictment undermines the U.S. Department of Justice’s previously longstanding policy of not taking legal actions — to include indictments or significant investigative steps — close to an election and sadly, this timing furthe
item.dc:creator: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
item.content:encoded: An 82-year-old Democratic state senator in Virginia, L. Louise Lucas, has been indicted alongside six others, including members of her family, over an alleged racketeering conspiracy involving the illegal sale of marijuana and money laundering. According to the indictment, Lucas, president pro tempore of Virginia’s Senate, allegedly operated several businesses that bought and sold illegal quantities of marijuana in the state to build her family’s wealth. The indictment also accuses her of using her political influence to protect the alleged operation from criminal scrutiny and influence legislation for financial gain. In a statement on the charges, FBI Director Kash Patel alleged that Lucas worked with “a close-knit group of family members and associates” to build a “criminal marijuana enterprise”. Patel further accused the senator of using her “position as Chairwoman of the Senate Finance and Appropriations Committee to insulate the enterprise from criminal scrutiny and influencing legislation to financially benefit themselves.” Lucas faces charges including racketeering conspiracy, conspiracy to possess and distribute marijuana, and conspiracy to launder money. A Justice Department spokesperson confirmed that she had surrendered to law enforcement. Responding to the indictment on Thursday, Lucas criticised the federal government’s actions against her. “Today, the FBI, the Department of Justice, and the full weight of the federal government have been wielded against an 82-year-old great-grandmother,” Lucas said in a statement. “I grew up under Jim Crow. I’ve seen what happens when people in power try to silence those who stand up to them. I spent my life fighting back, and I’m not stopping now.” Lucas has long advocated for the legalisation of marijuana in Virginia, including through legislative efforts. However, prosecutors allege that she and her co-conspirators spent years selling and maintaining illegal quantities of the drug through various businesses and shops. Virginia recently passed a law permitting regulated retail marijuana sales from July 1, 2027. The indictment comes weeks before Election Day, although Lucas is not seeking re-election this year. Her daughter, Lisa Lucas-Burke, who was also charged in the case, is running for City Council in Portsmouth, Virginia. Virginia Democratic Governor Abigail Spanberger said she had reviewed the charging document and maintained that Lucas and her family should be allowed to defend themselves against the allegations. “They deserve the opportunity to present their defense and speak to the allegations presented,” Spanberger said. She also criticised the timing of the indictment, arguing that it could undermine public confidence in the Justice Department. “The timing of this indictment undermines the U.S. Department of Justice’s previously longstanding policy of not taking legal actions — to include indictments or significant investigative steps — close to an election and sadly, this timing further erodes the trust the American people deserve to have in the Department of Justice,” Spanberger said. Earlier this year, FBI agents executed search warrants at two of Lucas’s marijuana shops as part of an investigation that began under former President Joe Biden. According to the indictment, investigators recovered marijuana and firearms from both locations. Lucas, who was elected to the Virginia State Senate in 1991, is also accused of paying $750,000 for a 100 per cent stake in a shell holding company that prosecutors allege was established to help a co-conspirator obtain a state licence to sell marijuana. Prosecutors further allege that Lucas subsequently received what the Justice Department described as a “bribery payment” from the co-conspirator in connection with her efforts. The department also alleged that Lucas “failed to report the interest obtained in this entity on her required Statement of Economic Interests forms” as a legislator. In a statement announcing the charges, the Justice Department alleged that Lucas met with the co-conspirator at her office in the Capitol complex to receive a partial repayment. “Lucas allegedly met with the co-conspirator at her office at the capitol complex to receive a partial repayment and spoke with other officials, including legislators, about the co-conspirator’s qualification for a recreational marijuana license depending on her receipt of a bribery payment from the co-conspirator,” the department said. Investigators also alleged that Lucas spoke with an unidentified co-conspirator by phone in February about obtaining a recreational marijuana licence and sharing the proceeds. “This is our last chance at generational wealth,” investigators quoted Lucas as telling the co-conspirator. “I’ve got too old to not be greedy.” Vanguard News The post 82-yr-old US senator charged with drug trafficking, money laundering appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: TUC not part of FG talks, issued no ultimatum, NLC clarifies
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has clarified that the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, neither issued an ultimatum to the Federal Government nor participated in the dialogue between the government and the NLC held on October 22, 2026. The clarification follows media reports that mentioned the TUC in connection with the ultimatum and the meeting, prompting the NLC to set the record straight and absolve the sister labour centre of any involvement in the specific engagement. In a statement signed by its Acting General Secretary, Comrade Benson Upah, the NLC said the TUC’s name was erroneously included in some newspaper reports, while acknowledging that a greater number of publications correctly attributed the statement to the NLC alone. The statement reads: “The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) wishes to clarify that the Trade Union Congress (TUC) did not issue an ultimatum to the government and was not part of the dialogue between the NLC and Federal Government yesterday, 22nd October 2026 even as the TUC side of Joint Health Workers Union of Nigeria, JOHESU and Joint Public Service Negotiating Council, JPSNC were represented at the dialogue. “TUC’s name featured in error in a paper or two but we note that a greater number of the papers appropriately attributed the statement to NLC only. “This is to categorically state that only the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) was present at the meeting. “The TUC is completely exonerated from the purports of this specific dialogue. We urge the public and media to take note of this correction, please.” The post TUC not part of FG talks, issued no ultimatum, NLC clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The reactor meant to showcase nuclear’s comeback keeps hitting problems
item.description: US regulators have issued a warning to a nuclear project critical to Donald Trump’s efforts to revive the industry, after a contractor fell into a reactor cavity and a bundle of fuel rods nearly tipped over during refuelling. The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission told Holtec International, a company racing to reopen a shuttered reactor at the Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan, to address a “chilled work environment” that has made staff hesitant to raise safety concerns without fear of retaliation. The warning has prompted concerns among critics that financial and political pressures to revitalise nuclear power as an answer to booming AI-driven energy demand are increasing risks of accidents. item.title: Casualties Feared As Multi-Storey Building Collapses In Nairobi
item.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building — thought to have been around 18 storeys high — came down in a densely populated business and residential area of Eastleigh. AFP journalists at the scene saw the building had been reduced to a pile of rubble as a small number of search and rescue teams arrived on the scene. “There were some businesses in the basement and workers who were busy building,” said local resident Abdi Aziz, 25. “But as it was (the Friday prayer), a lot of them were at the mosque. I think few people died because no one was living there,” he told AFP. Asked if he could see obvious flaws in the construction process, he said, “Everyone rushes to build in this neighbourhood.” This aerial view shows personnel from the Kenya Defence Forces Disaster Response Battalion inspecting the rubble of a collapsed residential building that was still under construction in the Eastleigh neighbourhood of Nairobi on October 23, 2026. (Photo by TONY KARUMBA / AFP) | TONY KARUMBA / AFP Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site immediately after the incident, which happened around lunchtime. AFP saw police use tear gas to disperse crowds gathering near the site. Rescue operations had yet to begin when AFP arrived, with the site hemmed in by high-rise buildings, complicating efforts. Nairobi is undergoing a rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city, particularly in Eastleigh which is known for its busy market areas and as a hub for the Somali community. There have been many concerns over safety. There were 86 building collapses between 2009 and 2019, killing an estimated 200 people, according to a report by the Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis. An audit of almost 15,000 buildings by the National Building Inspectorate found that 4.8 percent were very dangerous, 72.3 percent were classified as unsafe, the report said. The number of buildings completed annually in Nairobi has risen from 20,025 in 2022 to 25,090 last year, according to its statistics bureau, as east Africa’s leading business hub sucks in people from rural areas and neighbouring countries. The post Casualties Feared As Multi-Storey Building Collapses In Nairobi appeared first on Channels Television .

The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. item.title: PubKeep picks up where Microsoft Publisher signs off
item.description: Microsoft ended support for Publisher this month, but users with orphaned documents still have options. Support for perpetual versions ended on October 13, but those copies will keep working without further security updates, bug fixes, or technical support. Publisher left Microsoft 365 subscriptions on October 1, although existing installations may remain accessible until removal updates arrive. Those start reaching Current Channel devices in mid-November and Monthly Enterprise Channel devices in early December. Microsoft first let users know in 2024 that the venerable application would be scrapped, and the Windows behemoth offered little comfort to those who needed it. Microsoft suggested Word and PowerPoint as alternatives, but neither directly opens Publisher's .pub files. The Document Foundation, the organization behind LibreOffice, was quick to point users toward LibreOffice Draw , which uses the libmspub library to import Publisher files and can save them in OpenDocument Format (ODF). Other alternatives aim to recreate more of the Publisher experience. Adam Anderly, founder of Texas-based Saint Systems, created PubKeep to replace Microsoft's application. PubKeep is proprietary, with no plans to open source the code. But it doesn't require a subscription: a one-time payment of $99 buys the application. The application runs on Windows or macOS, and a lightweight browser version is available. It looks a lot like Publisher, and can handle files from Publisher 2000 through 2021. Publisher 97 and 98 are also supported, but the files are sent to a conversion service (with the user's approval) to be converted to a newer format, so anybody worried about data leaving their local device should think carefully before opening those older files. Anderly told The Register that the project began after users expressed alarm about losing access to decades of files because of Microsoft's plans. The first challenge was the file format itself. He said: "Microsoft never published a spec for the .pub format. It did document some of the pieces Publisher is built on: the OLE compound file container, the document properties, and the Office Drawing records used for shapes and pictures. For everything else, we used libmspub, the Document Liberation Project's open source parser behind LibreOffice's Publisher import, as a reference. "Our testing showed it had gaps, so we wrote our own engine in TypeScript. The same engine runs in the desktop app and in the browser. From there we built a test harness around Publisher itself. We assembled a corpus of real-world .pub files. An evaluation engine renders each file two ways, through Publisher's own PDF export and through our engine, and compares the output page by page, so every change we make is scored against Publisher." item.dc:creator: Richard Speed
item.content:encoded: Microsoft ended support for Publisher this month, but users with orphaned documents still have options. Support for perpetual versions ended on October 13, but those copies will keep working without further security updates, bug fixes, or technical support. Publisher left Microsoft 365 subscriptions on October 1, although existing installations may remain accessible until removal updates arrive. Those start reaching Current Channel devices in mid-November and Monthly Enterprise Channel devices in early December. Microsoft first let users know in 2024 that the venerable application would be scrapped, and the Windows behemoth offered little comfort to those who needed it. Microsoft suggested Word and PowerPoint as alternatives, but neither directly opens Publisher's .pub files. The Document Foundation, the organization behind LibreOffice, was quick to point users toward LibreOffice Draw , which uses the libmspub library to import Publisher files and can save them in OpenDocument Format (ODF). Other alternatives aim to recreate more of the Publisher experience. Adam Anderly, founder of Texas-based Saint Systems, created PubKeep to replace Microsoft's application. PubKeep is proprietary, with no plans to open source the code. But it doesn't require a subscription: a one-time payment of $99 buys the application. The application runs on Windows or macOS, and a lightweight browser version is available. It looks a lot like Publisher, and can handle files from Publisher 2000 through 2021. Publisher 97 and 98 are also supported, but the files are sent to a conversion service (with the user's approval) to be converted to a newer format, so anybody worried about data leaving their local device should think carefully before opening those older files. Anderly told The Register that the project began after users expressed alarm about losing access to decades of files because of Microsoft's plans. The first challenge was the file format itself. He said: "Microsoft never published a spec for the .pub format. It did document some of the pieces Publisher is built on: the OLE compound file container, the document properties, and the Office Drawing records used for shapes and pictures. For everything else, we used libmspub, the Document Liberation Project's open source parser behind LibreOffice's Publisher import, as a reference. "Our testing showed it had gaps, so we wrote our own engine in TypeScript. The same engine runs in the desktop app and in the browser. From there we built a test harness around Publisher itself. We assembled a corpus of real-world .pub files. An evaluation engine renders each file two ways, through Publisher's own PDF export and through our engine, and compares the output page by page, so every change we make is scored against Publisher." He added: "For the parts no one had documented, we made small, controlled changes to documents in Publisher and studied how the saved files changed. A licensed perpetual copy of Publisher on a Windows machine is the reference." Anderly emphasized: "We never decompiled or modified Publisher itself. Beyond Microsoft's published specs and libmspub, everything we learned came from the files and PDFs Publisher produces." We took a copy for a spin and it opened every .pub file we tried, although that was hardly an exhaustive compatibility test. Anderly said the company would rapidly address problems reported by users. Register readers will be unsurprised to know that Claude Code is involved, something that Anderly says makes responsive support possible, with agents reproducing problems and writing fixes. "Most issues are fixed the same day," said Anderly. "That leaves us time to answer every report and email personally." Although the code is proprietary, Anderly told us: "The .pubk format we save to is open, so anything you make in PubKeep isn't locked in the way .pub files were." PubKeep describes .pubk as a documented ZIP-based format containing JSON and images. That makes its contents inspectable, although it doesn't guarantee another application can reproduce the layout. For Publisher users seeking a familiar replacement, PubKeep offers another option. The $99 price includes a year of support. What's more striking is how quickly a relatively small team built something that reproduces much of Publisher's functionality. PubKeep is part of a broader reimplementation trend. Other projects are taking on applications that remain very much alive, including Word, Excel, and Photoshop. ®

item.title: Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick admitted on Friday his side have “lost their way” after a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como made it seven games without a win. After a successful interim spell in charge in the second half of last season, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis just five months ago, but his position is at risk ahead of Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth to Old Trafford. United are off to their worst start in the Premier League era, were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton and have lost two of their opening three Champions League games. “Recently we haven’t had a good time. I totally accept that. We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things we were doing as a team,” Carrick said in an impassioned address at the start of his press conference on Friday. “We haven’t done well enough lately. We’ve had a spell we’re really not happy with. Como was a bad night. It hurt me. It was really unacceptable. “The supporters have to make the effort and spend the money to come and watch us. To have the feeling we all had after the game was a tough moment.” Carrick added: “My job is to put a team on the pitch that represents the supporters and that they can be proud of the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently in certain games which I am fully aware of and definintely doing something about.” AFP The post Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William
item.description: Prince William has made a rare royal appearance on a BBC chat show, with the heir to the throne confessing he would have liked to join the police or be a DJ. The Prince of Wales appeared on an episode set to air Friday evening, to promote his Earthshot Prize, which goes to environmental causes. The show’s host, comedian Graham Norton, is known for his A-list guests and mildly ribbing celebrities. Wearing a blue suit, shirt and tie, William was roaring with laughter in images released ahead of the show on his and his wife’s Instagram. He sat on the show’s sofa next to actresses Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin, all involved in the prize. Hello! magazine wrote that William is the first working royal to appear on a British talk show although Sarah Ferguson, the former wife of William’s uncle, the former prince Andrew, was interviewed by Norton when she still had a royal title. The Graham Norton Show is now in its 33rd series and is the broadcaster’s most watched chat show. Recent guests include Madonna. The BBC reported there were “cheers and gasps from the audience” when William appeared as a surprise guest. He will present the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on November 17. Launched in 2020, the prize supports initiatives that help tackle environmental crises such as climate change. As with previous competitions, this year’s winners will receive one million pounds ($1.3 million) each “to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions”, organisers said. William was asked whether he ever fantasised about another job rather than becoming king, telling Norton: “I did want to be a policeman when I was younger. I thought I could make a good one,” adding that he also went through “a phase of wanting to be a DJ — I wasn’t very good.” William spoke of his family’s love for “The Celebrity Traitors”, a devious reality show currently topping ratings. He also said he was a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan’s “Dark Knight” trilogy about Batman, which he called “psychologically dark and deep”. The prince has kept tight-lipped about the return to Britain of his estranged brother Prince Harry, who said in an interview this week with GQ magazine that he wanted things to “work out” with his father, King Charles III, and William, his elder brother. AFP The post I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Malaria: Nigeria’s prevalence drops to 15.2%, FG targets 50% reduction by 2030
item.description: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has reported a decline in malaria parasite prevalence among children aged six to 59 months from 22 per cent in 2021 to 15.2 per cent in 2025, while setting a target to halve malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths by 2030. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) Report and the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 in Abuja. Pate, who was represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, said the 6.8 percentage-point decline reflected progress in the country’s malaria control efforts but warned that the gains must be sustained. He said the Federal Government was targeting a 50 per cent reduction in malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths from their respective 2025 levels by 2030. The minister, however, cautioned against interpreting the decline as evidence that malaria had been brought under control nationwide, stressing the need for stronger prevention, surveillance and funding. He cited Kebbi State as an example of significant improvement, with malaria prevalence reportedly dropping from 49 per cent in 2021 to 18 per cent in 2025. Pate said the findings underscored the importance of using reliable data to identify high-burden communities and direct interventions where they would have the greatest impact. Bed-net use remains a concern The minister also highlighted the need to improve the consistent use of insecticide-treated nets, a major tool for preventing malaria transmission. According to the survey findings, 72.3 per cent of children and 80.6 per cent of pregnant women in households that owned insecticide-treated nets slept under one. He said the figures demonstrated the need to strengthen public awareness and ensure that households translated access to preventive tools into consistent use. New strategy targets high-burden areas Pate said the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 was aligned with the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and would be implemented through the Sector-Wide Approach, guided by the principle of “One Plan, One Budget, One Report, One Conversation.” He explained that the plan’s sub-national tailoring approach would enable authorities to direct resources and interventions according to the malaria burden and epidemiological circumstances of individual states and communities. The minister urged state governments to take ownership of their respective survey findings, align malaria control plans and budgets with identified needs, and ensure timely release of funds. He also called on development partners to align their financial and technical support with national priorities. item.content:encoded: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has reported a decline in malaria parasite prevalence among children aged six to 59 months from 22 per cent in 2021 to 15.2 per cent in 2025, while setting a target to halve malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths by 2030. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) Report and the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 in Abuja. Pate, who was represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, said the 6.8 percentage-point decline reflected progress in the country’s malaria control efforts but warned that the gains must be sustained. He said the Federal Government was targeting a 50 per cent reduction in malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths from their respective 2025 levels by 2030. The minister, however, cautioned against interpreting the decline as evidence that malaria had been brought under control nationwide, stressing the need for stronger prevention, surveillance and funding. He cited Kebbi State as an example of significant improvement, with malaria prevalence reportedly dropping from 49 per cent in 2021 to 18 per cent in 2025. Pate said the findings underscored the importance of using reliable data to identify high-burden communities and direct interventions where they would have the greatest impact. Bed-net use remains a concern The minister also highlighted the need to improve the consistent use of insecticide-treated nets, a major tool for preventing malaria transmission. According to the survey findings, 72.3 per cent of children and 80.6 per cent of pregnant women in households that owned insecticide-treated nets slept under one. He said the figures demonstrated the need to strengthen public awareness and ensure that households translated access to preventive tools into consistent use. New strategy targets high-burden areas Pate said the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 was aligned with the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and would be implemented through the Sector-Wide Approach, guided by the principle of “One Plan, One Budget, One Report, One Conversation.” He explained that the plan’s sub-national tailoring approach would enable authorities to direct resources and interventions according to the malaria burden and epidemiological circumstances of individual states and communities. The minister urged state governments to take ownership of their respective survey findings, align malaria control plans and budgets with identified needs, and ensure timely release of funds. He also called on development partners to align their financial and technical support with national priorities. NPC calls for data-driven interventions The Director-General of the National Population Commission, Dr Abuh Muhammed, said the survey demonstrated the value of collaboration between the National Malaria Elimination Programme and the commission. He said the partnership combined technical expertise in malaria control with the commission’s survey infrastructure and field operations, providing evidence to guide national planning. Muhammed reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to supporting evidence-based policymaking and urged government officials and development partners to use the findings to direct resources to areas with the greatest need. Pate commended the National Malaria Elimination Programme, the National Population Commission and other partners involved in producing the survey. He reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening domestic financing, improving surveillance and sustaining coordinated action to reduce malaria cases and deaths. The 2030 target will require sustained investment in prevention, early diagnosis, effective treatment and routine health services, alongside targeted interventions in communities where malaria transmission remains high. item.title: Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The daughters of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, say they plan to pursue careers in the film industry and continue their father’s legacy. Taiwo Halima Olamide, known as Lima Ogogo, and her sister, Shakirat Taiwo, popularly called Kira Ogogo, announced their plans in an appreciation video shared on social media on Wednesday, October 21. The sisters also thanked Nigerians and members of the entertainment industry for supporting their family following their father’s death. “You guys loved our daddy so much. This is an appreciation video to tell you people thank you,” they said. Lima, speaking on behalf of the family, added: “On behalf of my family and I, we want to say thank you very much to everybody who stood by us.” The sisters acknowledged support from several public figures, including Honourable Tayo Ayinde, the First Lady, the Ogun State governor, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and the Olu of Ilaro. They also thanked those who sent messages of condolence during the family’s period of mourning. They said their entry into Nollywood would be a lasting commitment, rather than a one-off tribute to their father. “We are going to start seeing Ogogo through my sister Kira Ogogo. We are coming to the industry, and we’re here to stay,” Lima said. The sisters urged fans who enjoyed Ogogo’s films to support their upcoming projects by watching and sharing their content, particularly on Kira Ogogo’s YouTube channel, KiraOgogoTV. Ogogo, a prominent figure in Yoruba cinema, died on August 23, 2026, aged 66. He was buried the following day in Ilaro, Ogun State, according to Islamic rites. His death drew tributes from Nollywood colleagues and admirers. The post Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: What is The Hidden Cost of Nigerian Women’s Unpaid Labour?
item.description: Mother and children preparing food in a bright, cosy kitchen setting. Credit: RDNE Stock Project/Pexels. Fadekemi was six when she first felt the sting of splattered hot oil on her skin. She recalls her mother’s stern voice instructing her on how to make stew the way her father liked it. Fifty-one years and thousands of stew pots later, Fadekemi still wonders if that’s all she was made to do. In different parts of Nigeria today, there are millions of women like Fadekemi, each spending at least 5 hours daily on unpaid care and domestic work. Although Nigerians rarely pay women for care and domestic duties, research shows that it is real work with an annual economic value of up to $111 billion . How Women Carry Nigeria’s Unpaid Labour According to the Nigeria Time Use Survey (NTUS) 2024 report, the average Nigerian woman spends 21% of her day on unpaid domestic and care work ; this equals 5 extra hours, while men spend just one hour on unpaid work. This means that after spending 8 hours at work, she spends another 5 hours doing childcare and household work, making it a double shift. Yet when you look at the economic drivers of Nigeria’s economy, her time or work does not count; it is seen as a woman’s work. This inequality is seen as invisible labour. We see it show up in different phases of women’s lives, yet we still miss how heavy an unequal burden this is. Right from when a girl is 13, she becomes an unpaid labourer, doing domestic chores, taking care of siblings, yet these contributions are seen as nothing to Nigeria’s GDP. For Fadekemi, this unpaid labour started at six, continued into her teenage years, where she became a caregiver for her siblings, extended into motherhood, and now, as a grandmother, she continues to be a caregiver for her grandchildren because even traditions like Omugwo exclude men from care duties. Behind those hours of unpaid labour is a missed opportunity for the country’s GDP growth. What Happens When Care Is Shared? In a 2026 study published in BMC Paediatrics, over 64% of women said they were the primary caregivers of their newborn children. In some cases, this is a result of traditional belief systems that reinforce gender roles and assign domestic duties to women. In other cases, it is a systemic failure caused by policies that reinforce gender inequality. In Nigeria, for example, mothers are entitled to maternity leave with 50% pay, while only fathers in the civil service are entitled to 14 days of paternity leave. So what happens to private sector fathers? The national policy designs them to be absent fathers from day one and reinforces the narrative that their sole role is to be a provider and presence doesn’t matter. Experts have highlighted that cutting a new mother’s salary by 50% while excluding most fathers from paid leave reinforces the belief that a man’s primary duty is to be a financial provider and makes it harder for them to be present. And when that happens, care once again becomes the woman’s job.
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija Features
item.content:encoded: Mother and children preparing food in a bright, cosy kitchen setting. Credit: RDNE Stock Project/Pexels. Fadekemi was six when she first felt the sting of splattered hot oil on her skin. She recalls her mother’s stern voice instructing her on how to make stew the way her father liked it. Fifty-one years and thousands of stew pots later, Fadekemi still wonders if that’s all she was made to do. In different parts of Nigeria today, there are millions of women like Fadekemi, each spending at least 5 hours daily on unpaid care and domestic work. Although Nigerians rarely pay women for care and domestic duties, research shows that it is real work with an annual economic value of up to $111 billion . How Women Carry Nigeria’s Unpaid Labour According to the Nigeria Time Use Survey (NTUS) 2024 report, the average Nigerian woman spends 21% of her day on unpaid domestic and care work ; this equals 5 extra hours, while men spend just one hour on unpaid work. This means that after spending 8 hours at work, she spends another 5 hours doing childcare and household work, making it a double shift. Yet when you look at the economic drivers of Nigeria’s economy, her time or work does not count; it is seen as a woman’s work. This inequality is seen as invisible labour. We see it show up in different phases of women’s lives, yet we still miss how heavy an unequal burden this is. Right from when a girl is 13, she becomes an unpaid labourer, doing domestic chores, taking care of siblings, yet these contributions are seen as nothing to Nigeria’s GDP. For Fadekemi, this unpaid labour started at six, continued into her teenage years, where she became a caregiver for her siblings, extended into motherhood, and now, as a grandmother, she continues to be a caregiver for her grandchildren because even traditions like Omugwo exclude men from care duties. Behind those hours of unpaid labour is a missed opportunity for the country’s GDP growth. What Happens When Care Is Shared? In a 2026 study published in BMC Paediatrics, over 64% of women said they were the primary caregivers of their newborn children. In some cases, this is a result of traditional belief systems that reinforce gender roles and assign domestic duties to women. In other cases, it is a systemic failure caused by policies that reinforce gender inequality. In Nigeria, for example, mothers are entitled to maternity leave with 50% pay, while only fathers in the civil service are entitled to 14 days of paternity leave. So what happens to private sector fathers? The national policy designs them to be absent fathers from day one and reinforces the narrative that their sole role is to be a provider and presence doesn’t matter. Experts have highlighted that cutting a new mother’s salary by 50% while excluding most fathers from paid leave reinforces the belief that a man’s primary duty is to be a financial provider and makes it harder for them to be present. And when that happens, care once again becomes the woman’s job. According to Nigeria’s proposed National Care Policy, when care duties are shared, the entire country benefits. Care moves from an unpaid, largely invisible responsibility to a thriving economic sector that creates jobs, supports businesses, strengthens national productivity, and enables millions of women to participate more fully in the labour market. Recognising the value of care work drives employment of 1.7 million mothers and could add $111 billion to the economy, 8 times more than the oil sector. This invisible labour has a price tag, and even though it appears that Nigerian women are the only ones who bear the cost, the entire country pays for it. When one segment of the population is unable to fully participate in the labour market, growth stalls for everyone. If you’d like to provide input on the draft of the National Care Policy, please do so at nigeriacarepolicy.org . The post What is The Hidden Cost of Nigerian Women’s Unpaid Labour? appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: FG Designates Redeemer’s Health Village As TETFund Centre, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy
item.description: In a breakthrough for Nigeria’s healthcare sector, the Federal Government has adopted the newly inaugurated Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Robotic Surgery Academy as the nation’s 29th TETFund Centre of Excellence, guaranteeing full scholarship coverage for all enrolled trainees. Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. Co-founder of RoboMed Global, Dr. Obi Ekwenna, emphasised that the academy relies on a total-ecosystem training model inspired by aviation safety standards prioritizing communication, simulation, and strict team coordination. “The essence of the academy is to train the entire ecosystem, not just surgeons alone,” Ekwenna noted, explaining that candidate evaluation will blend advanced simulation, supervised clinical practice, and structured patient care. Institutional Backing, Local Accreditation The National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN) will oversee the academic standards and award official postgraduate fellowship diplomas upon completion, while Redeemer’s University will lead specialised training for nursing teams and biomedical maintenance eng

By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. Co-founder of RoboMed Global, Dr. Obi Ekwenna, emphasised that the academy relies on a total-ecosystem training model inspired by aviation safety standards prioritizing communication, simulation, and strict team coordination. “The essence of the academy is to train the entire ecosystem, not just surgeons alone,” Ekwenna noted, explaining that candidate evaluation will blend advanced simulation, supervised clinical practice, and structured patient care. Institutional Backing, Local Accreditation The National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN) will oversee the academic standards and award official postgraduate fellowship diplomas upon completion, while Redeemer’s University will lead specialised training for nursing teams and biomedical maintenance engineers. Vice-Chancellor of Redeemer’s University, Prof. Shadrach Akindele, and NPMCN President Prof. Anthony Ikefuna both hailed the project as a decisive milestone. Following RHV’s landmark execution of Nigeria’s first robotic and telesurgical procedures in September, the academy is positioned to establish West Africa as a regional hub for technology-driven patient care. Redeemer’s Health Village is a faith-based tertiary medical facility established by the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG). item.title: Musk disputes NASA safety panel's lunar launch estimates
item.description: NASA's safety watchdog, the Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel (ASAP), had good news and bad news for the space agency, and SpaceX boss Elon Musk quickly disagreed with some of it. Musk disputed the reported suggestion that approximately 22 launches might be needed to support a landing by the Human Landing System (HLS) variant of Starship on the Moon. "That's way too high," Musk responded on X. "Actual number will be more like 6 to 8." The US lunar landers being developed for Artemis require refueling in space, meaning additional launches to deliver propellant before astronauts can head to the surface. During Apollo, a single Saturn V launch was enough to send a fully fueled Lunar Module to the Moon. The problem is demonstrating reliable transfers of cryogenic propellant between spacecraft at the scale these heavier, more complex landers require. Apollo's Lunar Module used hypergolic propellants instead. To date, SpaceX has managed one Starship test flight to orbit. Many more will undoubtedly follow, but if the launch figure cited by the panel is accurate, Musk's rocketeers face a challenging road ahead. Even with the rescoping that made Artemis III a low Earth orbit demonstration of lunar technologies from Blue Origin and SpaceX in 2027, the Artemis program remains ambitious, particularly considering the desire to get humans on the lunar surface before President Trump leaves office. ASAP praised Artemis II and NASA's new administrator, Jared Isaacman, but raised concerns about future access to low Earth orbit. SpaceX's plans to phase out Falcon rockets and Dragon spacecraft could complicate any extension of International Space Station (ISS) operations and the launch of its deorbit vehicle. Then there is Boeing's Calamity Capsule, Starliner. Last month, a possible uncrewed launch date around December 2026 was mooted , but the panel now puts the earliest possible launch in mid-January 2027, with the schedule still under review. An end to Dragon operations could leave Starliner as the only commercial option for getting astronauts to and from the ISS, not quite the redundancy NASA hoped for, and a stark reminder that commercial businesses aren't required to provide services indefinitely and can change direction when their contracts end. There is also only one US alternative to the cargo variant of Dragon: Northrop Grumman's Cygnus. An international cargo alternative is JAXA's HTV-X. Russia continues to carry crews on Soyuz spacecraft and cargo on Progress freighters, but NASA has long sought US alternatives. A written report is due early next year, doubtless with plenty of observations and recommendations. ®
