item.dc:creator: Carly Page
item.content:encoded: Britain is funding the next generation of tech companies without making sure taxpayers get a slice of the action, MPs have warned. In a new report shared with The Register ahead of publication, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has accused UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) of being overly cautious about protecting taxpayers' interests. Rather than simply handing out grants, MPs want UKRI to consider taking equity stakes in more of the businesses it backs, giving the public a chance to cash in when those companies succeed. According to the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), UK universities produce more spinouts and patents per pound of research funding than their US counterparts. But Britain is less adept at cashing in on its inventions. British startups still struggle to attract the investment needed to grow without moving overseas, while universities have a patchy record when it comes to exploiting their intellectual property. UKRI, meanwhile, has been reluctant to impose tougher conditions on the research it funds, arguing that doing so could discourage companies from growing. “This approach is far too cautious and we urge the Department to do much more to recover taxpayer's money when a successful company exploits research which the taxpayer, via UKRI, has paid for," the PAC said. It wants UKRI to review its standard funding terms, including whether it should take equity stakes in more companies benefiting from public money. Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair of the PAC, acknowledged that calling for the government to behave more like a venture capitalist might seem an odd position for a committee normally concerned with keeping public spending in check. "It may strike followers of this Committee's work that our call for government to take a less cautious approach to taking a direct stake in British innovation is an unusual one," he said. "But we are a body dedicated to value for taxpayers' money, not hoarding it. The nations currently leading the global tech race did not achieve their positions by avoiding more entrepreneurial policies. This is a simple case for the government of nothing ventured, nothing gained." The government has made some effort to help British tech firms. UKRI gives AI startups free access to taxpayer-funded supercomputers, while DSIT has changed its procurement rules to give UK companies a better shot at supplying £400 million worth of specialist AI chips. The British Business Bank is also investing alongside pension funds, giving taxpayers a stake in some of the businesses receiving support. But efforts to attract more pension fund investment have been slower than ministers hoped, and MPs want DSIT to start measuring whether its various support schemes are actually helping British companies grow, rather than simply counting how much money it hands out. There's also the question of where all that research funding ends up. London, the South East, and the East of England continue to receive half of UKRI's funding, despite years of government promises to spread investment more evenly across the country. The North's share has improved from 12 to 20 percent over the past five years, but UKRI has yet to set specific regional funding targets. Clifton-Brown described the divide as "continuing and unacceptable," warning that progress could easily be reversed without a more deliberate effort to spread the cash around. And while MPs want UKRI to be more adventurous with its investments, they're considerably less impressed with how it manages some of the projects already on its books. The committee pointed to an airborne laboratory upgrade that UKRI abandoned after spending £46 million of its £49 million budget. Funding was finally canceled five years after the decision to upgrade the aircraft, prompting MPs to question why the plug hadn't been pulled sooner. Elsewhere, around 45 percent of the Science and Technology Facilities Council's estate is in unacceptable condition, and restoring university-owned research infrastructure to full working order would cost an estimated £5.6 billion. The PAC also criticized UKRI for failing to ensure a replacement for the ARCHER2 national supercomputer would be ready before the existing machine shuts down, leaving an expected 13-month gap. It seems Whitehall has mastered the art of spending money on innovation, but getting any back is another matter. ®

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: From Sequins to Cow Print, See the Rave Glam Looks at the Tele x Zikora Premiere
item.description: Sophia Chisom, Mike Afolarin, and Genoveva Umeh interpreting the rave glam dress code for Tele x Zikora. A Nollywood premiere is always a good excuse to dress up, but when the dress code says “rave glam,” you know the red carpet is going to be anything but ordinary. That was the scene at the premiere of Tele x Zikora , where the cast and guests stepped out in bold colours, unexpected combinations and outfits that gave us plenty to look at. Written, produced and directed by Adenike Adebayo – Esho , Tele x Zikora is a campus romance set at the fictional Lagos Metropolitan University. The film follows two young people from very different worlds whose paths cross, setting the stage for a love story. Ahead of its cinema release on 23 October 2026, the cast and crew gathered to celebrate, with the evening’s rave glam theme giving everyone room to experiment with their style. Tele x Zikora writer, producer, and director Adenike Adebayo-Esho at the film premiere. Photo Credit: Adenike Adebayo-Esho/Instagram Sophia Chisom gave us a colour combination we wouldn’t have immediately put together, and somehow, it worked. She wore a royal blue longline coat over a matching top with a sharp white collar and cuffs, pairing both with a burnt-orange wrap mini skirt. An orange beret, star drop earrings and white knee-high boots completed her look. Mike Afolarin took a different route with a cow-print shearling jacket, a black top and dark grey flared jeans featuring silver side-buckle details. He finished with a dark cap, keeping things casual while still having a little fun with the dress code. Mike Afolarin at the Tele x Zikora premiere in a cow-print jacket and flare jeans. Photo Credit: Mike Afolarin/Instagram Then there was Genoveva Umeh in magenta and rose-pink sequins. Her dress featured structured shoulders and an asymmetrical skirt with long, shredded ribbons that moved as she walked. She paired it with deep pink tights and metallic heels, making a strong case for wearing pink from head to toe. And those were only a few of the looks from the night. See how the cast and guests dressed for the Tele x Zikora premiere: Genoveva Umeh at the Tele x Zikora premiere in a rose-pink sequined dress and tights. Photo Credit: Genoveva Umeh/Instagram Chimezie Imo at the Tele x Zikora premiere wearing a black tank top, fur coat, and futuristic sunglasses. Photo Credit: Chimezie Imo/Instagram Angel Unigwe attending the Tele x Zikora premiere in a gold metallic top and denim cargo trousers. Photo Credit: Angel Unigwe/Instagram Emeka Nwagbaraocha attending the Tele x Zikora movie premiere in a sleeveless pink shirt and wide-leg trousers. Photo Credit: Emeka Nwagbaraocha/Instagram Gbubemi Ejeye stepping out for the Tele x Zikora premiere in a metallic silver chain dress. Photo Credit: Gbubemi Ejeye/Instagram Eronini Osinachim in a silver metallic jacket and matching trousers for Tele x Zikora. Photo Credit: Eronini Osinachim/Instagram Tomi Ojo in a red leather jacket and pink

item.title: Meet Solange Omon, the 21-Year-Old Cameroonian Model Who Made Her Victoria’s Secret Runway Debut
item.description: Solange Omon walking the runway in illuminated wings and a sweeping metallic train at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram Did you see an African woman on the runway of the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show? She walked with such a composed, smooth step that you couldn’t help but notice her as she stepped out into the bright spotlights of Los Angeles. Her name is Solange Omon , a 21-year-old rising star who has officially earned her wings as the newest Victoria’s Secret Angel. She secured her place on the global stage after beating over 100,000 applicants in the brand’s open casting search, Angels Among Us. The competition, documented in a special YouTube series, crowned her as the winner, awarding her a one-year modelling contract with IMG Models alongside her runway debut. Solange Omon with fellow Angels Among Us top 3 finalists Andreína Martínez and Tatyana Tinsley. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram Born in Cameroon as the eldest of six children, Solange moved to the United States and has spent the last few years living in Lewiston, Maine. Before entering the national spotlight, her everyday life looked quite different. She spent her time balancing university coursework with her job as a programme coordinator for a local non-profit organisation focused on supporting young people. Her work centred on helping Black and immigrant teenagers apply for jobs, find professional mentors, and access higher education resources across her community. When she attended the open casting call in Chicago, she carried that grounded background straight onto the runway. For her big moment, she wore a contrast ivory and black lace lingerie set featuring a plunge bra paired with high-cut briefs, styled with oversized gold hoop drop earrings . The focus of her outfit was a pair of illuminated golden wings featuring embedded warm lights, paired with a sweeping bronze metallic train attached at the base of the wings . Solange Omon walking the runway in illuminated wings and a sweeping metallic train at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram As she walked down the glossy black runway, she held the edges of her metallic train, letting the lightweight fabric float behind her as she moved . Midway through her walk, she turned toward the cameras with a warm smile, twirled gracefully on the catwalk, and gestured to the audience before stepping back up the stage . Her milestone victory marks a significant moment for African representation in global fashion, showing how a young woman from Central Africa went from community work to one of the most recognised runways in the world. Solange Omon backstage at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show in Los Angeles after earning her Angel wings. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram The post Meet Solange Omon, the 21-Year-Old Cameroonian Model Who Made Her Victoria’s Secret Runway Debut appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!

item.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
item.description: null SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle. So this is, I think, a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization and consciousness." Artist's illustration of SpaceX catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket, something the company expects to do on the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall when fully stacked. As Musk noted, both of its stages — the Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft — are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX thinks will make Mars settlement and other grand exploration feats economically feasible. Starship's recovery strategy is different than that for SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, which are partially reusable. (The latter two rockets have expendable upper stages). Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy boosters come back to Earth on landing pads near the launch site or on ships at sea downrange. Super Heavy and Ship, however, will steer themselves directly back to their launch tower, which will capture each vehicle with its "chopstick" arms. This will allow SpaceX to inspect, refurbish and refly Starship at an accelerated rate, which is a priority for the company: Musk has said he envisions launching Starship more than 10,000 times per year by 2030. Starship has conducted 14 test flights to date, and SpaceX has pulled off chopstick catches with Super Heavy on three of them. The company has not yet tried to catch Ship, which is a more difficult proposition, as the upper stage travels higher, farther and faster than the booster does. Still, Musk is confident that SpaceX will pull off a Ship catch on the first try. (He did not give a specific target date for Flight 15, saying only that it was expected next month.) "I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," he said. "And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year, and and then accelerating next year." Success would mean back-to-back Starship flights with huge milestones. On Flight 14, which occurred on Sept. 28, Ship reached orbit for the first time ever . It also deployed 26 of SpaceX's Starlink Version 3 satellites — the first 26 members of a next-gen broadband constellation in low Earth orbit that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft . item.dc:creator: Mike Wall
item.content:encoded: null SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle. So this is, I think, a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization and consciousness." Artist's illustration of SpaceX catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket, something the company expects to do on the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall when fully stacked. As Musk noted, both of its stages — the Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft — are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX thinks will make Mars settlement and other grand exploration feats economically feasible. Starship's recovery strategy is different than that for SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, which are partially reusable. (The latter two rockets have expendable upper stages). Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy boosters come back to Earth on landing pads near the launch site or on ships at sea downrange. Super Heavy and Ship, however, will steer themselves directly back to their launch tower, which will capture each vehicle with its "chopstick" arms. This will allow SpaceX to inspect, refurbish and refly Starship at an accelerated rate, which is a priority for the company: Musk has said he envisions launching Starship more than 10,000 times per year by 2030. Starship has conducted 14 test flights to date, and SpaceX has pulled off chopstick catches with Super Heavy on three of them. The company has not yet tried to catch Ship, which is a more difficult proposition, as the upper stage travels higher, farther and faster than the booster does. Still, Musk is confident that SpaceX will pull off a Ship catch on the first try. (He did not give a specific target date for Flight 15, saying only that it was expected next month.) "I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," he said. "And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year, and and then accelerating next year." Success would mean back-to-back Starship flights with huge milestones. On Flight 14, which occurred on Sept. 28, Ship reached orbit for the first time ever . It also deployed 26 of SpaceX's Starlink Version 3 satellites — the first 26 members of a next-gen broadband constellation in low Earth orbit that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft . The Starship Flight 15 preview was something of an aside during today's call. The event primarily served to announce SpaceX's financial performance during Q3, the three-month stretch that ended on Sept. 30. And that performance was strong, company representatives said. SpaceX recorded revenues of $14.6 billion during Q3, an increase of 161% from the $5.6 billion earned during Q3 of 2025. The company had a net income of $4.4 billion during Q3, $5.5 billion better than the result from the same stretch last year, when SpaceX lost $1.1 billion. Just $1.8 billion of 2026 Q3 revenue came from SpaceX's launch division. The vast majority was generated by two other segments — connectivity (services provided by its Starlink megaconstellation) and artificial intelligence (or, as the Trump administration has recently rebranded it, "superintelligence"). SpaceX thinks these latter two segments will continue to boom. That's why it's building the infrastructure to support thousands of Starship launches per year — to loft lots of Starlink satellites and AI data centers to Earth orbit. And the company believes that it's positioned to really start raking in the cash, starting as soon as next year. "In a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of '27 is somewhere between 500 billion [dollars] and a trillion," Musk said.

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 20, 1970: The Soviet Union launches last-ever Zond moon mission
item.description: null On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. This was the last mission in the Zond program. After the first three Zond missions explored Venus and Mars , the next ones were circumlunar missions that flew around the moon before returning to Earth. Although there was no crew on board, the Zond spacecraft was designed with cosmonauts in mind. The Zond missions served as test flights for the Soviet Union's plans to send cosmonauts to the moon. But those plans for crewed flights never came to fruition. This was partly because the U.S. had already put astronauts on the moon , but also because the Zond missions had a lot of technical problems. Zond 8 was considered a success — even though its guidance system malfunctioned on the way back to Earth. The spacecraft still returned to Earth safely and splashed down in the Indian Ocean one week after it launched. The Soviet Union's Zond 8 spacecraft, the last in a series of lunar spacecraft, captured this image of Earthrise on Oct. 24, 1970. (Image credit: Moscow State University of Geodesy and Cartography) Why it mattered While the Zond 1 and Zond 2 missions were launched toward Venus and Mars, respectively, the primary target of most Zond missions was the moon. At the time, the Soviet Union was embroiled in an ongoing space race with the United States to be the first on the moon with a human crew. By the time Zond 8 launched on Oct. 20, 1970, that space race was lost to the Soviet Union. NASA and the U.S. had already landed astronauts on the moon twice with Apollo 11 and Apollo 12 (in July and November of 1969, respectively), and even peformed the first space rescue fo the Apollo 13 astronauts in April 1970. While Zond 8 was uncrewed, it was a test flight of the Soviet Union's L1 spacecraft that was designed to fly a cosmonaut around the moon. It looped around the moon in a lunar flyby, approaching within 1,120 kilometers of the moon's surface at its closest point, according to RussianSpaceWeb.com . An artist's illustration of a Zond spacecraft. (Image credit: Future) Cameras on Zond 8 captured stunning views of the Earth and moon, recreating the iconic Earthrise views seen by Apollo 8 astronauts two years earlier in 1968. Zond 8 ultimately splashed down in the Indian Ocean on Oct. 27, 1970 after a solar attitude sensor failed, sending it on a shorter, steeper reentry path during landing, according to RussianSpaceWeb.com. It was retrieved by a recovery ship, marking the end of the Soviet moon landing program. Russian would go on to develop a series of Salyut space stations , culminating in the long-lived Mir space station . After decades without a moon probe, Russia did launch a new uncrewed moon lander in 2023. That Luna 25 mission failed and crashed into the lunar surface after an onboard engine controller malfunctioned. The country has pledged a return to the moon in 2027. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive an

item.title: Can’t make it to the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art for the 'Star Wars' display? This is the companion book set you’re looking for!
item.description: null Taschen, purveyors of fine art and design special-edition books, have teamed up with George Lucas and his newly opened Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles to present a masterful two-volume catalog of the museum’s illuminating offerings. Housed in a sturdy slipcase, readers will discover a pair of lavishly illustrated volumes spanning 832 pages and tipping the scales at nearly 14 pounds. At $200 for the pair, it's not cheap, but look on the bright side; hoisting these illustrated tomes will save you a subscription to your local gym! This immersive collection documents in great detail the astounding scope of rare items on display in Lucas’s treasury of paintings, murals, photographs, sculptures, posters, comic strips, illustrations, costumes, and magazine covers that have spurred humankind’s imagination. Developed in collaboration with George Lucas and the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, this extensive two-volume catalog brings together an unparalleled collection of narrative art. View Deal We'd absolutely recommend checking out the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in person if you can. Our own Chelsea Gohd visited the Los Angeles-based museum ahead of its opening in September 2026 and adored it. But if you're not a California local, getting lost in this collection's glossy pages is the next best thing to roaming the museum exhibitions on a rainy afternoon. Volumes I and II of Tashen's stunning "Lucas Museum of Narrative Art" edition (Image credit: Taschen) Far beyond a mere companion to the marvels inside the fantastic spaceship-shaped building poised near the University of Southern California campus — the same institution where Lucas attended film school in the late 1960s — these bold editions are an adventure in their own right. Waiting to be absorbed is an impressive assortment of storytelling expression that showcases beautiful works by everyone from Maxfield Parrish, N.C. Wyeth, and Norman Rockwell to Frank Frazetta, Jack Kirby, and Ralph McQuarrie. Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, curated the museum’s contents that represent decades of collecting narrative art in all of its forms. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) Our friends at Taschen were gracious enough to send us one of these Lucas Museum of Narrative Art special editions, and in unboxing this magnificent pair of books, one can feel the quality in the deluxe binding and thick covers. Inside you’ll find an eye-popping array of full-color photography and sharp descriptions for hundreds of artworks, all hand-picked by Lucas and Hobson. Lucas himself delivers the preface, which is titled "The Art of Story," where he professes his love of art, myth, anthropology, illustrators, and cinema. He recalls when he came to meet his mentor, Professor Joseph Campbell, and how he amassed 40,000 pieces of art beginning when he was a student at USC. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) The great di

Wyeth, and Norman Rockwell to Frank Frazetta, Jack Kirby, and Ralph McQuarrie. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) Our friends at Taschen were gracious enough to send us one of these Lucas Museum of Narrative Art special editions, and in unboxing this magnificent pair of books, one can feel the quality in the deluxe binding and thick covers. He recalls when he came to meet his mentor, Professor Joseph Campbell, and how he amassed 40,000 pieces of art beginning when he was a student at USC. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) The great director Guillermo del Toro provides a heartfelt foreword praising the importance of the museum and these prestigious companion volumes depicting a multitude of visual wonders. Between the duo of volumes, sections are divided into chapters dealing with topics such as history, children's stories, the American West, everyday life, romance and adventure, photography, science fiction and fantasy, and, of course, Star Wars in Motion. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) They take you on an overwhelming journey through the gallery’s incredibly diverse holdings, not least of which are archival items and concept art chronicling Lucas's involvement in the galaxy far, far away. This remarkable " Star Wars " section will be of particular interest to sci-fi aficionados, as it contains 100 pages of original props, paintings, concept artwork, costumes, models, and digital renderings created by some of Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic’s best and brightest talents. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) Taken with the rest of the 832 combined pages of Taschen's ambitious release that fully captures the dizzying breadth of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art , it's a brilliant keepsake to spark your soul and imagination. The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art two-book collection is available now via Taschen's website and Amazon . Developed in collaboration with George Lucas and the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, this extensive two-volume catalog brings together an unparalleled collection of narrative art. View Deal

item.title: Nigeria Confirms First Ebola Case in Abuja
item.description: Following the Federal Government’s confirmation of an Ebola case in the FCT, health authorities have activated nationwide surveillance and urged the public to remain calm while strictly following official safety guidelines. The Federal Government of Nigeria has confirmed a case of the Ebola virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja . According to an official press statement issued on October 20, 2026, and signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate , the patient is a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda . She was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before laboratory confirmation established the diagnosis . She has since been moved to an isolation facility, where she is currently receiving medical care . In response to the development, the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), and the FCT Health Services Secretariat have mobilised a swift public health response to contain the spread . Contact tracing is already underway, with 44 close contacts—spanning healthcare workers, caregivers, patients, and travel companions—identified and placed under monitoring . Public health teams have also stepped up surveillance and are providing direct support to the hospital to reinforce infection prevention and control standards . Authorities have put all public and private healthcare facilities nationwide on high alert, urging medical personnel to maintain a high index of suspicion, isolate suspected cases promptly, and report them to health authorities immediately . Reassuring the public, the government noted that Nigeria successfully contained an Ebola outbreak back in 2014, building a robust public health framework and experienced response system . However, officials emphasised that safeguarding public health requires a collective effort . What Nigerians Should Know and Do Public health authorities have outlined essential guidelines to keep everyone safe while urging citizens to remain calm and avoid panic : How It Spreads: Ebola is transmitted through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is exhibiting symptoms or has died from the disease, as well as through contact with contaminated materials . Individuals cannot transmit the virus before symptoms manifest . Stay Calm and Vigilant: Remain composed and rely strictly on verified updates from official health bodies to curb misinformation and stigma . item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: Following the Federal Government’s confirmation of an Ebola case in the FCT, health authorities have activated nationwide surveillance and urged the public to remain calm while strictly following official safety guidelines. The Federal Government of Nigeria has confirmed a case of the Ebola virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja . According to an official press statement issued on October 20, 2026, and signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate , the patient is a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda . She was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before laboratory confirmation established the diagnosis . She has since been moved to an isolation facility, where she is currently receiving medical care . In response to the development, the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), and the FCT Health Services Secretariat have mobilised a swift public health response to contain the spread . Contact tracing is already underway, with 44 close contacts—spanning healthcare workers, caregivers, patients, and travel companions—identified and placed under monitoring . Public health teams have also stepped up surveillance and are providing direct support to the hospital to reinforce infection prevention and control standards . Authorities have put all public and private healthcare facilities nationwide on high alert, urging medical personnel to maintain a high index of suspicion, isolate suspected cases promptly, and report them to health authorities immediately . Reassuring the public, the government noted that Nigeria successfully contained an Ebola outbreak back in 2014, building a robust public health framework and experienced response system . However, officials emphasised that safeguarding public health requires a collective effort . What Nigerians Should Know and Do Public health authorities have outlined essential guidelines to keep everyone safe while urging citizens to remain calm and avoid panic : How It Spreads: Ebola is transmitted through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is exhibiting symptoms or has died from the disease, as well as through contact with contaminated materials . Individuals cannot transmit the virus before symptoms manifest . Stay Calm and Vigilant: Remain composed and rely strictly on verified updates from official health bodies to curb misinformation and stigma . Practice Good Hygiene: Maintain regular hand hygiene and strictly avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone suspected of carrying the virus . Watch for Symptoms: Look out for warning signs such as sudden fever, severe weakness, headaches, vomiting, and diarrhoea, particularly if there is a history of potential exposure . Report Immediately: If you suspect exposure, even if you feel completely well, isolate yourself from close contact and contact public health authorities for guidance prior to visiting any clinic or hospital . Cooperate with Contact Tracing: Anyone reached by public health officials, including fellow airline passengers, must provide accurate information and follow professional guidance . For inquiries, updates, or to report a suspected case, the NCDC toll-free call centre is open 24/7 at 6232 *** Featured image generated by AI The post Nigeria Confirms First Ebola Case in Abuja appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Jeff Bezos is playing the long game with Blue Origin (op-ed)
item.description:
Daniel Biedermann is a Partner at NewSpace Capital, a private equity firm investing in high-growth space companies. He has more than 30 years' experience in the space industry and was previously SVP of Corporate Strategy at SES, where he played a leading role in acquisitions and the creation of joint ventures, including LuxGovSat. Before joining SES, he held engineering and mission management roles at Arianespace and Contraves Space, working on more than 40 space and launch missions.

Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . Jeff Bezos , the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin , his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets , spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen. He may be right to keep his options open. Bezos founded Blue Origin in 2000. Because he has financed so much of its development by himself , the company has been able to pursue ambitious engineering projects without the financial pressures that publicly listed businesses typically face. But developing reusable rockets, manufacturing spacecraft and building the infrastructure needed for future lunar missions requires extraordinary amounts of capital: These projects can take decades to complete, and even the wealthiest investors must think hard about how best to finance them over the long term. Bezos, then, has good reasons to seek additional sources of investment — particularly as Blue Origin prepares to expand its commercial operations. An IPO would give Blue Origin the means to raise substantial capital from public investors and reduce its dependence on Bezos's personal wealth. The company could then use that money to expand manufacturing, develop new technology and compete for a greater share of the growing space market. Public ownership would also give existing investors the power to sell some of their holdings and could make it easier for Blue Origin to finance acquisitions. But the company would also have to meet the expectations of shareholders, who would expect to see regular evidence of commercial progress. item.content:encoded:
Daniel Biedermann is a Partner at NewSpace Capital, a private equity firm investing in high-growth space companies. He has more than 30 years' experience in the space industry and was previously SVP of Corporate Strategy at SES, where he played a leading role in acquisitions and the creation of joint ventures, including LuxGovSat. Before joining SES, he held engineering and mission management roles at Arianespace and Contraves Space, working on more than 40 space and launch missions.

Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . Jeff Bezos , the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin , his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets , spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen. He may be right to keep his options open. Bezos founded Blue Origin in 2000. Because he has financed so much of its development by himself , the company has been able to pursue ambitious engineering projects without the financial pressures that publicly listed businesses typically face. But developing reusable rockets, manufacturing spacecraft and building the infrastructure needed for future lunar missions requires extraordinary amounts of capital: These projects can take decades to complete, and even the wealthiest investors must think hard about how best to finance them over the long term. Bezos, then, has good reasons to seek additional sources of investment — particularly as Blue Origin prepares to expand its commercial operations. An IPO would give Blue Origin the means to raise substantial capital from public investors and reduce its dependence on Bezos's personal wealth. The company could then use that money to expand manufacturing, develop new technology and compete for a greater share of the growing space market. Public ownership would also give existing investors the power to sell some of their holdings and could make it easier for Blue Origin to finance acquisitions. But the company would also have to meet the expectations of shareholders, who would expect to see regular evidence of commercial progress. This, I suspect, is why Bezos wants to establish a stronger business before committing to a listing. It might have much to prove commercially, but Blue Origin’s technical progress has been remarkable. In January 2025, its New Glenn rocket reached orbit for the first time — a significant achievement for a vehicle built to compete in the heavy-lift launch market. The company has also secured government and commercial contracts and continued developing its lunar capabilities. But it will eventually have to demonstrate that it can launch New Glenn frequently, reliably and at a commercially competitive cost, and it is still some way away from that point. Some will be asking whether Bezos wants to raise money to accelerate growth or simply to reduce the amount he himself must invest. Such doubts could affect the company's valuation and make it harder to attract investors who share its long-term ambitions. But again, this suggests Bezos is playing the long game. And given the enthusiasm that has surrounded some billionaire-led space ventures, this is sensible. Investors have sometimes attached extraordinary valuations to companies with ambitious plans but limited commercial experience. Space businesses certainly require ambition: engineers will often spend years developing technology before they can sell it. But investors have to distinguish between technical achievement and commercial performance. At the end of the day, they are seeking a strong rate of return. Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket launches NASA's ESCAPADE Mars mission on Nov. 13, 2025. (Image credit: Blue Origin) What’s also worth considering is how Blue Origin's progress could benefit the wider space industry, particularly the specialist companies that supply technology to larger manufacturers and operators. SpaceX has achieved remarkable success in part by developing and manufacturing much of its technology internally. This includes its rockets, spacecraft and satellites . Blue Origin also does something similar, undertaking substantial engineering and manufacturing work itself, but it is not quite so vertically integrated, and thus may have greater scope to work with external suppliers as it expands. It already buys parts, equipment and services from hundreds of businesses. If it can successfully increase its production and launch activity, these suppliers could receive more orders and gain opportunities to develop new technologies. That’s to the good of the sector as a whole. Why? Because a successful space industry needs more than a handful of large launch providers. It needs companies specializing in satellite communications, propulsion, electronics, software and other areas. Such businesses may have developed highly sophisticated products, but they need bigger customers and predictable demand to expand and produce more. Blue Origin could become an important customer for some of these, particularly if it chooses to buy specialist technology rather than make everything internally. Greater competition between the bigger space companies could translate to more potential customers for suppliers and fewer dependent commercial relationships. Investors would benefit. There’s real potential in businesses that provide the technology and services on which larger space companies depend — the ‘picks and shovels.’ These can sometimes serve several customers and markets, making them less dependent on the success of a single program. A growing Blue Origin would create more opportunities for companies like these — although, of course, much will depend on how Bezos chooses to organize its supply chain. We shouldn’t assume that Blue Origin will become more open to external suppliers than its competitors, but the possibility is at least worth entertaining. As it is, Bezos still faces substantial challenges. Blue Origin is not yet a commercially mature business. The company must increase its launch activity; it must demonstrate its reliability; and it must compete for customers in the public and private sectors. It must also decide how much technology to manufacture internally and whether and where third parties can provide better products or products at a lower cost. Bezos has the resources to give the company time to answer these questions, and he appears to be willing to use them. If he continues to prioritize commercial performance before pursuing an IPO, then Blue Origin could eventually enter the public markets in a much stronger position.

item.title: Folorunso Alakija Receives Honorary Doctorate From UK’s University of Buckingham
item.description: Folorunso Alakija with Vice-Chancellor Professor David Cole at the University of Buckingham. From fashion and banking to oil and gas, Nigerian businesswoman and philanthropist Folorunso Alakija has built a career across several industries. Now, the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom has recognised her achievements with an honorary doctorate, celebrating her contributions to business, philanthropy and society. The honour was conferred on Friday, 16 October 2026, at the university’s Radcliffe Centre during Buckingham Africa Day, as the institution marked its 50th anniversary. Dressed in a red doctoral gown, Alakija received the degree from Vice-Chancellor Professor David Cole , with family, friends and members of the university community in attendance. For Alakija, the occasion was also an opportunity to speak to the next generation about ambition, responsibility and the importance of creating opportunities for others. Folorunso Alakija in her doctoral gown at the University of Buckingham conferment ceremony. Accepting the honorary degree, she thanked God and the university for the recognition, sharing her belief in Africa’s potential and the responsibility that comes with achievement. “Africa is a continent of immense potential, creativity and resilience and that achievement carries responsibility to serve others,” she said. She also encouraged students and young people to pursue their goals with passion, perseverance and diligence, while remaining humble and recognising the value of their contributions. Her message reflects a career that has taken her through several fields. Before becoming widely known for her work in oil and gas through Famfa Oil, Alakija worked in banking and established herself in Nigeria’s fashion industry. She has also been involved in real estate, printing and philanthropic initiatives supporting education, women and vulnerable communities. Folorunso Alakija with Dean of Faculty Professor Debarpita Bardhan-Correia at the Radcliffe Centre. During the ceremony, Professor Debarpita Bardhan – Correia , Dean of the Faculty of Business, Humanities and Social Sciences, spoke about Alakija’s commitment to opening doors for others. Professor Shalom Lloyd MBE also highlighted the importance of investing in young Africans, asking, “What better investment can we make than developing Africa’s future leaders?” After the conferment, Alakija spent time with students and guests at a reception hosted in her honour, offering advice and encouragement. Her son, Dele Alakija , and sister, Arinola Ogbara , were among the family members who joined her for the celebration, alongside friends and other guests who travelled from Nigeria. The honorary doctorate adds another chapter to Alakija’s journey, one that began long before her success in the oil industry. And as she celebrated the recognition in Buckingham, her message to young people was clear: pursue your ambitions, remain committed to your work and use what you achieve to create

item.title: A supercomputer is about to launch to the moon aboard a rover named FLIP
item.description: null HAWTHORNE, Calif. — A moon buggy carrying a history-making supercomputer is ready to launch to the lunar surface. And it's taking some inspiration from Mars. Later this year, Astrolab will launch its uncrewed moon rover FLIP to the lunar south pole as part of the Griffin Mission 1, or Griffin-1. The California company is one of two that NASA has selected to develop a drivable rover for the agency's Artemis program. On board FLIP will be Hewlett Packard Enterprise's (HPE) Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced computer module built to be used in space. This will be the first time that high-performance computing and artificial intelligence will be tested on the lunar surface. As NASA gets closer to landing humans back on the moon with Artemis, advancements like this aim to support future human habitation as well as economic activity on and around the moon. "We're sending the first supercomputer from HPE to the lunar surface later this year, doing the first GPU [graphics processing unit] on the moon [and the] first AI experiments on the moon," Jaret Matthews, founder and CEO of Astrolab, said during an Oct. 14 media event here at Astrolab's headquarters. "They're breaking new ground, and they're ahead of the curve." The computer is designed to be lightweight, compact, self-contained and fanless. It has a low-power 64-bit CPU (central processing unit) with a GPU. The computer will be attached to FLIP's cooling system and will be powered by a system supported by both batteries and solar cells on the rover. The computer will also be paired with solid state drives from the company KIOXIA that will allow for memory storage. Mission Control at Astrolab. Chelsea Gohd Astrolab CEO and founder Jaret Matthews points out the Astrolab landing site among other locations at the lunar south pole. Chelsea Gohd Jaret Matthews presents Astrolab's FLIP rover. Chelsea Gohd The FLIP rover's headlights and attached artwork. Chelsea Gohd A close-up of the attached artwork on the FLIP rover. Chelsea Gohd So, what will a supercomputer and AI accomplish on this uncrewed mission? First and foremost, the flightwill test how the computer works in this extreme environment. The computer is built with heat-conductive aluminum and is designed with the specific conditions of the lunar south pole in mind. But while it was designed and tested to be able to withstand the extreme temperatures and conditions on the moon's surface, the upcoming mission seeks to show that this advanced technology can actually work in this environment. "NASA's given us a real challenge," Matthews told Space.com at the media event. "We have to design for a full year on the lunar surface. So that means surviving multiple lunar nights, upwards of 150 hours of complete darkness where we're not receiving energy or warmth from the sun. And then, also, there's going to be a long period [in] which we're operating semi-autonomously for [when] the astronauts are not there … and so we're having to develop a semi-auto
item.dc:creator: Chelsea Gohd
item.content:encoded: null HAWTHORNE, Calif. — A moon buggy carrying a history-making supercomputer is ready to launch to the lunar surface. And it's taking some inspiration from Mars. Later this year, Astrolab will launch its uncrewed moon rover FLIP to the lunar south pole as part of the Griffin Mission 1, or Griffin-1. The California company is one of two that NASA has selected to develop a drivable rover for the agency's Artemis program. On board FLIP will be Hewlett Packard Enterprise's (HPE) Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced computer module built to be used in space. This will be the first time that high-performance computing and artificial intelligence will be tested on the lunar surface. As NASA gets closer to landing humans back on the moon with Artemis, advancements like this aim to support future human habitation as well as economic activity on and around the moon. "We're sending the first supercomputer from HPE to the lunar surface later this year, doing the first GPU [graphics processing unit] on the moon [and the] first AI experiments on the moon," Jaret Matthews, founder and CEO of Astrolab, said during an Oct. 14 media event here at Astrolab's headquarters. "They're breaking new ground, and they're ahead of the curve." The computer is designed to be lightweight, compact, self-contained and fanless. It has a low-power 64-bit CPU (central processing unit) with a GPU. The computer will be attached to FLIP's cooling system and will be powered by a system supported by both batteries and solar cells on the rover. The computer will also be paired with solid state drives from the company KIOXIA that will allow for memory storage. Mission Control at Astrolab. Chelsea Gohd Astrolab CEO and founder Jaret Matthews points out the Astrolab landing site among other locations at the lunar south pole. Chelsea Gohd Jaret Matthews presents Astrolab's FLIP rover. Chelsea Gohd The FLIP rover's headlights and attached artwork. Chelsea Gohd A close-up of the attached artwork on the FLIP rover. Chelsea Gohd So, what will a supercomputer and AI accomplish on this uncrewed mission? First and foremost, the flightwill test how the computer works in this extreme environment. The computer is built with heat-conductive aluminum and is designed with the specific conditions of the lunar south pole in mind. But while it was designed and tested to be able to withstand the extreme temperatures and conditions on the moon's surface, the upcoming mission seeks to show that this advanced technology can actually work in this environment. "NASA's given us a real challenge," Matthews told Space.com at the media event. "We have to design for a full year on the lunar surface. So that means surviving multiple lunar nights, upwards of 150 hours of complete darkness where we're not receiving energy or warmth from the sun. And then, also, there's going to be a long period [in] which we're operating semi-autonomously for [when] the astronauts are not there … and so we're having to develop a semi-autonomous platform that will spend many months [and] travel hundreds of kilometers [on the moon]." But the computer will more than just prove its durability, if all goes to plan. It will also analyze visual data captured on the mission and enable autonomous observations, process navigation, mapping and terrain analysis. The mission also promises to test AI capabilities, though it's unclear what exact applications we'll see with this lunar AI. HPE shared in a statement that "an AI services container will demonstrate reliable deployment of scalable AI service applications on the moon." It is also to be determined exactly how, once tested, these capabilities might be used with future crewed missions. Astronauts aboard the International Space Station already use computers for communications, science experiments and other daily tasks while living in space, but we can't say yet exactly how future astronauts might use these capabilities, especially with the addition of AI, on the moon. From Mars to the moon One interesting aspect of this new development is where it came from. While HPE has provided computing power to NASA for decades, Matthews is also bringing his previous experience working at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) into this new venture. "One of the experiments [that will be] running on the spaceborne computer on the moon is a localization software experiment from JPL. It has been used on Mars, and this will be the first time it's used on the moon," Matthews said. "The challenge with the moon and Mars is that there's no GPS, so locating yourself and knowing where you are on the surface [can be difficult]," he added. "So we're going to be running what is essentially a machine learning algorithm that JPL developed to take a map that's stored in memory … and compare it to the local terrain we see around us, and then do a match. So essentially, match features of the local terrain to the map that's stored in memory to help find ourselves on the map and keep ourselves away from dangerous craters." As its name suggests, Griffin-1 will be the first mission for the robotic Griffin moon lander, which was developed by Astrobotic. The Pittsburgh company is flying Griffin-1 for NASA, under the agency's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) program. In addition to FLIP, the mission will carry Astrobiotic's CubeRover, a small, uncrewed rover; LandCam-X, an optical navigation system; and Nanofiche GLPH (Galactic Library to Preserve Humanity), a tiny archive of human history, to the moon's surface. "The moon presents a challenging environment for advanced computing, and we’re pleased to provide HPE with an opportunity to demonstrate its technology on the lunar surface," Matthews added in a statement. "Our FLIP rover is designed to accommodate a variety of payloads, and this mission will demonstrate how commercial lunar mobility platforms can support technology development and scientific research."

item.title: Talks Around Contour: Have You Met the New ZARON Contour Stick Yet?
item.description: Okay ladies, gather around because there is something to talk about! You know that moment when your makeup is looking good, but you just want a little extra definition? A little cheekbone action? A little sculpted-but-still-natural magic? You get the gist! Well, ZARON Cosmetics might just have something for you: the new ZARON Contour Stick ! And before you ask, we are talking about the kind of product that lets you decide how snatched you want your look to be. Soft glam today? Full glam tomorrow? The choice is yours! First Things First, Why a Contour Stick? Let’s be honest. Contouring can sometimes feel like a whole mathematics exam. Where exactly do you apply it? How much is too much? And why does blending sometimes feel like a workout? The struggle is real! That’s why a contour product that makes the process feel easier deserves a little attention. The ZARON Contour Stick is designed to sculpt, define, and enhance your features without making your makeup routine unnecessarily complicated. Think of it as another tool in your beauty bag for creating the look you want, whether you’re getting ready for a casual outing, a date night, or that event where you need your pictures to come out looking extra good. Wait, There’s More! Let’s Talk About the Formula Now, here’s where things get interesting. The ZARON Contour Stick is creamy, blendable, and buildable. Three words every contour lover wants to hear! Creamy? Everyone loves a product that glides onto the skin. Blendable? Because nobody is trying to walk around with harsh contour lines announcing themselves before we do! The formula is designed to blend seamlessly for a natural-looking finish without that cakey feel. Buildable? Now we’re talking! Some days, you want just a little definition. Other days, you’re going all out with the sculpted glam. This contour stick lets you build your desired level of definition with every swipe. In other words, you don’t have to commit to one look. Start soft, blend it out, and build up if you want more drama. Your face, your rules! Fall, Spring or Autumn? Pick Your Shade! You know what can make or break your contour look? Finding a shade that works for your complexion and the kind of definition you’re going for. The ZARON Contour Stick comes in three shades: Fall, Spring and Autumn. Whether you’re keeping things subtle or going for a more defined finish, these options give you room to explore your preferred contour look. And please, don’t be afraid to experiment! Makeup is supposed to be fun. Try your shade, blend it out, see how it works with your foundation, and find the finish that makes you feel your best. There’s a Little Story Behind This Launch! Here’s a detail we love: the ZARON Contour Stick was inspired by feedback from the brand’s beauty community, affectionately known as Zaronistas. Yes, the people have been talking, and this launch reflects the brand’s response to what its customers want from their beauty essentials. We love seeing beauty conversatio

The formula is designed to blend seamlessly for a natural-looking finish without that cakey feel. Buildable? Now we’re talking! Some days, you want just a little definition. Other days, you’re going all out with the sculpted glam. This contour stick lets you build your desired level of definition with every swipe. In other words, you don’t have to commit to one look. Start soft, blend it out, and build up if you want more drama. Your face, your rules! Fall, Spring or Autumn? Pick Your Shade! You know what can make or break your contour look? Finding a shade that works for your complexion and the kind of definition you’re going for. The ZARON Contour Stick comes in three shades: Fall, Spring and Autumn. Whether you’re keeping things subtle or going for a more defined finish, these options give you room to explore your preferred contour look. And please, don’t be afraid to experiment! Makeup is supposed to be fun. Try your shade, blend it out, see how it works with your foundation, and find the finish that makes you feel your best. There’s a Little Story Behind This Launch! Here’s a detail we love: the ZARON Contour Stick was inspired by feedback from the brand’s beauty community, affectionately known as Zaronistas. Yes, the people have been talking, and this launch reflects the brand’s response to what its customers want from their beauty essentials. We love seeing beauty conversations inspire new additions to a makeup collection! Because really, makeup isn’t just about following trends. It’s about finding products that fit into your routine, complement your style, and let you express yourself. So, Girl, Is It Time to Add This to Your Makeup Bag? If you’ve been looking for a contour product that offers a creamy texture, seamless blending, and buildable definition, the ZARON Contour Stick is one to check out. The ZARON Contour Stick is now available online and at ZARON outlets. You can shop yours at www.zaroncosmetics.com or head to your nearest ZARON outlet. Your contour era starts now. item.title: BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey Launches in Nigeria With “Party Like It’s ’98” Lagos Experience
item.description: What happens when Irish whiskey meets ’90s nostalgia, Lagos nightlife and a room full of people ready to have a good time? For BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey , the answer was “Party Like It’s ’98” , an immersive experience that marked the brand’s formal Nigerian launch at Nomaada Restaurant in Victoria Island, Lagos. Bringing together celebrities, media personalities, distributors, tastemakers and industry stakeholders, the evening moved beyond the conventional whiskey launch format, creating an experience built around music, food, cocktails, fashion, storytelling and, naturally, whiskey. But there was something particularly interesting about the choice of theme. The ’80s, ’90s and early-2000s-inspired direction was not created as a reaction to the current nostalgia wave dominating social media and popular culture. The consumer strategy had been developed and concluded months before the event. By the time BOLD ’98 brought the concept to life in Lagos, retro culture had become increasingly visible everywhere, making the brand’s choice of direction feel almost like a glimpse into the future. L-R Kelvin Orogun, Board Chairman, Jambitts Limited; Ita Ntekim, CEO, Miami Escape; Olajumoke Oladimeji, CEO, Capston Bee; Motunrayo Raheem, Executive Director, Commercial Operations, Stafford Irish Spirits/Jambitts Limited; Kelechi Obichendu, CEO, Simple Life; and Chris Obihai, Board Chairman, Jambitts Limited. When Strategy Meets Culture For BOLD ’98, nostalgia was never simply about dressing up a premium Irish whiskey launch in old-school aesthetics. The thinking was to create an experience that would make the brand’s heritage feel relevant, familiar and culturally engaging to Nigerian consumers. “Our theme for BOLD ’98 was going to be old school, the ’90s, the ritual vibes, everything that makes you remember where you’re coming from,” said Motunrayo Raheem, Executive Director, Commercial Operations, Stafford Irish Spirits/Jambitts. item.content:encoded: What happens when Irish whiskey meets ’90s nostalgia, Lagos nightlife and a room full of people ready to have a good time? For BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey , the answer was “Party Like It’s ’98” , an immersive experience that marked the brand’s formal Nigerian launch at Nomaada Restaurant in Victoria Island, Lagos. Bringing together celebrities, media personalities, distributors, tastemakers and industry stakeholders, the evening moved beyond the conventional whiskey launch format, creating an experience built around music, food, cocktails, fashion, storytelling and, naturally, whiskey. But there was something particularly interesting about the choice of theme. The ’80s, ’90s and early-2000s-inspired direction was not created as a reaction to the current nostalgia wave dominating social media and popular culture. The consumer strategy had been developed and concluded months before the event. By the time BOLD ’98 brought the concept to life in Lagos, retro culture had become increasingly visible everywhere, making the brand’s choice of direction feel almost like a glimpse into the future. L-R Kelvin Orogun, Board Chairman, Jambitts Limited; Ita Ntekim, CEO, Miami Escape; Olajumoke Oladimeji, CEO, Capston Bee; Motunrayo Raheem, Executive Director, Commercial Operations, Stafford Irish Spirits/Jambitts Limited; Kelechi Obichendu, CEO, Simple Life; and Chris Obihai, Board Chairman, Jambitts Limited. When Strategy Meets Culture For BOLD ’98, nostalgia was never simply about dressing up a premium Irish whiskey launch in old-school aesthetics. The thinking was to create an experience that would make the brand’s heritage feel relevant, familiar and culturally engaging to Nigerian consumers. “Our theme for BOLD ’98 was going to be old school, the ’90s, the ritual vibes, everything that makes you remember where you’re coming from,” said Motunrayo Raheem, Executive Director, Commercial Operations, Stafford Irish Spirits/Jambitts. The result was a Lagos whiskey experience that invited people to participate rather than simply watch. Guests captured their own Polaroid ‘’98 moments’, explored a Cocktail Lab, enjoyed food and whiskey pairings, and experienced a chef’s table curated by Nomaada. There was also a fireside conversation hosted by Zion Rufus , a staged bottle reveal, a catwalk featuring retro-inspired props, live performances and a spirited Gen-Z versus Millennial rap and dance battle. It was nostalgic, but it was also distinctly Lagos. A Whiskey With a Story Behind the party is a whiskey whose story stretches much further back than the 1990s. BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey draws inspiration from the 1798 uprising in Ireland and the story of the pikemen of Wexford, whose fight for liberty became part of the brand’s heritage narrative. The story includes the image of barley from the rebels’ pockets sprouting on the battlefield after the fighting at Vinegar Hill, a powerful symbol of hope emerging from loss. That heritage is reflected in BOLD ’98’s philosophy: “ Rooted in Courage .” It is a story that connects Ireland’s history with a broader idea of resilience, determination, and the belief that something meaningful can emerge from adversity. For Raheem, that connection resonates strongly with Nigeria. “BOLD ’98 is rooted in bold characters and in the belief that something good can come from defiance. Nigerians will recognize that spirit, because it’s how many of us have built our own lives and businesses.” The result is an Irish whiskey brand whose story travels beyond its origins in Ireland to connect with a new generation of Nigerian consumers. Experience Before Explanation The Lagos launch was also a reflection of how BOLD ’98 intends to introduce itself to the Nigerian market. Rather than relying solely on a product presentation, the brand allowed guests to encounter the whiskey organically throughout the evening. As Raheem explained: “A whiskey is best introduced by tasting it, in good company, and not by telling people about it. We wanted the trade and consumers to feel the brand before they hear our pitch.” BOLD ’98 is a premium blended Irish whiskey with roots in County Wexford, Ireland, made from a blend of grain, pot still and malt whiskeys. The whiskey is characterized by a creamy, smooth profile with notes of caramel and toasted oak, and can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks or as part of a cocktail. At the Lagos launch, that versatility came to life through cocktails, food pairings and shared drinking occasions designed to introduce guests to the character of the whiskey rather than simply tell them about it. Why Nigeria? BOLD ’98 enters a Nigerian premium spirits market where consumers are increasingly exposed to international whiskey brands and have developed more discerning expectations around what they drink. For a new Irish whiskey in Nigeria, simply being an imported spirit is not enough. Consumers want quality, character, provenance and a story they can connect with. “Nigeria is one of the most exciting consumer markets in the world, and Nigerians have a discerning palate,” Raheem said. “They do not just want a famous name; they want quality, character and a brand with something to say.” That thinking shaped the Nigerian launch. The strategy was to create something consumers could taste, photograph, talk about, share and remember. And with Nigeria’s growing premium drinking culture, Lagos provided a natural setting for a brand that wants to sit at the intersection of Irish whiskey heritage and contemporary Nigerian culture. From 1798 to ’98 There was a fitting connection between the brand’s Irish heritage and its Nigerian launch. A whiskey inspired by a story from 1798 arrived in Lagos through a celebration centred on ’98, creating a bridge between historical heritage and contemporary culture. “Party Like It’s ’98” was ultimately more than a launch party. It was BOLD ’98’s first major statement about how it intends to show up in Nigeria: rooted in heritage, but expressed through contemporary culture, music, food, fashion and shared experiences. For Raheem, however, the ambition extends well beyond the launch night. “ Our promise with BOLD ’98 is simple. As a whiskey brand with a real Irish story, made with care and meant to be shared, we came to Nigeria to stay, and we are only getting started.” Where to Buy BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey in Nigeria BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey is available through selected retail stores, liquor outlets and HORECA locations across Nigeria. Consumers can also order BOLD ’98 online through participating Nigerian e-commerce and drinks platforms, including Drinks.ng . Order BOLD ’98 online: BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey With its combination of Irish heritage, a distinctive brand story and a contemporary approach to whiskey culture, BOLD ’98 is positioning itself as more than another premium Irish whiskey in Nigeria . It has arrived with a story to tell, a culture to participate in, and an experience to build. BOLD ’98 Irish Whiskey has arrived in Nigeria, and the party is just beginning. item.title: BEYOND on Tour V: Redefining Rest, Recovery and the Future of African Wellness
item.description: From its signature Sunset Ride at Lakowe Lakes to personalised recovery experiences and dermatological skincare innovation, BEYOND Fitness Africa is creating a new expression of wellness rooted in movement, culture and community. African wellness is evolving, and BEYOND Fitness Africa is helping shape what comes next. From 30 October to 1 November 2026, BEYOND Fitness Africa returns to Lakowe Lakes Golf and Country Resort for the fifth edition of BEYOUND on Tour , its signature destination wellness retreat. Built around the theme Rest, Reset and Recover , the three-day experience invites guests to step away from everyday demands and reconnect with their wellbeing through movement, personalised recovery, nourishing food, meaningful connections and genuine rest. This year’s edition features an expanded partnership with La Roche-Posay, the Official Dermatological Skincare Partner, connecting the retreat’s approach to wellbeing with expert skincare education and the brand’s upcoming Living Lab experience in Lagos. From Lagos to a Broader African Wellness Vision Founded in 2021, BEYOND Fitness Africa has spent five years building a premium community around high-performance group fitness, recovery and human connection. What began as a boutique fitness studio in Victoria Island has evolved into a wellness business spanning corporate wellness, destination retreats and brand collaborations, with ambitions to expand beyond Lagos into other Nigerian and African markets. BEYOND on Tour has become an important expression of that vision. Its fourth edition captured widespread attention when guests cycled beside the lake at sunset while Loud Urban Choir performed live, creating an unforgettable fusion of movement, music and nature. The fifth edition builds on that momentum, offering a more expansive recovery programme and greater freedom for guests to experience the weekend on their own terms. Simisola Williams, Founder and Managing Director of BEYOND Fitness Africa, explains: “When I founded BEYOND, I wanted to create a space where people could invest in their wellbeing while continuing to pursue full, ambitious lives. “Five years on, that vision has grown beyond our Victoria Island studio. Through BEYOND on Tour, we’re creating opportunities for people to step away from their routines and experience wellness differently. “What we’ve learnt is that people need different things at different moments. Sometimes it’s movement and the energy of a community. Other times, it’s rest, recovery or simply the freedom to do nothing. “As we look towards expanding BEYOND beyond Lagos, our ambition is to build a distinctly African wellness brand that delivers exceptional experiences while helping people live healthier, fuller lives.” Three Days of Movement, Recovery and Connection BEYOND on Tour V offers an all-inclusive retreat where guests can shape their weekend around what they need most.
