item.dc:creator: Jeff Spry
item.content:encoded: null HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return. Warning: Major Spoilers For " Lanterns " Season 1 Ahead! "Lanterns" redefines what is possible with episodic superhero TV shows (Image credit: HBO MAX) One of "Lanterns"' standout achievements is revealing the true costs of superheroism by deconstructing its DNA and examining the ugly guts of it all. It dives into the fear, trauma, and seduction that drive humans to take up the serious business of protecting the universe and doling out justice against both Earth-bound evil and intergalactic threats. "Lanterns" also explores mental health issues and PTSD that are the inevitable byproducts of a life of unimaginable violence. The compelling series achieves a provocative dissection of it all with rare confidence without the overindulgence of distracting CGI tossed in for sheer spectacle. It might not have been exactly the Green Lantern TV series fans wanted, but it was the show we got, and kinda the show we needed. Sure, for a series about a noble order of intergalactic space cops, we were treated to very little cosmic action, and instead we're given a grounded slow-burn police procedural à la "True Detective." As I said before, it's not perfect, but we shouldn’t dismiss "Lanterns" for its mild shortcomings when it gets so much right. We're willing a second season into existence, and with an average of 20 million global viewers and solid reviews, HBO/HBO Max would be very wise to bring it back. Whether a second season shifts into the heavens to rocket off on an outer space trajectory for a follow-up season is yet to be seen. For now, though, the Lanterns season one finale has left us with plenty of questions to ponder. Is Hal Jordan really dead? Kyle Chandler stars as Hal Jordan in "Lanterns" (Image credit: HBO MAX) "Lanterns"' season finale revealed that Kerry, in an unhinged moment of maternal panic trying to protect her mutant son, Noah, had put a bullet in Hal's head. RIP to the original Green Lantern... or is it? Kyle Chandler was a fantastic choice to play Hal Jordan, and he brought a charismatic gravitas and twisted sense of humor to the storied comic character. His sudden death in Rushville, frozen in the bleachers of the high school football stadium, certainly looked final, but this is the wild topsy-turvy universe of superheroes, so anything is possible. And don’t forget that the newly-freed Thaal Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) told the AI “Halogram” and Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart on Antaan's dead planet that the magical green ring could be used to restore Hal’s life. But Sinestro is a sly, slippery foe and is never to be trusted! Online speculation has proposed that Hal Jordan might be revived and enter the series as Parallax, the living embodiment of fear, but that’s not likely according to the series creators. What’s more probable is that we either see Chandler's Hal Jordan revived, or he'll just turn up in occasional flashbacks or Halogram pop-in scenes. John Stewart goes rogue? John Stewart prepares to power up his ring with Sinestro's yellow lamp! (Image credit: HBO MAX) With his unsanctioned lantern battery now in hand to power his ring, Stewart has become an independent contractor protecting Earth for Guy Gardner’s (Nathan Fillion) Sector 2814. Fortified with the Sinestro-forged yellow charging unit deemed illegal by the Guardians and the broader members of the Green Lantern Corps., this unattached Lantern is now free to make sure Noah doesn’t turn to the dark side and lean into his evil Manhunter programming. Will Stewart be seduced into the path of corruption by using Sinestro’s emotionally tainted battery, or steel himself against ill influences and continue to blaze his own trail as Earth's sole protector for the time being? As a gold-toothed Gardner tells Stewart, "When I take this bull**** up back to Oa, they’re gonna send an army to put you down." This sounds like the perfect setup for an eventful "Lanterns" season 2 where the Lantern Corps come to take Jordan in, dead or alive. It’ll be interesting to see which of the infamous space cops they eventually send. This ain't over! Noah Macon the Manhunter Shea Pritchard co-stars as Noah Macon in "Lanterns" (Image credit: HBO MAX) Sheriff Kerry Kane (Kelly Macdonald) and the dorky Billy Macon’s (Jason Ritter) immaculately conceived son, Noah, is outed as a Human-Manhunter hybrid that came into being after Kerry’s initial encounter with Manhunter Zoe years ago. He might be one helluva gunslinging high school quarterback now, but that pales in comparison to what he could become using his frightful shapeshifting Manhunter genes inherited from his grandmother. With his new Nebraska collegiate ball cap and now headed off to university, the sleeper agent has some vital decisions to make way beyond declaring a major. His desire will be to wipe out the Green Lanterns and the Guardians, but Earthly domination might come first unless he pledges to subdue his instincts and lead a normal life. And is Noah really the last Manhunter, or are there legions more ready to activate? Sinestro's fate? Ulrich Thomsen makes for a fantastic Sinestro in "Lanterns" (Image credit: HBO MAX) Spazkaban (or Space Azkaban), the notorious cosmic penitentiary controlled by the Guardians, lost one of its most lethal inhabitants in the crimson-skinned Sinestro when Noah (Shea Pritchard), the nascent Manhunter, broke him out of jail to craft him a yellow fear-based lantern. This persuasive villain was last seen wrapped in chains in the season finale, "Dirt and Stars," being dunked in the waters of madness by Stewart on the poison planet after a portal hop, before trying to coerce Halogram to deliver the prized ring for Jordan's resurrection. Avid comic fans know Sinestro once commanded his own intergalactic corp that fed upon the addictive yellow glare of fear instead of the emerald light’s will-imposed power. Will he unite with Noah to take down the manipulative Guardians of the Universe and their legion of space-bound enforcers, the Green Lanterns? Will Noah break bad or go good? And is it possible for Sinestro to forge another yellow lantern and a custom companion ring to escape captivity? As Sinestro explains, "If harnessed correctly, fear can be the most powerful force in the universe." Shards of "Lanterns" will invariably bleed over into James Gunn's "Superman" sequel, "Man of Tomorrow," which soars to theaters on July 9, 2027, so there’s still a lot of life left in DC Studios' DCU. All 8 episodes of "Lanterns" season 1 are available on HBO and HBO Max. item.title: Watch ‘Fishbone’, a 2020 Short Film by Anakle Films About Drug Counterfeiting
item.description: Years after its release, Fishbone remains relevant as Nigeria continues to grapple with counterfeit and substandard products. NAFDAC has repeatedly warned about falsified drugs and other products in circulation, including products that can lead to treatment failure, drug resistance and even death. Nigerians share their outcry on social media about their encounters with counterfeit products, from deodorant, chicken, toothpaste, to drinks, body and hair cream, soy sauce, palm oil, and many others. It is an ongoing public health concern. Released in 2020 by Anakle Films in collaboration with the US Mission in Nigeria and the US Department of Justice, Fishbone is a short film that explores the dangers of drug counterfeiting through the story of Mama T ( Shaffy Bello ), a respected philanthropist who secretly runs a counterfeit drug operation in Makoko, Lagos, and Inspector Cole ( Daniel Etim Effiong ), who is determined to bring her down. Beyond its crime-drama storyline, Fishbone explores the layers of counterfeiting, from the exploitation of vulnerable communities and the influence of wealth and social status to the devastating consequences of putting profit before human life. Its central message is particularly unsettling because the people who manufacture and distribute fake products can be deeply embedded in the same communities they endanger, without their knowledge. Rewatching Fishbone is an opportunity to remind ourselves how dangerous counterfeit products are. By showing how counterfeit drugs move through a community and affect people who may have no idea what they are buying, the film reminds viewers that awareness, vigilance and accountability matter. It is also a timely prompt to be more careful about where medicines are purchased and to report suspected falsified products to the appropriate authorities. Watch Fishbone again, and remember that behind every counterfeit product is a risk someone else may have to pay for with their life. The post Watch ‘Fishbone’, a 2020 Short Film by Anakle Films About Drug Counterfeiting appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
item.description: null The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower. Remember to use a trusted website like Time and Date to discover the exact moment of moonset for your location. Where should I look to see Orionid meteors? Orionid shooting stars will appear to originate from a patch of sky, or radiant, located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion , which glistens above the southeastern horizon for stargazers in the U.S. during the early hours of Oct. 22. For the best views look 40-90 degrees away from the radiant, where the glowing trains left in the wake of the fast-moving meteors will be at their longest. Be sure to head away from artificial lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to fully adapt to the dark for the best What causes the Orionid meteor shower? The Orionid meteor shower is active each year as Earth passes through the stream of debris left behind by Comet 1P/Halley , which was observed by a fleet of spacecraft when it last visited the inner solar system in 1986. Shooting stars become visible when particles of the ancient comet collide with our planet's atmosphere at 147,600 miles per hour (237,539 kilometers per hour), vaporizing in a spectacular display of natural fireworks. Hoping to catch a shooting star for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing meteor showers , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography . Editor's Note: If you would like to share your Orionid photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: For a Mere $2 Million, You Could Own Three Books That Unlocked the Universe

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: The Real Flex Is Healthy Skin: Inside the Vaseline and Dove Experience at BITML 2026
item.description: From personalised skin consultations and hands-on product trials to picture-perfect Glow Cam portraits, Vaseline and Dove delivered a memorable experience at Beauty in the Motherland (BITML) 2026 . As sponsors, both brands made healthy skin the focus of the experience, inviting visitors to understand that “ The Real Flex Is Healthy Skin .” Held from 5–7 October at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos, the event brought together Africa’s beauty professionals, brands, manufacturers, retailers, distributors, creators and consumers. Exhibitions and panel discussions explored everything from local manufacturing to skincare, haircare and the future of the continent’s beauty industry. Within that wider conversation, Vaseline and Dove encouraged beauty enthusiasts to move beyond simply following the latest skincare trend and spend time understanding their own skin. Their booth became a destination for visitors to get better acquainted with products they knew and discover others they could add to their routines. Vaseline’s and Dove’s pop-up booths stood out across the exhibition floor, drawing guests into an experience that encouraged them to ask, explore and try for themselves. At the Vaseline Skin Proof Lab and Texture Bar , guests explored textures, tried products, and spoke with Estheticians about their skin type. With Vaseline Original jellies, oils and lotions on deck, there was something for everyone and every skincare need. Dove extended that attention to underarm and body care through its Advanced Care range, exfoliating scrubs and Beauty Bar. Visitors explored the products and discussed how to give the skin beyond their face the same thoughtful attention. Event-exclusive discounts gave guests another reason to explore. Those who found a product they liked bought it at a discounted rate and received freebies, giving them more opportunities to add healthy skincare to their daily routine. But it was not all skincare. Adding excitement to the shopping and discovery experience, the Vaseline Glow Cam let guests strike a pose and smile for an instant Polaroid. Guests and creators stepped in to capture their best glow. Friends posed together, strangers shared a hello on camera, solo shots turned into mini photoshoots, and the space quickly became one of those BITML stops everyone wanted to experience. Vaseline and Dove’s experience at BITML 2026 reflect how the beauty industry is changing. With social media constantly introducing consumers to new ingredients, routines, and products, there is no shortage of beauty advice to scroll through. But more information brings more questions. Consumers today want to know what a product does, how it feels, whether it suits their skin and whether it can deliver real benefit. At BITML, both brands made everyday care approachable, giving guests opportunities to learn while enjoying the experience. item.title: Understanding Your Milk Options: A Dietitian’s Guide to Choosing the Right Milk
item.description: Buying milk used to be simple; you walked into a supermarket, reached for a familiar tin or sachet, and carried on with the rest of your shopping. Today, that same trip can leave many people standing in the dairy aisle far longer than they expected. While shopping at one of the large supermarkets when a young couple standing in front of the milk shelf was noticed. They had been there for what felt like ten minutes, carefully picking up one product after another, turning the packs over to read the labels before placing them back. The wife was scrolling through Instagram, almost desperately, as though she hoped someone had recently posted the answer to the question they were trying to solve. “ Which milk should we buy?” Interestingly, they weren’t comparing brands or prices. They were trying to understand the different options available. Should they choose dairy milk or a non-dairy alternative? And if dairy was the right choice, what exactly was the difference between Full Cream Milk and Filled Milk ? They wanted to make the right choice but weren’t sure what those terms meant. Eventually, I smiled and walked over. “ Hello, I’m sorry to interrupt. I’m a dietitian, and from what I’ve overheard, I think I can help explain the differences.” Within a few minutes, what had seemed like a complicated shopping decision suddenly became much clearer. They thanked me, picked the product that best suited what they were looking for and continued with the rest of their shopping. That encounter reminded me of something I have observed repeatedly throughout my years of practice: many consumers assume that milk is simply… milk. Yet today’s supermarket shelves tell a very different story. Before deciding which milk to buy, many consumers are first faced with an important question: Should I choose dairy milk or a non-dairy alternative? For those who choose dairy milk, there is another decision to make. Understanding the difference between Full Cream Milk, Filled Milk and age-appropriate milk products is key to choosing the option that best meets their needs. The challenge is that these differences aren’t always obvious to the average shopper. As a result, many people make their decisions based on familiarity, price or attractive packaging rather than understanding what the product was designed to do. Making informed food choices doesn’t always begin with eating something different. Sometimes, it begins with simply understanding what you’re buying. And that’s exactly where we’ll begin. For those who choose dairy milk, there is another decision to make. Understanding the difference between Full Cream Milk, Filled Milk and age-appropriate milk products is key to choosing the option that best meets their needs. The challenge is that these differences aren’t always obvious to the average shopper. As a result, many people make their decisions based on familiarity, price or attractive packaging rather than understanding what the product was designed to do. Making informed food choices doesn’t always begin with eating something different. Sometimes, it begins with simply understanding what you’re buying. And that’s exactly where we’ll begin. Understanding the Two Main Milk Options When we think about the milk aisle, it can sometimes feel as though there are endless options. The first decision is much simpler than many people realise. Broadly speaking, there is Dairy milk and non-dairy milk Dairy milk comes from animals, most commonly cows, although goat’s and sheep’s milk are also consumed in many parts of the world. It naturally provides high-quality protein, calcium and several essential vitamins and minerals that support growth, bone health and overall wellbeing. For consumers who choose dairy milk, there is one more decision to make. Not All Dairy Milk Products Are The Same Within the dairy category, the two most common options consumers will come across are Full Cream Milk and Filled Milk. While both are dairy products and both provide important nutrients, they differ in their fat composition and are designed to meet different nutritional needs and consumer preferences. Understanding these differences is the next step in choosing the milk that’s right for you. Understanding Your Options Standing in that supermarket, I realised the couple weren’t just trying to choose a brand. They were trying to understand which type of dairy milk best suited their needs. Once you’ve decided that dairy milk is the right choice for you, the next step is understanding the different dairy products available. Peak’s dairy range, for example, includes Full Cream Milk, Filled Milk and Peak 456 Growing-Up Milk . Although they all contain dairy ingredients, each has been developed to meet different nutritional needs and life stages. Rather than thinking of these as different versions of the same product, it helps to think of each one as serving a different purpose. Peak Full Cream Milk is designed to provide complete dairy nutrition for everyday family use. Peak Filled Milk, on the other hand, offers consumers another dairy option with a different fat composition while still providing important nutrients such as protein and calcium. Peak 456 Growing-Up Milk is specially formulated to support the nutritional needs of children aged four to six years. Understanding what each product is designed to do makes choosing the right one much easier. Let’s take a closer look at each one. Peak Full Cream Milk When most people think of milk, Full Cream Milk is usually what comes to mind. Made from whole cow’s milk, it naturally contains milk fat, giving it the rich, creamy taste many people enjoy. It also provides complete dairy nutrition by supplying high-quality protein, calcium and a range of essential vitamins and minerals that contribute to bone health, muscle function and overall wellbeing. One example within this category is Peak Full Cream Milk, which is available in both powdered and evaporated formats. Its versatility makes it suitable for drinking, breakfast cereals, smoothies, tea, coffee, cooking and baking, making it a practical choice for everyday family use. Best suited for: Families looking for complete dairy nutrition for everyday use. Peak Filled Milk Filled Milk is a dairy milk product in which part or all the natural milk fat has been replaced with vegetable oils. While this gives it a different fat composition from Full Cream Milk, it continues to provide important nutrients such as high-quality protein, calcium and essential vitamins. Peak Filled Milk offers consumers another dairy milk option that combines these nutritional benefits with a different fat composition to suit varying dietary preferences. Rather than thinking of Filled Milk as “better” or “worse” than Full Cream Milk, it is more helpful to understand that each product has been developed to meet different consumer needs. The right choice depends on your nutritional requirements, health goals and personal preferences. Best suited for: Consumers looking for a dairy milk option with a different fat composition. Peak 456 Growing-Up Milk Children have different nutritional needs at different stages of growth, which is why age-appropriate milk products have an important role in supporting a balanced diet. Peak 456 Growing-Up Milk is specially formulated for children aged four to six years. In addition to providing high-quality protein and calcium, it is fortified with essential vitamins and DHA, an omega-3 fatty acid that supports normal brain development during childhood. By providing nutrients tailored to this stage of growth, Peak 456 helps support the nutritional needs of young children as part of a healthy, balanced diet. Best suited for: Children aged 4–6 years. A Simple Guide to Choosing the Right Milk Choosing the right milk doesn’t have to be complicated. Once you understand what each product is designed to do, the decision becomes much simpler. If you’re looking for… A suitable option is… Complete dairy nutrition for the family Peak Full Cream Milk A dairy milk option with a different fat composition Peak Filled Milk Nutrition designed for children aged 4–6 years Peak 456 Growing-Up Milk Before adding any dairy milk product to your shopping basket, ask yourself three simple questions: Which dairy milk do I need? Full Cream or Filled milk Who am I buying this product for? Does this product meet my nutritional needs and suit how I intend to use it? item.title: Penguin Colony review – an Antarctic odyssey of Nazis and Lovecraftian horrors
item.description: PC; Origame Digital This odd but absorbing adventure sends you waddling across Antarctica in search of an eldritch entity – uncovering a world far stranger than it first appears A Nazi kneels down on frozen snow, staring at an endless Antarctic horizon. Another holds a gun to his head, ready to end his own life. I direct a small waddling penguin up to them, trying to imagine what it could be thinking. Dismay, perhaps. Likely bewilderment. But then a faint smile seems to break out across its beaky face, as if amused by these silly humans and their misguided belief that they could ever best this howling, harsh landscape. For most games, the idea of playing as a penguin observing Nazis losing the plot near the south pole would be weird enough. But Penguin Colony, developed by Origame Digital, pushes further. This is an audacious, frequently brilliant retelling of HP Lovecraft’s 1936 novella At the Mountains of Madness, in which eldritch horrors are just as common as Nazis. Further weirdness abounds: the many collectibles scattered about this place are not shiny gold objects à la Super Mario or Sonic. Rather, they are words. So tottering about as a semiaquatic bird, you have a unique mission: collect human language. Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.description: Upgraded, cheaper AirPods have noise cancelling, sound and controls to rival many plugged-in buds but without tips Apple’s latest AirPods set a new standard for open-fit buds with upgraded noise cancelling that now rivals many plugged-in designs of the same price. The AirPods 5 have the same design the popular AirPods 4 offering an option for those that do not like silicone ear tips used by most noise cancelling earbuds. They come in two versions, with or without a wireless charging case and swipe controls, costing from £119 (€149/$129/A$219) – £10 cheaper than the launch price of their predecessors . item.title: Systolic style: meet the medical-grade smartwatch revolutionising blood pressure monitoring
item.description: An estimated one-third of adults in England have high blood pressure, with research showing that many are unaware of their condition. But thanks to the new Huawei Watch D3, monitoring blood pressure is easier, accurate and more stylish than ever Wearable technology has come a long way in the past decade. Take a look around at your colleagues, friends and family, and you’ll be hard pushed to find anyone not wearing some kind of health monitoring ring, watch or band – there are even tracking insoles and patches, too. These gadgets have myriad benefits – not least, allowing us more control and insight over our health and wellbeing than ever before. We’re able to monitor everything from sleep and stress to heart health and more, and the technology is becoming more refined and intuitive seemingly by the day. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac mini M6 review: truly mighty but now more pricey
item.description: Apple’s cheapest desktop computer is no longer a bargain but its newest, fastest chip makes it a pocket powerhouse Apple’s latest Mac mini brings real speed and power for far more than everyday tasks in a practically pocketable form you can fit almost anywhere. The impressive new desktop machine is the first to receive an update to Apple’s latest M6 chip while remaining smaller than a headphones box. It is the cheapest computer Apple sells with an M-series chip, but like every other memory-containing piece of electronics, it has been hit by RAMageddon , driving up the starting price to £899 (€1,049/$899/A$1,449) from the £599 or equivalent of its M4 predecessor. item.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold review: the foldable with the best triple camera
item.description: Big screen folder with slick software and advanced AI is just like a regular Android when closed Google’s latest folding phone sticks with its tried and tested design of a traditional phone shape when closed and almost square when open, in the face of new competition from Apple’s squat iPhone fold . The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is Google’s fourth-generation folder and is still one of the only models with a full water and dust resistance rating similar to standard slab phones. It costs from £1,799 (€1,999/$1,899/A$2,799), which is £50 (€100/$100/A$100) more than last year as the pressure of RAMageddon continues to push up prices. Continue reading...

item.title: Pixel 11 Pro review: Google’s best pocket camera goes customisable
item.description: Solid battery life, snappy performance and quality software make for a great smaller phone with a killer camera Google’s latest Pro phone is out to prove it has the best camera on a smartphone while embracing customisation, allowing you to change the look and feel of your photos far beyond simple filters even if that means making them technically worse. The Pixel 11 Pro packs the best of Google’s hardware and software into a still-pocketable and easy to handle frame, instantly making it a contender for best smaller phone of the year. Screen: 6.3in 120Hz QHD+ OLED (495ppi) Processor: Google Tensor G6 RAM: 12 or 16GB Storage: 256, 512GB or 1TB Operating system: Android 17 Camera: 50MP + 48MP UW + 48MP 5x tele; 42MP selfie Connectivity: 5G, eSIM, wifi 7, UWB, NFC, Bluetooth 6, Thread and GNSS Water resistance: IP68 (1.5m for 30 minutes) Dimensions: 152.7 x 71.9 x 8.4mm Weight: 204g Continue reading...

item.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
item.description: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.
item.content:encoded: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.

item.title: Igniting Roman's Journey
item.description: Now on a three-month, million-mile journey to its final orbit, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will soon reveal the universe’s darkest secrets. The mission launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift
item.description: Technicians prepare to transfer the #2 RS-25 SLS (Space Launch System) rocket engine (front) to the work stand with the #3 engine (back) for integration with the Artemis III core stage rocket on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. During Artemis III, the four RS‑25 engines will launch the Orion spacecraft and its crew of four into low Earth orbit, generating more than two million pounds of thrust at liftoff.

item.title: Intuitive living is the latest wellness trend – meet the new tech making it work
item.description: Wellness culture can be overwhelming, but a more fluid approach is emerging. Smart devices such as the Huawei Watch Fit 5 perfectly embody this shift in direction – whether you’re regularly sleep tracking or just occasionally using data to support your lifestyle When it comes to the world of health and wellness, it’s easy to suffer from information overwhelm. We’ve never had more access to data, research and expertise which, while valuable, isn’t always applicable to our own lives. What’s more, few of us have time to spend hours sifting through content to devise a personalised health routine, let alone work out if a “routine” is necessary at all. All this information and expectation can come at a cost: emotional strain, guilt and confusion about where to turn. Health and fitness then start to feel like abstract milestones that we’re blindly chasing rather than important components of our lives. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of ‘earvolution’: from ceremonial piercings to fashion-statement earbuds
item.description: For millennia, humans have been captivated by ear decorations. Now, earbuds not only connect us to the digital world, they also showcase our personal sense of style – and the HUAWEI FreeClip 2 is at the forefront of that development When we are born, a cry can let the world know that we are healthy and OK. When we first begin to talk, we learn to express our needs and understand the needs of others. As we grow older, we learn that the sound of a siren denotes danger, that certain notes swelling together create the sound of a favourite song which lifts our spirits, or that a warm familiar voice on the other end of the phone means our best friend has our back. Our ears give us grounding and clues: they are our maps of the world, guiding us towards truth, keeping us from harm, giving us a constant stream of sensory information. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
